tickets.investigation:
- `src/ffi/callback.rs` declares 4 `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"` callbacks — `on_incoming_call` (:31), `on_reg_state` (:51), `on_call_state` (:73), `on_call_media_state` (:89) — each body is `let _ = (...)` (pure no-op). The design-constraint comment (:6-14) mandates: never lock, never allocate, never await, never call back into PJSUA; the only permitted operation is copying event params into a pre-allocated NativeEvent and pushing onto a lock-free queue / MPSC. The `[::STUB::] P11-11` marker (:16) covers callback.rs:16,30,51,74,91,97 and expects 8 callbacks total.
- `src/ffi/mod.rs:27` documents the `callback` module but exposes no `register_callbacks` entry point; `pub mod callback;` exists at :28.
- Vendored header `vendor/pjsip/pjsip/include/pjsua-lib/pjsua.h` defines `typedef struct pjsua_callback { ... } pjsua_callback;` (:1311) and `pjsua_config.cb` is a `pjsua_callback` field (:2612). The REAL ABI signatures differ from the current stubs: `on_incoming_call(pjsua_acc_id, pjsua_call_id, pjsip_rx_data*)` (:1331); `on_reg_state(pjsua_acc_id)` (:1734, single argument — the 4-arg stub is fabricated); `on_call_state(pjsua_call_id, pjsip_event*)` (:1321, state lives in the event); `on_call_media_state(pjsua_call_id)` (:1372); `on_reg_started(pjsua_acc_id, pj_bool_t renew)` (:1715); `on_dtmf_digit(pjsua_call_id, int digit)` (:1461); `on_call_transfer_status(pjsua_call_id, int st_code, const pj_str_t* st_text, pj_bool_t final, pj_bool_t* p_cont)` (:1552); `on_call_redirected(pjsua_call_id, const pjsip_uri*, const pjsip_event*) -> pjsip_redirect_op` (:2048). `pjsip_redirect_op` enum (`sip_util.h:84`): REJECT=0, ACCEPT=1, ACCEPT_REPLACE=2, PENDING=3, STOP=4.
- `src/ffi/bindings.rs` stub_aliases define only the id typedefs, `pj_str_t`, `pjsua_call_info`, `pjsua_codec_info`, status/state consts — NO `pjsua_config`, `pjsua_callback`, `pjsip_event`, `pjsip_rx_data`, `pjsip_uri`, `pjsip_transaction`, `pjsua_reg_info`, `pjsip_redirect_op`. The same callback code must compile against the bindgen output under `pjsua-native`, so the stub must mirror the field names/pointer types bindgen emits.
- `src/ffi/backend_calls.rs` `initialize()` (:23) is `#[cfg(feature = "pjsua-native")]` and calls `pjsua_create()` → `pjsua_init(null, null, null)` → `pjsua_start()` — no config struct, no callback registration. This is the init-time call site where `register_callbacks` must be wired.
- `src/build/build_script_bindgen.rs` — `BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST_TYPES` lacks `pjsua_config`, `pjsua_callback`, `pjsip_event`, `pjsip_rx_data`, `pjsip_uri`, `pjsip_transaction`, `pjsua_reg_info`, `pjsip_redirect_op`; `BINDGEN_ALLOWLIST_FUNCTIONS` already has `pjsua_init`. `wrapper.h` includes `<pjsua.h>`.
- `src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs` — `NativeEvent` enum (:46) has P0 (RegistrationStateChanged, RegistrationStarted, CallStateChanged, CallMediaStateChanged, DtmfDigit), P1 (TransportStateChanged, IceTransportError), P2 (CallTsxStateChanged, CallRedirected, CallTransferStatus, CallReplaced, NatDetected). No `IncomingCall` variant. `convert_native_event_to_payload` (:87) returns `None` for all P1/P2. RFC §15 (N0021) documents P2 → `None` as intentional (finer granularity than the public SipEventPayload API; RawSIP covers it).
- RFC §27.3 (N0037) specifies the callback bridge: `extern "C" fn on_incoming_call(...) { if let Some(rt) = runtime::global_runtime() { rt.enqueue_native_event(NativeEvent::IncomingCall { acc_id, call_id }); } }` — confirming a dedicated `NativeEvent::IncomingCall { acc_id, call_id }` variant (carries the account because an incoming call is not yet in the reactor CallTable).
- `src/runtime/reactor.rs` — `process_native_event` (:521) and `dispatch_event` (:483) exist (P7-2) but are `#[allow(dead_code)]`; `extract_event_ids` (:570) matches every NativeEvent variant — a new `IncomingCall` arm must be added. P12-7 (reactor wiring) and P12-8 (CallDirection) are downstream; examples note "reactor NativeEvent dispatch pending P12-7".
- `src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs` — `SipEventPayload::IncomingCall(IncomingCallInfo { call_id, account_id, caller_uri, caller_name })` (:338, :185) is the conversion target; `CallId`/`AccountId` `from_u64` reject 0.
- `crossbeam-queue` 0.3 is already a dependency (Cargo.toml) — lock-free `ArrayQueue<T>` with `force_push` on a full queue enables the loss-tolerant no-block design. The reactor's `tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender<DispatchCommand>` is a separate command channel, not the NativeEvent queue.
- The ticket's prior-make data is stale: `nodeIds`/`referenceSection`/`default_files`/`contracts` still carry P4-2 audio/codec content (N0030/N0035/N0036/N0040, §21/25/26/29, codec_policy_fallback.rs / audio_format_chunkpair.rs, C031/C041/C042) — none matches the callback-bridge scope; corrected in this re-make.

contracts.precondition: Audio delivery is part of the public API surface; callers supply a (sample_rate, bit_depth, channel_layout, frame_ms) tuple with frame_ms ∈ {10,20,40,60} (Rust struct: AudioFormat::new(SampleRate, BitDepth, ChannelLayout, u16) -> Result<AudioFormat, AudioFormatError>).
contracts.postcondition: AudioFormat validates the tuple and constructs only valid values; AudioChunk::I16(Vec<i16>)/F32(Vec<f32>) wraps raw samples with len()/is_empty(); AudioChunkPair { call_id: CallId, account_id: AccountId, timestamp: SystemTime, in_chunk, out_chunk } pairs IN and OUT under one shared SystemTime.
contracts.invariant: IN/OUT are paired by a single shared timestamp (no per-side timestamp field); every constructed AudioFormat satisfies sample_rate∈{Hz8000,Hz16000,Hz24000,Hz48000}, bit_depth∈{I16,F32}, channel_layout∈{Mono,StereoInOut}, frame_ms∈{10,20,40,60}.

contracts.precondition: Audio pipeline needs alignment; callers push IN (network-origin) and OUT (mixer-origin) frames as (Vec<i16>, Instant) via PairAligner::push_in/push_out with tolerance ≥ 20ms.
contracts.postcondition: PairAligner::try_pair() returns Some((in_data, out_data, ts)) when |ts_in − ts_out| ≤ tolerance, drops the earlier frame when over tolerance, and zero-pads the missing side when only one queue has data past tolerance; alignment_drift() counts zero-padding events.
contracts.invariant: Zero-padding fills the missing side with zeros of matching length; drift is reported as a counter metric (MediaActiveInfo::alignment_drift), not a hard MediaError, until sustained loss.

contracts.precondition: Audio pipeline needs resampling; callers provide distinct in/out AudioFormat values with matching bit_depth and channel_layout (ResamplePipeline::new(in_fmt, out_fmt) -> Result<ResamplePipeline, &'static str>).
contracts.postcondition: ResamplePipeline::new validates the format combination (distinct sample rates, same bit_depth, same channel_layout); interleave_in_out(in_mono: &[i16], out_mono: &[i16]) -> Vec<i16> maps stereo L=IN, R=OUT deterministically, truncating to min length.
contracts.invariant: Stereo output preserves L=IN, R=OUT for every index i in 0..min(len): output[2i]==in[i] and output[2i+1]==out[i]; interleave_in_out is pure and deterministic.

contracts.precondition: AccountConfig defines a codec policy; negotiation receives a remote codec list (&[CodecInfo]) and a CodecSelectionPolicy (Ordered | PreferOpusFallbackPcmu).
contracts.postcondition: Codec selection resolves the negotiated codec: PreferOpusFallbackPcmu tries Opus then PCMU; Ordered uses CodecAutoMode priority order; no mutually supported codec → Err(MediaNegotiationFailed); NegotiatedCodec::{Pcmu, Opus(OpusConfig)} is produced.
contracts.invariant: Only PCMU and Opus are accepted codecs; NegotiatedCodec has exactly 2 variants (adding a third requires updating AccountCodecPolicy and CodecAutoMode).

contracts.precondition: Codec policy is defined; caller passes an enumerated &[CodecInfo] list and a preferred_codecs &[String] selector to CodecAutoMode::apply.
contracts.postcondition: CodecAutoMode::apply returns HashMap<String,u8> of {codec_id → priority}: auto mode assigns opus/*=255, PCMU/8000/1=254, others=0; non-empty preferred_codecs returns an empty map (explicit mode bypasses auto mode).
contracts.invariant: Auto mode always assigns Opus=255, PCMU=254, all other codecs=0; a non-empty preferred_codecs list always yields an empty result map (explicit mode).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P4-2 specified the foundational audio primitives: AudioFormat/AudioChunkPair (model/audio_format_chunkpair.rs), PairAligner (model/audio_aligner.rs), ResamplePipeline (model/audio_resampler.rs), and NegotiatedCodec/CodecSelectionPolicy (config/codec_policy_fallback.rs). The audio/ module was commented out in src/lib.rs:64-66 because those format types were not yet stable. This work item uncomments the audio/ module and implements higher-level audio orchestration that composes the model/ primitives into a usable pipeline.

### Goal
Uncomment `pub mod audio;` in src/lib.rs and deliver a compiled, fully tested `src/audio/` orchestration module (src/audio/mod.rs + src/audio/pipeline.rs) that composes the P4-2 model/ primitives — AudioFormat, AudioChunkPair, PairAligner, ResamplePipeline/interleave_in_out — and the config/ codec types — NegotiatedCodec, CodecSelectionPolicy, CodecAutoMode — into a usable align → resample → codec-policy pipeline, re-exported from the crate root.

### Purpose
The model/ layer defines formats, alignment, and resampling as isolated primitives but no higher-level API connects them. P11-12 provides the first composition point: a caller feeds an AudioChunkPair and receives a processed stereo frame (L=IN, R=OUT) with a negotiated codec. This resolves the `[::STUB::] P11-12` marker at src/lib.rs:64 and removes the dead commented-out module block that has blocked the module graph since P4-2.

### Motivation
P4-2 delivered the primitives but left audio/ commented out because the format types were not yet stable. Those types are now implemented, tested (P4-2: 26 tests in audio_format_chunkpair.rs, 15 in audio_aligner.rs, 13 in audio_resampler.rs, 10 in codec_policy_fallback.rs) and re-exported from model/ and config/. This INSPECTION_FLAGGED re-implementation round requires a complete, STUB-free delivery: closing the module-graph gap lets dependent tickets (P5-2 AudioMixer, P2-3 event AudioChunk, P7 audio subscribe) bind to the orchestrated API.

### Constraints
- Reuse model/ and config/ types read-only — do not modify audio_format_chunkpair.rs, audio_aligner.rs, audio_resampler.rs, codec_policy_fallback.rs, or m20_codec_auto_mode.rs.
- No new dependencies: rubato is NOT in Cargo.toml and ResamplePipeline currently validates format combinations only (distinct rates + matching bit_depth/layout); do not add rubato or cpal in this ticket.
- Out of scope: FFI audio capture/playback (P8-26 / P3-2 FFI), AudioMixer/process_frame internals (P3-2), cpal device I/O (P8-7).
- Mandatory process: TDD Red → Green → Refactor; all new code must be translatable (Readability is Translatability) and [::STUB::]-free.

testExceptions:
Exception 1 — Item: Actual rubato resampling fidelity/performance (real rate conversion of arbitrary sample buffers).
Reason: The actual rate-conversion path is not testable in this ticket because rubato is not a dependency of this crate (Cargo.toml has no rubato entry) and ResamplePipeline exposes only format validation (ResamplePipeline::new) plus interleave_in_out — there is no resample() method to invoke, so we cannot test real resampling without adding the rubato crate, which is out of P11-12 scope. This is not a design defect — it is a genuine external-dependency gap tracked by P5-2/P8-26, and the orchestration is explicitly designed to reuse the currently implemented validation API.
Alternative verification: distinct-rate format validation and stereo L=IN/R=OUT mapping are covered by UT [C037-Normal/Error/Boundary/Invariant] and the IT pipeline end-to-end test; the orchestration compiles and runs with in_format != out_format without attempting actual rate conversion.

Exception 2 — Item: FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort get_frame/put_frame, cpal device I/O).
Reason: This FFI/cpal path is not testable in unit tests because FFI callbacks and cpal device binding require the PJSIP native library and audio hardware, which are not available in unit-test execution environments and are explicitly out of scope (P8-26 / P8-7); we cannot test it without the native stack. This is not an architectural defect — the FFI/cpal paths have their own tickets (P8-26, P8-7) with dedicated test plans.
Alternative verification: the orchestration layer is exercised with in-memory AudioChunk buffers (UT [Normal-orch], IT pipeline end-to-end).

Exception 3 — Item: Real-time deadline behavior of the orchestration loop under a live PJSUA call.
Reason: This is not testable in a unit test because real-time scheduling under a live call requires runtime/audio_worker integration (P3-2/P8-26) and physical audio hardware, which are non-deterministic and unavailable in the test environment. This is not a design defect — the audio/ orchestration itself is pure and deterministic (verified by UT [Invariant-orch]); only the live-call scheduling wrapper is excluded.
Alternative verification: AudioPipeline methods are pure and deterministic — determinism is asserted directly in UT [Invariant-orch] (same inputs → same outputs), and zero-padding/drift metrics are asserted numerically in UT [C036-Invariant] and IT [Zero-padding propagation].

tickets.title: DTMF Specification, AsyncAudioSource & Incoming Call/Transfer

contracts.precondition: Call API supports DTMF — pjsua_call_dial_dtmf() can be called with valid native_call_id and digit string; AccountConfig::validate() rejects empty DtmfPolicy::send_methods or receive_methods
contracts.postcondition: DTMF specification defined — DtmfMethod enum has variants for Inband, SipInfo (Info), Rfc4733; DtmfReceivedInfo struct contains method:DtmfMethod, digit:char, duration_ms:Option<u16>, volume_dbm0:Option<i8>; data types implement Clone + Debug
contracts.invariant: 3 DTMF method categories: Inband (RFC 2833 in-band tone), SIP INFO (SipInfo in Info variant), RFC 4733 (out-of-band RTP event). DtmfPolicy always has at least one send_method and one receive_method — validated in AccountConfig::validate().

contracts.precondition: DTMF spec defined — DtmfMethod, DtmfReceivedInfo, DtmfPolicy types exist in the crate; DtmfSent event variant exists in SipEventPayload
contracts.postcondition: DtmfSentInfo and two-phase design — DtmfSentInfo { method, digit, status: Result<(), SentDtmfError>, pjsip_status } defined; send_dtmf() returns Ok(()) synchronously for command acceptance; DtmfSent event fires asynchronously on completion or timeout
contracts.invariant: 500ms default timeout (DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS) for DtmfSent fallback when PJSIP callback unavailable; configurable via DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms

contracts.precondition: Audio subscribe uses sources — AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource+Send>; AsyncAudioSource trait defined with async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize
contracts.postcondition: AsyncAudioSource trait with RPITIT — async fn next_chunk in trait definition (currently #[async_trait] desugaring). ErasedAudioSource blanket impl auto-derived for all T: AsyncAudioSource + Send. SyncAudioSource trait and SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> provided for synchronous sources.
contracts.invariant: ErasedAudioSource auto-derived for every AsyncAudioSource implementor — blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> ErasedAudioSource for T must compile. SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send.

contracts.precondition: Call API defined — IncomingCallInfo, ReferRequest, TransferInfo event types exist in SipEventPayload; CallEntry state machine creates entries on incoming INVITE
contracts.postcondition: IncomingCall struct { from_uri, to_uri, display_name, headers, offered_codecs, has_early_media } defined; optional auto-reject timer configurable in account config; ReferRequest { refer_to, referred_by, replaces? } creation from SIP REFER; blind transfer NOTIFY → TransferCompleted event
contracts.invariant: Blind transfer (REFER without Replaces header) is first-class — ReferRequest::replaces is Option; transfer completion always emits TransferCompleted event via NOTIFY subscription state

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

- 【Goal】Define and implement the DTMF specification (DtmfMethod, DtmfReceivedInfo with the method:DtmfMethod field and contract-correct Option<u16>/Option<i8> field types), the AsyncAudioSource adapter types (ErasedAudioSource, SyncAudioSource, SyncSourceAdapter<T>), and the IncomingCall / REFER-transfer types (IncomingCall, IncomingCallConfig, ReferRequest.replaces, TransferInfo) per RFC nodes N0028 / N0032 / N0048. Close the 4 ABC inspection omissions (O-001..O-004) and resolve the TS-003 orphan-ticket crime in src/config/versioning_policy.rs so the ticket survives a full make → plan → start → review → resolve cycle this time.
- 【Purpose】Provide type-safe DTMF signalling primitives for SIP call control (send + receive with DtmfPolicy validation). Enable downstream crates to implement custom async audio sources for AudioMixer via the SyncAudioSource → SyncSourceAdapter bridge and the ErasedAudioSource dynamic-dispatch wrapper. Expose incoming call metadata (from_uri, to_uri, display_name, headers, offered_codecs, has_early_media) and REFER-based transfer capabilities (ReferRequest.replaces, TransferCompleted) to application code as typed SipEventPayload variants.
- 【Motivation】The ABC Inspection Pipeline remanded P8-4 with one critical omission (O-001: ReferRequest.replaces missing and zero tests construct ReferRequest/TransferInfo, so the C049 invariant and acceptance criteria are unenforced), one major (O-002: DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms widened to Option<u64> and volume_dbm0 to Option<i32> vs the contract Option<u16>/Option<i8>, and no None/0/MAX edge tests), and two minor (O-003: no SipEventPayload::DtmfSent construction test; O-004: no 65536-sample SyncAudioSource boundary test). The versioning_policy.rs STUB (TS-003) is an orphaned ticket reference that must be resolved this round. Every contract (C029/C030/C033/C049) must be translated into precise test assertions so that removing any contract behavior fails a test.
- 【Constraints】MSRV 1.95 — RPITIT is stable but the existing AsyncAudioSource uses #[async_trait] for Box<dyn> compatibility in AudioMixer; the ErasedAudioSource blanket impl provides the dynamic-dispatch path without refactoring existing implementors. Do NOT add new crate dependencies — all required derives (Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq) are std. Keep the canonical 4-variant DtmfMethod (Rfc2833, Rfc4733, Info, Inband) from account_config_spec.rs; leave the separate 2-variant DtmfMethod in m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs intact to avoid breaking DtmfSentInfo consumers (unification is an open item, not a forced change). Maintain backward compatibility with existing DtmfReceivedInfo consumers (m20_native_event_conv.rs constructs with None/None, so field-type narrowing is compatible). ReferRequest gains the additive replaces: Option<String> field; all struct-literal construction sites must add it.
scope: Changes (path): src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs (MODIFY) — narrow DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms to Option<u16> and volume_dbm0 to Option<i8>; add ReferRequest.replaces: Option<String>; add payload-construction and edge/boundary tests. src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs (VERIFY) — the 65536-sample SyncAudioSource/SyncSourceAdapter boundary test is in place and open_default_microphone_source (C051) is fully implemented behind the cpal-input feature (P8-7); no STUB marker remains to re-scope. src/config/versioning_policy.rs (VERIFY) — VersionPolicy per N0006 §4.1 is implemented with tests and the TS-003 STUB marker is removed. src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs (VERIFY) — DtmfReceivedInfo construction still compiles after type narrowing.

Changes (action): 1) Verify DtmfReceivedInfo field types match the contract types (Option<u16>/Option<i8>). 2) Verify ReferRequest.replaces: Option<String> exists. 3) Verify the event-payload construction tests and boundary tests exist. 4) Verify VersionPolicy (semver phase classification, CHANGELOG requirement, 1.0+ MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH semantics) is implemented with a #[cfg(test)] module. 5) Verify the microphone source STUB is resolved — open_default_microphone_source is a real implementation (CpalMicrophoneSource) behind the cpal-input feature, added by P8-7.

Changes (detail): DtmfReceivedInfo { method: DtmfMethod, digit: char, duration_ms: Option<u16>, volume_dbm0: Option<i8> } (was Option<u64>/Option<i32>). ReferRequest { call_id: CallId, refer_to: String, referred_by: Option<String>, replaces: Option<String> }. VersionPolicy type in src/config/versioning_policy.rs implementing the N0006 §4.1 rules (0.x CHANGELOG-based breaking changes; 1.0+ MAJOR = breaking / MINOR = additive / PATCH = bugfix; security-fix PATCH exception). New tests: payload_dtmf_sent, payload_refer_received, payload_transfer_completed, dtmf_received_info_none_edge, dtmf_received_info_duration_boundary, dtmf_received_info_volume_boundary, refer_request_blind, refer_request_full, transfer_info_fields, sync_source_adapter_65536_buffer, version_policy_0x_and_10x.

Changes (before/after): BEFORE — DtmfReceivedInfo.duration_ms: Option<u64>, volume_dbm0: Option<i32>; ReferRequest { call_id, refer_to, referred_by }; versioning_policy.rs holds only a doc comment + STUB; no DtmfSent/ReferReceived/TransferCompleted payload tests. AFTER — duration_ms: Option<u16>, volume_dbm0: Option<i8>; ReferRequest gains replaces: Option<String>; VersionPolicy implemented with tests and the STUB marker removed; payload_* tests assert each event variant; the 65536-sample buffer boundary is covered.

Changes (API): DtmfReceivedInfo field types narrow (Option<u64> → Option<u16>, Option<i32> → Option<i8>) — a type-level change affecting struct-literal construction sites (only m20_native_event_conv.rs today, None-compatible). ReferRequest gains the additive replaces: Option<String> field. VersionPolicy is a new public type in the config domain. No changes to the AsyncAudioSource / ErasedAudioSource / SyncAudioSource / SyncSourceAdapter signatures (already present from P5-2/P0-6).
Changes (schema): None — pure Rust API types; no serialization, DB, or wire-format changes. DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms and IncomingCallConfig already exist (P7-2 / P5-2) and are untouched.

Changes (config): No AccountConfig or ClientConfig changes required for the P8-4 core scope. versioning_policy.rs is a standalone config-domain module (N0006) implemented independently of account/client config to avoid entanglement.

Changes (dep): No new crate dependencies for THIS ticket. All derives (Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq) are std. VersionPolicy uses only std. The microphone source sits behind the cpal-input feature gate; the cpal optional dependency was already added by P8-7 (Cargo.toml:73 cpal = { version = "0.18", optional = true }), so no Cargo.toml change is required here.

Non-change (item): PJSIP FFI callback wiring (on_dtmf_digit / on_incoming_call / on_refer) and the Reactor event dispatch — separate P5-3 ticket. RPITIT refactoring of the existing #[async_trait] AsyncAudioSource — deferred. Attended transfer end-to-end (REFER with Replaces targeting a live call) — depends on the multi-call state machine, P5-3+. Unification of the 2-variant DtmfMethod with the 4-variant canonical — open item, not forced.

Non-change (why): The P8-4 scope is the pure type definitions + test assertions that close the ABC gaps. FFI wiring needs a live PJSIP stack; RPITIT refactor risks the working AudioMixer integration; attended transfer needs multi-call semantics; DtmfMethod unification would break DtmfSentInfo consumers (P7-2 tests). Each is a separate, larger change better owned by a dedicated ticket.

Impact (component): src/api/event_model_payload_bus.rs — event payload structs (DtmfReceivedInfo, ReferRequest) + SipEventPayload variants. src/config/versioning_policy.rs — VersionPolicy type (already implemented, additive). src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — 65536-sample boundary test + C051 microphone source (resolved by P8-7). src/state/m20_native_event_conv.rs — DtmfReceivedInfo construction (None-compatible). runtime/audio_worker consumers — ErasedAudioSource blanket impl adds an impl boundary with zero migration cost.

Impact (nature): API surface expansion (additive: replaces field, VersionPolicy) + field-type narrowing (minor breaking for DtmfReceivedInfo literal constructors). Existing Default implementations and None-construction paths remain compatible. No behavioral change to event dispatch.

Impact (response): Downstream crates constructing DtmfReceivedInfo must pass Option<u16>/Option<i8> values (u64/i32 literals beyond the range fail to compile — intended, enforces the boundary invariant). ReferRequest constructors must add replaces: Option<String>. VersionPolicy is additive with no consumer impact.

testExceptions: - Item: Attended transfer (REFER with Replaces header targeting a live call). Reason: NOT TESTABLE at the P8-4 type level — the end-to-end flow depends on the live multi-call PJSIP state machine and call-lingering semantics, which cannot be exercised without a running PJSIP stack. This is NOT A DEFECT: ReferRequest.replaces (added in P8-4) fully models the attended-transfer payload and the type is unit-tested; only the integration wiring is deferred. Alternative verification: Layer-4 integration test with a live SIP server in a future P5-3 ticket.

- Item: Real microphone capture via open_default_microphone_source. Reason: NOT TESTABLE in P8-4 — the ticket Constraints prohibit adding the cpal crate dependency, which is required for device capture; the function stays behind the cpal-input feature and returns a typed error. This is NOT A DEFECT: the RFC §40 signature is verified by the C051 signature test and the feature gate is honest about the missing device backend. Alternative verification: C051 compile-time signature test; device capture deferred to a cpal-authorized future ticket.

- Item: PJSIP callback timing for on_dtmf_digit / on_incoming_call / on_refer. Reason: NOT TESTABLE without a live PJSIP v2.x stack — the exact callback signature and invocation context are runtime FFI-linked. This is NOT A DEFECT: the type definitions (DtmfReceivedInfo, IncomingCall, ReferRequest, TransferInfo) and the DtmfSent 500ms timeout fallback are fully unit-tested; only callback-to-event conversion is deferred to P5-3. Alternative verification: the spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout fallback is tested with tokio::time; Layer-3 integration with a Docker SIP server in a future ticket.
acceptanceCriteria: - [Happy path] DtmfReceivedInfo constructed with method=Rfc4733, digit='5', duration_ms=Some(100), volume_dbm0=Some(-15) round-trips all four fields; SipEventPayload::DtmfReceived matches. ReferRequest with replaces: Some("sip:carol@example.com") and TransferInfo with status_code=200 construct and match their SipEventPayload variants (ReferReceived / TransferCompleted). SyncSourceAdapter wraps a SyncAudioSource and AsyncAudioSource::next_chunk returns the correct sample count; the ErasedAudioSource blanket impl works for MockAsyncAudioSource. IncomingCall with from_uri / to_uri / headers / codecs / has_early_media constructs. VersionPolicy classifies a 1.0+ MAJOR breaking change correctly.

- [Error case] AccountConfig::validate with empty DtmfPolicy::send_methods or receive_methods returns Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig). DtmfPolicy::is_send_allowed / is_receive_allowed return false for disallowed methods. SyncSourceAdapter with an exhausted inner source returns 0. IncomingCall with empty from_uri / to_uri does not panic on access or Debug formatting. spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes DtmfSent{Err(Timeout)} after the deadline. VersionPolicy rejects an invalid change classification without panicking.

- [Edge case] DtmfReceivedInfo with duration_ms=None and volume_dbm0=None remains well-formed; duration_ms at u16::MAX and volume_dbm0 at i8::MIN / i8::MAX round-trip unchanged. IncomingCall with empty offered_codecs (pre-negotiation) and empty headers is accepted; has_early_media=false behaves identically to true. SyncAudioSource buffer sizes at both extremes (0 and 65536) are handled without overflow. ReferRequest blind transfer has replaces=None — the first-class blind-transfer path.

Run `make check-be` and `make test` until green.
- 【Risks】Field-type narrowing (Option<u64> → Option<u16>, Option<i32> → Option<i8>) is a breaking change for any struct-literal consumer passing values beyond u16/i8 — audit all construction sites (only m20_native_event_conv.rs today, None-compatible). ReferRequest.replaces is additive but breaks struct-literal constructors that omit it — audit event_model_payload_bus consumers (zero external references today). The separate 2-variant DtmfMethod in m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs remains a type-confusion risk; unification is preferred but deferred to avoid breaking DtmfSentInfo consumers (P7-2 tests depend on it).
- 【Caveats】DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms already exists in src/config.rs (P7-2 O-002 closure) — do NOT re-add it to account_config_spec.rs. The open_default_microphone_source STUB is ALREADY RESOLVED by P8-7 (real CpalMicrophoneSource behind the cpal-input feature; cpal optional dep in Cargo.toml) — do NOT re-introduce a marker; the C051 contract is satisfied by the existing implementation. VersionPolicy (N0006 §4.1) is a distinct domain from the DTMF/audio/call scope — implement it as a standalone config type so it does not entangle account config.
- 【Open items】Unify the 2-variant DtmfMethod (m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs) with the 4-variant canonical (account_config_spec.rs)? Option (a) use the canonical in DtmfSentInfo — breaks P7-2 tests; option (b) keep separate and add a From conversion. Deferred to avoid scope creep. Microphone capture is implemented behind the cpal-input feature (P8-7); end-to-end testing against a real input device is deferred to a hardware-backed integration environment. The RPITIT refactor of AsyncAudioSource (native async fn in trait) remains deferred; the ErasedAudioSource wrapper covers dynamic dispatch in the meantime.
- 【Future】P5-3 wires DtmfReceived / IncomingCall / ReferReceived / TransferCompleted events through PJSIP callbacks in the Reactor. Attended transfer (REFER with Replaces targeting a live call) becomes first-class once the multi-call state machine lands. VersionPolicy will drive release automation (CHANGELOG enforcement, semver classification checks) in a later tooling ticket.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】DtmfPolicy always has >= 1 send_method and >= 1 receive_method (enforced in AccountConfig::validate() returning SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig otherwise). DtmfReceivedInfo is always constructed with method + digit populated; duration_ms and volume_dbm0 are Option fields typed Option<u16>/Option<i8> that stay None when the remote endpoint reports no data. AsyncAudioSource::next_chunk and ErasedAudioSource::next_chunk return 0 when the source is exhausted and never panic. SyncSourceAdapter<T> delegates every call to the inner SyncAudioSource::next_chunk without adding logic.
- 【Invariant on error】DTMF method validation helpers (DtmfPolicy::is_send_allowed / is_receive_allowed) return bool and never panic; empty-policy rejection lives in AccountConfig::validate() and returns Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig). SyncSourceAdapter with an exhausted inner source returns 0, never garbage. IncomingCall with empty from_uri/to_uri remains a valid, Debug-printable struct (no panic on field access). spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout always publishes DtmfSent{Err(Timeout)} after the deadline — the async completion event is emitted even when the PJSIP callback is absent.
- 【Internal state invariant】ErasedAudioSource blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> compiles for every concrete source type — no manual per-type impl required. SyncSourceAdapter<T> implements AsyncAudioSource + Send exactly when T: SyncAudioSource + Send. DtmfReceivedInfo / ReferRequest / TransferInfo / IncomingCall implement Clone + Debug (compile-time verified); DtmfMethod implements Clone + Copy + Debug + PartialEq + Eq. ReferRequest::replaces is Option<String> — the blind transfer (REFER without Replaces) is the first-class flow. DtmfConfig::sent_timeout_ms (src/config.rs) drives the DtmfSent fallback timer with DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS == 500.
- 【Boundary invariant】duration_ms accepts the full [0, u16::MAX] range without truncation (field type Option<u16>). volume_dbm0 accepts the full [i8::MIN, i8::MAX] range (field type Option<i8>). SyncAudioSource buffer sizes at both extremes — 0 and 65536 samples — are handled without overflow or panic. IncomingCall offered_codecs and headers accept the empty vec (pre-negotiation state) as well as single/multi-element vecs. IncomingCallConfig reject_timeout_ms accepts 0 and custom values.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvement plan (Boy Scout Rule — leave code cleaner than found):
- Function names as verb phrases: DtmfPolicy::is_send_allowed / is_receive_allowed already read as verbs — keep. VersionPolicy methods must be verbs: classify_change(), requires_changelog(), current_phase() — never generic names like process() or check().
- Variable names as domain concepts: DtmfReceivedInfo fields already use SIP domain terms (method, digit, duration_ms, volume_dbm0). ReferRequest.replaces is the domain term for the Replaces header — no generic option. VersionPolicy must name the semver concepts (phase, change_kind, changelog) not raw strings.
- One function one responsibility: VersionPolicy::classify_change answers only "what kind of change" — CHANGELOG gating is a separate method requires_changelog(). Do not merge classification with release automation.
- Hardcoded values as named constants: DEFAULT_AUTO_REJECT_TIMEOUT_MS (incoming_call_refer.rs:36) and DEFAULT_DTMF_SENT_TIMEOUT_MS (m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:64) already exist — keep. Any new versioning thresholds become named constants in versioning_policy.rs.
- No error swallowing: AccountConfig::validate errors propagate via ?. spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes errors on the EventBus instead of log-and-continue. VersionPolicy returns typed errors for invalid classifications.
- Proactive cleanups in touched files: update the stale [::STUB::] P0-1 reference in versioning_policy.rs (resolved by implementation); re-scope the microphone STUB to MUST RESOLVE with the cpal constraint reason instead of leaving a misleading P8-4 reference that would later read as a completed-ticket staleness crime; in event_model_payload_bus.rs, align the DtmfReceivedInfo doc comment with the narrowed Option<u16>/Option<i8> types and add the replaces field doc to ReferRequest.

foundOmissions.recommendation: In dtmf_sent_timeout_fallback_publishes_timeout (src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:111-134), after receiving the event, assert ev.meta.call_id == Some(CallId::from_u64(1)) to satisfy the P8-4 IT test plan item 'assert the event carries the call_id and digit' for the C030 DtmfSent timeout fallback.

evaluations.reason: C030 postcondition requires 'DtmfSent event fires asynchronously on completion or timeout' and the P8-4 IT test plan (Layer-2 DtmfSent timeout fallback) explicitly requires 'assert the event carries the call_id and digit'. spawn_dtmf_sent_timeout publishes the event with EventMeta::new(0, None, Some(call_id)) at src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:89, but dtmf_sent_timeout_fallback_publishes_timeout (src/api/m20_dtmfsent_twophase.rs:111-134) only matches ev.payload and asserts info.digit/status/pjsip_status, never inspecting ev.meta.call_id — if the call_id were dropped from the published event (Some(call_id) -> None), every test would still pass. No test anywhere in the crate asserts a DtmfSent event's meta.call_id.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal (original)
Establish the siprs crate's public identity as a safe asynchronous SIP audio client library. Define SipClient as the top-level facade that integrates with P0-2's CoreReactor/RuntimeHandle/RuntimeCommand infrastructure.

### Purpose (original)
Provide Rust application code with a safe, async-native facade over PJSUA SIP functionality, limited to audio-only voice communication. This crate exists to eliminate unsafe FFI boilerplate and deliver SIP calling capabilities through idiomatic Rust APIs — Result propagation, tokio async/await, typed events, and structured configuration.

### Motivation (original)
P0-3 is the gateway ticket that establishes the crate's architectural identity before downstream tickets implement specific sub-systems: error types (P0-4), event system (P0-5), FFI layer (P0-6), audio pipeline (P1+). Without a defined SipClient + ClientConfig, no downstream implementation has a cohesive host. This ticket crystallizes the purpose defined in RFC 1 (§1) into concrete public API surface.

### Constraints (original)
- Audio-only: no video API surface (RFC §1, §2). Enforced by compile-time assertions.
- All async public APIs must return Result<T, SipError> (RFC §1 constraint on N0001).
- PJSIP v2.x via FFI only — no raw socket-level SIP stack.
- Single crate with modular internal structure (RFC §6, C009).
- Shutdown must be cancellation-safe and idempotent (RFC §32, C044).
- SecretString for password storage (RFC §35-36, C048).
- Microphone input is optional via cpal-input feature flag (RFC §40, C051).
- MSRV 1.95, OS targets per RFC §4 (C006).

### Goal (re-implementation round)
Make the crate identity verifiable and regression-proof: the facade `SipClient` + `ClientConfig` must exist as typed, validated, audio-only API surface, and the test suite must detect any violation of the 15 RFC §1 contracts. Concretely: all four ABC findings (O-001 `assert_sync::<SipClient>()`, O-002 `metrics` feature presence, O-003 `tls`/`srtp` independence, O-004 `std::thread::JoinHandle<()>` type assertion) are closed by new test assertions, and `make test` stays green (baseline 647 unit + 37 integration + 1 doc-test).

### Purpose (why this exists)
The crate exists to eliminate unsafe PJSUA FFI boilerplate and deliver SIP voice calling through idiomatic Rust — `Result<T, SipError>` propagation, tokio async/await, typed events, structured configuration. This ticket defines and locks the crate's public identity so downstream tickets (P0-4 error, P0-5 event, P0-6 FFI, P1+ audio) have a stable host. The ABC round re-confirms that identity through precise test assertions rather than broad ones.

### Motivation (why now)
The ABC Inspection Pipeline (criteria A contract-translation, B violation-detection, C test-precision) found 4 violations in the prior P0-3 implementation: the `Sync` half of `SipClient: Send + Sync` was unenforced (O-001), `metrics` feature presence was untested (O-002), tls/srtp feature independence was untested (O-003), and the `std::thread` reactor model was not type-pinned (O-004). These are regression gaps, not new features: without them, future refactors could silently break the crate identity. This ticket is remanded to close the gaps and re-verify all 15 contracts.

### Constraints (re-implementation round boundaries)
- Audio-only: no video API surface (RFC §1/§2, C001 invariant) — enforced by compile-time tests.
- All async public APIs return `Result<T, SipError>` (RFC §1, N0001 global invariant).
- PJSIP v2.x (pinned 2.17, RFC §4) via FFI only; no raw socket-level SIP stack.
- Single crate, modular internal structure (RFC §6, C009 invariant).
- Shutdown cancellation-safe and idempotent (RFC §32, C044 invariant).
- `SecretString` (zeroize) for password storage (RFC §35-36, C048 invariant).
- Microphone optional via `cpal-input` feature (RFC §40, C051 invariant).
- MSRV 1.95; OS targets Windows x86_64, macOS arm64, Ubuntu x86_64 (RFC §4, C006 invariant).
- No new dependencies and no public API changes in this round — test-hardening only.

### Goal (this ABC round)
Close all 7 ABC omissions (O-001..O-007) so the crate's RFC-driven identity is verifiable and regression-proof. Concretely: add RFC-ROOT.md section-presence assertions for §34 (C047-Pre), §35/§36 (C048-Pre), §40/§41 (C051-Pre/Post), §45/§46 (C056-Pre/Post), §61 (C059-Pre), tighten io_boundaries_documented_as_reference to pin the §61 参考情報 marker (C068-Inv), and add a src/lib.rs pub mod declaration test (C009-Post). All 15 contracts stay green.

### Purpose (why this exists)
This ticket exists to make the crate identity (established by the facade SipClient + ClientConfig) empirically verifiable. The ABC Inspection Pipeline found that removing RFC sections (§34/§35/§36/§40/§41/§45/§46/§61) or pub mod declarations would not fail any test, because the contract Pre/Post conditions referencing them were never asserted. This round adds the missing assertions so the contract suite actually detects those regressions.

### Motivation (why now)
The ABC Inspection Pipeline (criteria A contract-translation, B violation-detection, C test-precision) confirmed 7 violations in the prior implementation: C047-Pre (§34 観測性 unasserted), C048-Pre (§35/§36 セキュリティ unasserted), C051-Pre/Post (§40/§41 unasserted), C056-Pre/Post (§45/§46 unasserted), C059-Pre (§61 completeness unasserted), C068-Inv (§61 参考情報 marker not pinned — broad I/O substring instead), C009-Post (src/lib.rs pub mod declarations unasserted — the spec-text test reads the spec, not the source). These are regression gaps, not new features: without them, a future RFC refactor or module reorganization could silently break the crate identity while every test stays green.

### Constraints (this ABC round boundaries)
- Test-hardening only — no production behavior change, no new dependencies, no public API changes.
- All new assertions are deterministic source/RFC inspections (read RFC-ROOT.md, src/lib.rs, Cargo.toml).
- Exact heading strings (e.g. `## 34. 観測性`) are pinned — never substring fragments that appear elsewhere in the document.
- The §61 assertion pins the 参考情報 marker on the §61 heading; a §61 heading without the marker fails.
- Baseline `make test` must stay green (990+ unit + 37 integration + doc-tests, zero warnings).
- `SipError` is owned by P6-2; this ticket consumes SipErrorKind only and must not add variants.

testExceptions: Exception: Video API absence is a structural invariant, cannot test as runtime assertion — Reason: The crate purpose explicitly excludes video (RFC §1). No video-related types exist in any src/ file. This is a compile-time property verified by the type system and module visibility. Any future addition of video types would fail the compile-time invariant tests defined in testUnit. This is NOT an architectural defect — the RFC deliberately scopes to audio-only, and the type system enforces this at compile time. Alternative verification: compile-time invariant checks in testUnit (UT: [Boundary] Audio-only API surface, UT: [Invariant] No video types in public module exports).

Exception: SipClient::new returning Result is a type-level invariant, cannot test as individual runtime assertion — Reason: The function signature SipClient::new(config: ClientConfig) -> Result<(Self, Receiver<SipEvent>), SipError> is enforced by the Rust compiler at compile time — every caller must handle both Ok and Err. The Err branch IS tested in testUnit for invalid config. Alternative verification: compile_fail tests in testUnit cover the error path at the type level. This is NOT an architectural defect — returning Result from fallible operations is idiomatic Rust design.

Exception: All public async fn signatures returning Result<T, SipError> cannot test individually at runtime — Reason: This architectural invariant is enforced by the Rust compiler and verified by compile-time tests in testUnit. Runtime testing of each method's specific error return path requires downstream tickets (P0-4 for SipError variants, P0-5 for event types, P0-6 for FFI integration). This ticket establishes the convention and verifies it at compile time. This is not a defect — this is a deliberate design choice for the facade layer.

**Exception entry — CoreReactor::spawn is the single reactor-thread factory**
- [Item] The invariant "exactly one reactor thread exists per SipClient, created only via `CoreReactor::spawn`" **cannot test** as a single runtime assertion: other code could spawn additional threads, and the reactor thread terminates on shutdown, so a liveness check alone cannot assert exclusivity.
- [Reason] This is a crate-wide *structural* property, not a single-function behavior. A runtime test can observe the reactor it spawns (`JoinHandle`, `is_terminated`) but cannot observe threads created elsewhere. This is **not testable** as one assertion, yet it is NOT an architectural defect: the thread *factory* is fully testable (O-004 type assertion + `"siprs-reactor"` thread name), and only the exclusivity of the factory is a source-review property. Stating it is "not a defect" because the testable part is fully covered by testUnit.
- [Alternative verification] (1) O-004 closure: `let _: std::thread::JoinHandle<()> = join;` in `reactor_spawn_creates_thread` proves `spawn` uses `std::thread`. (2) `make stubs` / source review enforces that `thread::Builder`/`thread::spawn` appear only in `src/runtime/reactor.rs`. (3) Integration tests join the `JoinHandle` and assert `is_terminated()` to prove the reactor thread lifecycle.

**Exception entry (copy this block for each non-testable item):**
- [Item] The RFC-presence tests assert heading markers, not the semantic completeness of each RFC section's prose.
- [Reason] RFC-ROOT.md is a natural-language design document; the contract Pre/Post conditions reference section *presence* (`## 34. 観測性`, `## 35. セキュリティ`, etc.), which is precisely and deterministically testable via exact heading assertions. The semantic completeness of each section's prose is not testable as a single assertion without fragile keyword heuristics that carry false-positive risk. This is not a design defect — the presence invariants ARE testable (exact headings), and the remaining prose-quality review is a documentation-review property, not a code invariant. The item is not testable only in the sense that prose quality is a non-deterministic documentation property, which is not an architectural defect.
- [Alternative verification] Source review of RFC-ROOT.md in the review phase; content-keyword assertions where a contract demands semantic content (e.g. purpose_scope_remains_audio_only already asserts `音声のみ`).
acceptanceCriteria: [Happy path] SipClient::new is called with a valid ClientConfig — returns Ok(SipClient) with initialized CoreReactor. All five module declarations (client, config, account, call, transport) are active in lib.rs. SipClient::shutdown() terminates cleanly. The compile-time invariant tests pass (no video types, all APIs return Result, SipClient is Send+Sync).
[Error case] SipClient::new is called with empty sip_proxy_host — returns Err(SipError::InvalidConfig("sip_proxy_host must not be empty")). CoreReactor is NOT spawned. No orphaned resources.

[Edge case] SipClient::shutdown() is called twice — first call succeeds (returns Ok(())), second call is a no-op (also returns Ok(()), verifying C044: Shutdown is idempotent). Calling any method after shutdown returns Err(SipError::Shutdown).

**[Happy path] — Crate identity complete; all invariant tests green**
- `make test` passes: 647+ unit, 37+ integration, doc-tests — all green, zero warnings.
- `SipClient::new(valid ClientConfig)` returns `Ok((SipClient, broadcast::Receiver<SipEvent>))`; `client.is_terminated() == false`; `client.handle()` exposes a live `RuntimeHandle`.
- `SipClient::shutdown()` returns `Ok(())` and terminates the reactor within 5s.
- `src/lib.rs` declares all RFC §6 modules as `pub mod` (client, config, account, call, transport, event, error, runtime, api, state, ffi, security, build, tests, model).
- All four ABC closures pass: O-001 `assert_sync::<SipClient>()`, O-002 `manifest.contains("metrics")`, O-003 `features_independently_selectable`, O-004 `let _: std::thread::JoinHandle<()> = join;`.

**[Error case] — Invalid configuration rejected; no orphaned resources**
- `SipClient::new` with empty `sip_proxy_host` returns `Err(SipError)` with `kind == SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig` and message containing "empty".
- `sip_proxy_port(0)` and `user_agent` > 256 bytes are likewise rejected by `ClientConfig::validate()`.
- On construction failure the reactor is NOT spawned: no `siprs-reactor` thread leaks, no command-channel resources remain, and no half-constructed `SipClient` is observable (the `Err` path returns before `Self` is built).

**[Edge case] — Idempotent shutdown and boundary values**
- `shutdown()` called twice: both return `Ok(())`; the second is a no-op (C044 invariant).
- `sip_proxy_port(65535)` (max `u16`) accepted; `0` rejected; 256-byte `user_agent` accepted; 257-byte rejected.
- `subscribe_raw_sip()` returns `None` when raw SIP is disabled, `Some(receiver)` when enabled — the Option boundary is exercised both ways.
- Feature boundary: `metrics`, `cpal-input`, `zeroize` are each selectable without being in `default = [...]`; `tls` and `srtp` are independently selectable (C003 invariant).

tickets.invariants:
- [Normal condition] P0-2 CoreReactor must be initialized before SipClient accepts commands — SipClient::new spawns CoreReactor via RuntimeHandle and blocks until initialization confirms. After successful construction, initialized == true.
- [Error invariant] On SipClient::new failure, no resources leak — If CoreReactor spawn fails or initialization returns Err, all allocated resources (channels, threads) must be cleaned up. No orphaned threads.
- [Internal state invariant] SipClient must hold a valid RuntimeHandle at all times after construction — RuntimeHandle is protected by Arc and cannot be invalidated externally. Drop order: SipClient first, then RuntimeHandle.
- [Boundary invariant] ClientConfig fields must pass validation before construction — sip_proxy_host must be non-empty, sip_proxy_port in [1, 65535], user_agent max 256 bytes, credentials password must use SecretString for zeroization on drop.

- [Normal condition] `SipClient::new` returns `Ok` only after the reactor thread is spawned and `backend.initialize(&config)` succeeds; the returned `RuntimeHandle.is_terminated() == false`. The facade never hands back a client whose reactor is down (C002 precondition).
- [Error invariant] On `SipClient::new` failure (invalid config or spawn error), no resources leak: the `Err` path returns before `Self` is constructed, the command-channel sender is dropped, and no `siprs-reactor` thread remains orphaned (acceptance error case).
- [Internal state invariant] `SipClient` holds `Arc<RuntimeHandle>` + `EventBus` + `ClientConfig` for its whole lifetime; `handle()` always returns a live handle; drop order is `SipClient` first (dropping `EventBus` receivers) then `RuntimeHandle`.
- [Boundary invariant] `ClientConfig.validate()` enforces `sip_proxy_host` non-empty, `sip_proxy_port ∈ [1, 65535]` (the `u16` type makes >65535 unrepresentable), `user_agent ≤ 256` bytes; `AuthCredentials.password` is `SecretString` (zeroized on drop, never visible in `Debug`).

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvements for P0-3:
1. lib.rs: Uncomment module declarations — convert [::STUB::] comments into active pub mod statements. Each module gets a one-line comment explaining its responsibility (noun phrase).
2. BootConfig → ClientConfig migration: Rename BootConfig::config: String to typed ClientConfig fields. This improves reader comprehension because "config" as a String tells nothing about its structure, while ClientConfig.sip_proxy_host etc. are self-documenting.
3. RuntimeCommand::Initialize { config: String } → { config: ClientConfig }: Replace opaque String with typed struct. This transforms a function that reads as "initialize with string" to "initialize with client configuration" — a transparent statement of intent.
4. ClientConfig validation: Extract validate() method with named error variants (InvalidConfig::EmptyHost, InvalidConfig::InvalidPort) instead of leaving validation implicit. This turns "check config" into "validate config structure" — a verb phrase that communicates what happens.
5. SipClient::new constructor: Implement the Builder pattern (already designed in client_config_spec.rs) for optional fields, keeping required fields in a non-optional constructor. This makes the calling code read as SipClient::builder().stun(...).ice(true).build() instead of SipClient::new(config_with_15_fields).
6. Apply the Boy Scout Rule to any runtime code touched during migration: ensure all functions read as verb phrases, all variables as domain nouns, no single-letter variable names, no hardcoded magic values.

### Re-implementation-round Boy Scout plan (test-precision hardening is translatability)
1. src/client.rs `_assert_send_sync`: widen the bound to `SipClient: Send + Sync` and add a one-line comment stating WHY both auto-traits are required (`Arc<RuntimeHandle>` + `EventBus` are Send+Sync; the facade must stay usable across `.await` points and `tokio::spawn`). This turns an ambiguous `Send`-only helper into a truthful `Send + Sync` claim (O-001).
2. `tracing_and_metrics_specified` (src/client.rs:383): the function name already promises "tracing AND metrics"; extend the body to assert both, making the name and body agree — a lying test name is comment rot (O-002).
3. New `features_independently_selectable` / `metrics_optional_feature` tests: extract a helper `parse_feature_section(manifest: &str) -> &str` that reads as "parse the features section" and is reusable across both tests; avoid hardcoded line numbers (O-003).
4. Extract config boundary constants into named consts: `pub const MAX_USER_AGENT_BYTES: usize = 256;` and `pub const MIN_SIP_PORT: u16 = 1; pub const MAX_SIP_PORT: u16 = 65535;` (src/config.rs) so `validate()` reads as prose — "if user_agent.len() > MAX_USER_AGENT_BYTES" — instead of magic numbers; the 256/257 boundary tests reference the same consts.
5. src/runtime/reactor.rs `reactor_spawn_creates_thread`: add `let _: std::thread::JoinHandle<()> = join;` with a one-line comment ("std::thread reactor model is an architectural invariant — C002") so the type assertion documents intent (O-004).
6. Do NOT refactor production behavior beyond these doc/const touches: facade, config, and reactor are already green and translatable. The round is test-precision hardening, so the Boy Scout effort concentrates on making the tests read as precise prose that cannot lie.

### ABC-round Boy Scout plan (test-precision hardening is translatability)
1. Extract a shared `read_rfc(path: &str) -> Result<String, std::io::Error>` helper (verb phrase: "read the RFC") to remove the repeated `std::fs::read_to_string("RFC-ROOT.md").unwrap()` boilerplate across the 6+ RFC-presence tests — turns duplicated unwrap lines into one reusable, error-propagating call.
2. Name the new tests as property statements (verb/noun): observability_section_documented_in_rfc, security_and_platform_sections_documented_in_rfc, audio_device_policy_and_usage_examples_documented_in_rfc, challenges_and_panic_policy_documented_in_rfc, rfc_contains_all_sections_through_61, crate_architecture_defined — each reads as "verify <invariant>" and cannot lie about what it checks.

4. Do NOT refactor production behavior: facade, config, and reactor are already green and translatable. The Boy Scout effort concentrates on making the tests read as precise prose that cannot lie.

contracts.postcondition: No new SipErrorKind variants are introduced for M20 — all M20 error conditions are expressed using existing SipErrorKind variants (InvalidState, AccountNotFound, NativeError). Postcondition tests: exhaustive 24-arm match compiles (exhaustive_match_over_sip_error_kind_has_24_branches); variant-count test asserts exactly 24 (sip_error_kind_variant_count_is_24); a hypothetical 25th variant (e.g. ConfConnectError) would fail both.
contracts.invariant: SipErrorKind variant count is invariant at 24. Verified via the variant-count list assertion (sip_error_kind_variant_count_is_24) and the exhaustive match. M20 mapping is fixed: (1) conf_port unresolved (PJ_EINVALIDOP) → InvalidState (native_status=None, retryable=false); (2) account deleted → AccountNotFound (retryable=false); (3) PJSIP API error → NativeError (native_status=Some(pj_status), retryable=true) — verified by conf_connect_other_error_keeps_native_status_and_retryable, conf_disconnect_other_error_keeps_native_status_and_retryable, get_account_info_pjsip_error_keeps_native_status_and_retryable, and m20_converter_distinguishes_state_error_from_ffi_error.

tickets.background:
- 【Goal】Complete the RFC §14 N0016 (SipError/SipErrorKind) and N0017 (M20 RuntimeCommand error mapping) design so that all four ABC inspection omissions (O-001..O-004) are closed against the CURRENT source tree. The production code already conforms: SipError (6 fields) + SipErrorKind (24 variants), native_error_with_status helper (m20:46-55), AccountInfo::from_entry (m20:131-147). O-003 (native_status always None on M20 FFI errors) was the implementation defect, already fixed; O-004 (convert_get_account_info_error unasserted) already closed. This ticket closes the two remaining test gaps: O-001 (compile-time Result<_, SipError> type assertions for all 9 public SipClient async fns — today only new()/shutdown() are pinned) and O-002 (message-context assertions for the ConfDisconnect and GetAccountInfo M20 error tests — today only err.kind is asserted). End state: every public SipClient async fn and every M20 converter is compile-time-verified to return Result<T, SipError>; every M20 FFI-error test asserts native_status, retryable, AND operation-context message; all 24 SipErrorKind variants Display their exact variant name.
- 【Purpose】Provide the unified, type-safe error foundation for the siprs public API so that every public surface returns Result<T, SipError> (RFC §14:612). SipErrorKind's 24-variant semantic classification lets application code handle errors without parsing message strings; the retryable flag guides retry logic; native_status preserves the PJSUA diagnostic code for logging/debugging; account_id/call_id carry operation context as NonZeroU64 newtypes. Under the ABC lens, this Purpose is only satisfied when it is translated into testable assertions — O-001/O-002 are the remaining untranslated remnants of this purpose.
- 【Motivation】P0-3's minimal 3-variant placeholder enum could not distinguish transient errors (Timeout → retry) from permanent errors (InvalidConfig → fix config). The subsequent implementation satisfied the type design, but the ABC Inspection proved remaining detection gaps: (O-001) if accounts(), add_account(), remove_account(), account(), add_transport(), call_state(), or subscribe_audio() changed to Result<_, String>, every existing test (.expect()/.is_ok()) would still pass — only new() and shutdown() are type-pinned; (O-002) if the ConfDisconnect/GetAccountInfo error messages lost their operation context ('ConfDisconnect failed' / 'GetAccountInfo failed'), conf_disconnect_other_error_returns_native (m20:271) and get_account_info_pjsip_error_returns_native (m20:298) — which assert only err.kind — would not detect it. Re-implementation is mandatory to make the design provably correct.
- 【Constraints】(1) No new SipErrorKind variants — the 24-variant set is an immutable public-API invariant (C017/C018); M20 errors reuse InvalidState/AccountNotFound/NativeError. (2) pj_status_t constants come exclusively from ffi::bindings (single FFI source of truth — PJ_SUCCESS, PJ_ENOMEM, PJ_EINVALIDOP, PJ_EBUSY); P4-2 plans a bindgen replacement; no local duplicates. (3) SipError is the crate's public error type — the 6-field struct and 24-variant enum are not modified; this ticket changes no field types and adds no variants. (4) Pure error-design test closure — no feature creep beyond the O-001/O-002 assertions. (5) TDD Red-Green-Refactor is mandatory; the new O-001/O-002 assertions must be added first and verified green against the conforming production code.

testExceptions: Exception — a live PJSUA session end-to-end M20 converter test cannot test the converters with a real pj_status_t. Reason: a real pj_status_t requires the FFI media stack (pjsua_conf_connect / pjsua_acc_get_info), which requires a live PJSUA session (P0-6 runtime) — an external runtime dependency not present in unit tests. This is not a design defect: the converters are deterministic pure functions over (pj_status: i32, call_id: u64) / (account: Option<&AccountEntry>, pj_status: i32), fully testable by supplying the ffi::bindings sentinel constants (PJ_SUCCESS=0, PJ_EINVALIDOP=150002, PJ_EBUSY=150003); only the value source is external. Alternative verification: unit tests pass the sentinels and assert native_status==Some(sentinel) and retryable==true; P4-2 bindgen validates constant alignment; a P0-6 integration smoke test confirms real pj_status flow.

Exception — the pj_status_t constant integer values are not testable as local Rust literals. Reason: the exact values (PJ_ENOMEM=-2, PJ_EINVALIDOP=150002, PJ_EBUSY=150003) come from ffi::bindings (bindgen under pjsua-native, stub aliases otherwise), an external FFI source — reading them as local literals would duplicate the source of truth. This is not a design defect: the conversion functions are pure i32→SipErrorKind/SipError. Alternative verification: tests use the ffi::bindings constants directly (both modules already do), so a bindgen value change is automatically reflected in the sentinel.

Exception — the AccountId/CallId newtype conversion at the FFI boundary cannot test the full round-trip. Reason: PJSUA ids are u32/u64 while SipError context fields are Option<AccountId>/Option<CallId> (NonZeroU64); the full conversion requires the real FFI layer (P0-6) — an external dependency. This is not a design defect: the newtype conversion is deterministic and unit-tested (nonzero round-trip, zero→Err/None). Alternative verification: unit tests sip_error_newtype_ids_round_trip_nonzero / *_zero_sentinel_is_none pin the boundary; the FFI layer applies AccountId::from_u64 at call sites.

Exception — the full SipError→UI display path is not testable in this ticket. Reason: the complete path involves the event bus (P0-5) and frontend rendering — external subsystems outside this error-design scope. This is not a design defect: SipError is a self-contained data struct with Display/Debug for diagnostics. Alternative verification: unit tests verify Display ('{kind}: {message}') and Debug (all 6 fields); P0-5 validates event bus embedding.

Exception — P4-2 bindgen constant alignment is not testable here. Reason: P4-2 replaces the ffi::bindings stub aliases with bindgen-generated pj_status_t values; until P4-2 lands, the stub aliases (matching PJSIP docs) are the source of truth — a future external change. This is not a design defect: the conversion logic is independent of the exact constant encoding. Alternative verification: record in notes that P4-2 must revalidate the InvalidState-vs-NativeError boundary tests against real bindgen values.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】All 9 public SipClient async fns (new, accounts, add_account, remove_account, account, add_transport, call_state, subscribe_audio, shutdown) are compile-time-verified to return Result<_, SipError> via the O-001 type-annotation helpers. All 24 SipErrorKind variants display their exact variant name (sip_error_kind_display_shows_variant_name_for_all_24). M20 ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect return Ok(()) on PJ_SUCCESS and Err(InvalidState) on PJ_EINVALIDOP with a conf_port message. convert_get_account_info_error(Some(&entry), PJ_SUCCESS) returns Ok(AccountInfo). From<ReactorError> maps all 3 variants correctly.

【Error case】A PJSUA FFI error (pj_status_t=150003, PJ_EBUSY) flowing through convert_conf_connect_error(PJ_EBUSY, 42) produces Err(SipError { kind: NativeError, message: 'ConfConnect failed: pjsua_conf_connect returned 150003', native_status: Some(150003), retryable: true, .. }). The same holds for convert_conf_disconnect_error and convert_get_account_info_error(Some(&entry), PJ_EBUSY). O-002 closure: conf_disconnect_other_error_returns_native asserts message contains 'ConfDisconnect failed'; get_account_info_pjsip_error_returns_native asserts message contains 'GetAccountInfo failed'. A conf_port-unresolved error (PJ_EINVALIDOP) still maps to InvalidState with native_status=None and retryable=false (state error, not FFI error). An account not found maps to AccountNotFound with native_status=None and retryable=false (permanent deletion).

【Edge case】Boundary values remain exact: PJ_SUCCESS (0) returns Ok from all three converters (no native_status leak); account_id/call_id zero is unrepresentable (NonZeroU64 newtypes — from_u64(0)→Err, maps to None at the FFI boundary); message='' produces Display '{kind}: ' with no panic; convert_pj_status(-9999) falls back to Some(NativeError); the 24-variant exhaustive match compiles — a 25th arm (e.g. ConfConnectError) would fail compilation (C018). The O-001 helpers compile and pass for a validly-constructed client; changing any public async fn's error type to a non-SipError type fails compilation.

tickets.notes:
- 【Implementation steps】TDD Red-Green-Refactor: (1) RED — in src/client.rs, extend sip_client_new_and_shutdown_return_sip_error (or add a sibling test) with the 7 missing type-annotation helpers (accounts/add_account/remove_account/account/add_transport/call_state/subscribe_audio) applied to the awaited results; in src/error/m20_runtime_command_error.rs, add message-context assertions (contains('ConfDisconnect failed') / contains('GetAccountInfo failed')) to conf_disconnect_other_error_returns_native and get_account_info_pjsip_error_returns_native. (2) RED confirm — run make test; the new assertions compile and pass because the production code already conforms (they are contract pins, not behavior fixes — O-003/O-004/O-002-Display closures are already in the tree). (3) GREEN — no production change is needed; verify the full suite stays green. (4) REFACTOR — Boy Scout: match the existing test style; re-run make test. (5) Add/refresh [::TICKET::] P11-15 annotations on the two changed test modules. (6) make test full suite green; run quality checks.
- 【Risks】(1) The new O-001 type-annotation helpers reference types (AccountSnapshot, SipAccountHandle, CallEntry, AudioTapHandle, AccountConfig, TransportConfig) that must be in scope in the client.rs test module — verify imports. (2) The O-001 helpers exercise accounts()/call_state()/add_account() etc. which require a running reactor — the test must construct a valid ClientConfig and bind the helpers only within the Ok branch of SipClient::new. (3) The O-002 message assertions assume the exact prefixes 'ConfDisconnect failed' / 'GetAccountInfo failed' — produced by the converters today (m20:104, m20:178); a future reword fails by design (that is the point of the closure). - 【Normal establishment】SipError is constructible with exactly 6 fields (kind, message, native_status: Option<i32>, account_id: Option<AccountId>, call_id: Option<CallId>, retryable: bool). SipErrorKind has exactly 24 discriminant variants. Both SipError and SipErrorKind implement Send + Sync for async API compatibility. retryable flag is set per variant (13 transient variants true, 11 permanent false — verified by sip_error_kind_retryable_is_consistent_with_new). Every non-EINVALIDOP M20 PJSIP error carries native_status=Some(pj_status) and retryable=true (native_error_with_status, m20:46-55 — O-003 closure).
- 【On error】Error conversion functions (convert_pj_status, convert_conf_connect_error, convert_conf_disconnect_error, convert_get_account_info_error, From<ReactorError>) never panic. No uninitialized SipError instances. On error, no code path silently drops the FFI diagnostic code: a non-EINVALIDOP pj_status must be preserved in native_status (O-003). An unresolved conf_port (PJ_EINVALIDOP) maps to InvalidState with native_status=None and retryable=false — the semantic boundary between state errors and FFI errors is stable.
- 【Internal state】SipError is a pure data struct with no mutable state — once constructed it is immutable (with_account_id / with_call_id return new instances preserving all other fields). SipErrorKind is a Copy enum (no heap allocations). The M20 converters are deterministic pure functions of (account: Option<&AccountEntry>, pj_status: i32) / (pj_status: i32, call_id: u64) — same inputs always produce the same SipError field values.
- 【Boundary】account_id/call_id use Option<AccountId>/Option<CallId> — None = context N/A; the PJSUA 0 invalid sentinel is unrepresentable (NonZeroU64 newtypes) and maps to None at the FFI boundary. native_status Option<i32>: None = no FFI code, Some(status) = pj_status_t value; converters never wrap Ok in Some(0). message is always String (constructors accept Into<String>); empty message accepted without panic. pj_status_t boundary: 0 → Ok/None, PJ_EINVALIDOP (150002) → InvalidState, every other non-zero value → NativeError with native_status=Some(value) and retryable=true.

tickets.title: Codec Policy, SRTP, Transport Reconnection & Shutdown Command Routing

contracts.precondition: Codec policy is defined in ClientConfig — either preferred_codecs non-empty (explicit mode) or empty (auto mode). Input schema (verified): `codecs: &[CodecInfo]` where `CodecInfo { codec_id: String }` with `new(impl Into<String>)`, and `preferred_codecs: &[String]`. Fixture ids: "PCMU/8000/1", "opus/48000/2", "opus/48000/1", "G722/8000/1", "iLBC/8000/1". Empty preferred slice selects auto mode. Testable form: build `Vec<CodecInfo>` + `Vec<String>` fixtures in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
contracts.postcondition: After `CodecAutoMode::apply()`, each enumerated codec maps to a priority in the returned `HashMap<String, u8>`: every `opus/*`→255, `PCMU/8000/1`→254, all others→0 (disabled). When `preferred_codecs` is non-empty, auto mode is bypassed and an empty map is returned (no priorities changed). Duplicate codec_id in the enumeration yields `Err(SipErrorKind::NativeError)` with message containing "duplicate"; no partial map is produced. Testable form (verified in source): apply_assigns_opus_255_and_pcmu_254_in_auto_mode, apply_returns_exact_priority_values, apply_bypasses_auto_mode_when_preferred_codecs_non_empty, apply_rejects_duplicate_codec_id, apply_empty_codec_list_returns_empty_map, apply_unknown_codec_receives_priority_zero.
contracts.invariant: Opus always receives priority 255 in auto mode; PCMU always receives 254. These are immutable named constants (OPUS_PRIORITY=255, PCMU_PRIORITY=254). Priority assignment is a pure function of codec_id alone (no state dependence). Priority values are u8: 255=max valid, 254=fallback, 0=disabled. Testable form: opus_invariant_always_255_in_auto_mode iterates the returned map asserting every opus/* == 255 and PCMU/8000/1 == 254.

contracts.precondition: Transport configuration is defined (TransportConfig enum with UDP/TCP/TLS variants per N0015). SrtpPolicy has one of three values (Disabled/Optional/Mandatory). validate() signature (verified): `SrtpPolicy::validate(&self, feature_enabled: bool) -> Result<(), SipError>` — feature_enabled is the runtime srtp feature flag (no #[cfg] in the function body). Testable form: instantiate each variant and call validate with both flag states.
contracts.postcondition: SrtpPolicy::validate() returns Ok(()) when (a) policy is Disabled (feature state irrelevant) or (b) policy is Mandatory/Optional AND feature_enabled=true. Returns Err(InvalidConfig) with message containing the policy variant — implementation formats `format!("SRTP {:?} requires srtp feature to be enabled", self)` at srtp_transport_reconnect.rs:63 (e.g. "SRTP Mandatory requires srtp feature to be enabled") — when Mandatory/Optional AND feature_enabled=false. Never panics — always returns Result. Testable form (foundOmission O-001, must be added): srtp_mandatory_requires_feature_enabled / srtp_optional_requires_feature_enabled assert `err.kind == SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig` AND `err.message.contains("SRTP")` AND `err.message.contains("Mandatory"|"Optional")`.
contracts.invariant: SrtpPolicy Disabled is universally valid. Mandatory and Optional are gated by the srtp feature — the validate function receives a bool feature_enabled flag that enforces this gate (no #[cfg], enabling testability without conditional compilation). Testable form: srtp_disabled_invariant_universally_valid loops both flag states for Disabled and asserts Ok; Mandatory/Optional are rejected exactly when feature_enabled=false.

contracts.precondition: Reactor shutdown sequence has started (is_shutting_down == true). A RuntimeCommand is submitted for dispatch. Command schema (verified, src/runtime/command.rs): `GetAccountInfo { native_acc_id: u32, reply: Reply<Result<AccountInfoSnapshot, ReactorError>> }`, `ConfConnect { call_id: u64, reply: Reply<Result<(), ReactorError>> }`, `ConfDisconnect { call_id: u64, reply: Reply<Result<(), ReactorError>> }` — `reply` is the `Reply<T>` wrapper (P10-4) constructed via `Reply::new(tx)` over tokio::sync::oneshot. Testable form: build commands with the test helpers make_get_account_info / make_conf_connect / make_conf_disconnect / make_other_command; pass is_shutting_down=true/false.

Returns Reject(SipError::new(InvalidState, "shutting down")) — kind=InvalidState, message containing 'shutting down', retryable=false — for ConfConnect, ConfDisconnect, AND all other commands (catch-all). When is_shutting_down=false, every command is Permitted. Testable form (verified): classify_get_account_info_permitted_during_shutdown, classify_conf_connect_rejected_during_shutdown, classify_conf_disconnect_rejected_during_shutdown, classify_other_commands_rejected_during_shutdown, classify_all_permitted_when_not_shutting_down.

### Goal
Deliver a corrected test suite for three already-implemented M20 policy modules: (1) two-layer codec selection — CodecAutoMode::apply in src/config/m20_codec_auto_mode.rs (explicit mode bypass / auto mode Opus=255, PCMU=254, others=0); (2) SRTP policy + transport reconnection — SrtpPolicy / ReconnectPolicy / TransportProtocol in src/config/srtp_transport_reconnect.rs; (3) M20 shutdown command routing — ShutdownCommandRouter::classify in src/error/m20_shutdown_routing.rs. The concrete deliverable of this round: resolve foundOmission O-001 (C043 message-context) by adding message-content assertions to srtp_mandatory_requires_feature_enabled and srtp_optional_requires_feature_enabled, while keeping contracts C042/C043/C045 at 100% test coverage. The O-001 (deterministic-jitter) and O-002 (tightened jitter bound) fixes from the P6-3 round are already present in the source and must remain green.
### Purpose
These policies form the core control layer for media configuration and lifecycle management in the M20 extension. Without them: (a) codecs default to PJSIP's built-in ordering instead of Opus-first prioritization, (b) SRTP cannot be controlled via config (always enabled or always disabled), and (c) shutdown behavior for M20 commands is undefined — the reactor would dispatch media operations during teardown, causing undefined PJSIP behavior. This re-implementation round exists because the ABC Inspection Pipeline proved the C043 postcondition's message clause was untranslated into test code: the two validate() error tests assert only err.kind, so a regression that omitted the policy variant from the error message would pass every existing test.
### Motivation
ABC criteria A (Contract Translation) and B (Violation Detection) flagged srtp_mandatory_requires_feature_enabled (src/config/srtp_transport_reconnect.rs:239-243) and srtp_optional_requires_feature_enabled (:248-252): they assert only `err.kind == SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig`. The implementation formats "SRTP {:?} requires srtp feature to be enabled" at :63, but no test verifies the message contains the variant name — a test-design defect, not an implementation defect; it must be corrected in this final round. These modules are preconditions for P1-2 (Security & Platform) and P1-3 (Audio Pipeline).
### Constraints
1. No FFI dependency: configure_codecs_auto_mode must produce a priority map (pure function) rather than calling pjsua_codec_set_priority directly — the FFI binding is deferred to P2-4. 2. SrtpPolicy::validate receives a runtime bool feature_enabled rather than using #[cfg(feature = "srtp")] in the function body, enabling testability without conditional compilation. 3. ShutdownCommandRouter::classify must be a pure function — no reactor state access, no async, no side effects. 4. No new dependencies beyond the existing Cargo.toml (no random crate for jitter — deterministic seed based on attempt number). 5. The `Initial Design Artifact` header in each target file must never be deleted or edited. 6. targetStubs/targetCrimes are verified_empty; the 1 foundOmission (O-001 message-context) must be resolved by ADDING test assertions, never by weakening the implementation or existing tests.
