tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】C042: when preferred_codecs is empty, CodecAutoMode::apply assigns Opus=255, PCMU=254, and all other codecs=0 for every enumerated CodecInfo; when preferred_codecs is non-empty, auto mode is bypassed and the returned map is empty (no priorities changed). C043: SrtpPolicy::validate returns Ok(()) for Disabled (always, regardless of feature_enabled) and for Mandatory/Optional when feature_enabled=true. C045: during shutdown (is_shutting_down=true), classify returns Permit for GetAccountInfo and Reject(InvalidState) for ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect; during normal operation (is_shutting_down=false) every command is Permit.
- 【Invariant on error】SrtpPolicy::validate must never panic — it always returns Result<(), SipError> with InvalidConfig kind for feature violations, and the error message contains the policy variant (e.g. "SRTP Mandatory requires srtp feature to be enabled"). CodecAutoMode::apply with a duplicate codec_id must return Err(NativeError) without partial priority assignment (no map is produced). ReconnectPolicy::new must reject invalid parameters (zero base_delay, max_delay < base_delay, jitter_ratio outside [0.0, 1.0]) at construction time with InvalidConfig, never at next_delay call time.
- 【Internal state】ReconnectPolicy fields (base_delay, max_delay, jitter_ratio) are immutable after construction — no setter methods provided; accessors return construction-time values. ShutdownCommandRouter has no mutable state — classify() is a pure function of (cmd, is_shutting_down) with no side effects. CodecAutoMode is a stateless unit struct; apply has no side effects and no dependence on ambient state.
- 【Boundary】Codec priority values are u8: Opus=255 (max valid priority), PCMU=254 (fallback), others=0 (disabled) — backed by named constants OPUS_PRIORITY and PCMU_PRIORITY. jitter_ratio must be in [0.0, 1.0] — values outside are rejected at construction. ReconnectPolicy::next_delay(attempt) with jitter_ratio=1.0 produces a delay in [computed, 2·computed] where computed = min(base_delay·2^attempt, max_delay); the same (attempt, policy) pair always produces the same delay (deterministic jitter even when jitter_ratio > 0).

phases.name: Omissions: Runtime State, Reactor Wiring & State Machines

tickets.title: Wire the real CallId assigned by the backend reactor from the MakeCall reply into the public API

contracts.precondition: Command serialization established — every public API operation (make_call included) is expressed as a RuntimeCommand variant dispatched through the reactor's serialized loop with a oneshot Reply channel.
contracts.postcondition: Public API designed around RuntimeCommand pattern — SipAccountHandle::make_call submits RuntimeCommand::MakeCall and returns Result<u64, SipError> where the u64 is the reactor-assigned CallId.
contracts.invariant: API is Send+Sync — SipAccountHandle and the returned CallId value must be safely shareable across async tasks.

contracts.precondition: Call API needs state — make_call must produce a CallEntry (state=Calling) that the reactor registers in ClientState.calls before replying.
contracts.postcondition: Call state machine defined — the reactor registers the CallEntry with the assigned logical CallId so Hangup/Hold/call_state operate on a valid id.
contracts.invariant: max_calls enforced — the reactor's ClientState.calls size must stay within the backend-reported max_calls; unique CallId assignment is the precondition for the max_calls bound enforced by the call-lifecycle ticket P6/P7.

contracts.precondition: Reactor thread owns single source-of-truth ClientState; Tokio runtime provides async RwLock for snapshot sharing.
contracts.postcondition: ClientState with initialized, accounts BTreeMap, calls BTreeMap, transports Vec, capabilities. CallEntry with id, native_id, account_id, state, media; conf_port_id NOT in CallEntry. After MakeCall the client_state.calls map contains the entry under the returned CallId.
contracts.invariant: Read-only snapshots via read().await (never blocking_read()); updates via write().await (reactor only). The returned CallId equals the client_state.calls key.

contracts.sourceEdge: P12-1 (new) — SipBackend::make_call → reactor → MakeCall reply → public API
contracts.precondition: SipBackend::make_call returns Result<(i32, CallEntry), ReactorError> where CallEntry.id is the backend-assigned logical CallId and the i32 is the native call id.
contracts.postcondition: RuntimeCommand::MakeCall reply is Result<u64, ReactorError> carrying the assigned CallId; the reactor inserts the CallEntry into client_state.calls keyed by CallId; SipAccountHandle::make_call awaits the reply and returns the same u64.
contracts.invariant: The MakeCall reply is sent exactly once on every outcome (success, backend error, panic); a failed MakeCall returns Err(ReactorError) and never fabricates a CallId (no hardcoded Ok(1)).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P3-2 (PJSIP FFI Layer, Runtime State & AudioMixer Architecture) defined the CallEntry state machine (C027) and ClientState with a calls map keyed by CallId (C046). SipAccountHandle::make_call was left returning a hardcoded Ok(1) because the MakeCall reply did not yet carry the assigned CallId. This work item resolves the marker by threading the real CallId assigned by the backend reactor through the MakeCall reply and returning it from make_call().

### Goal
Wire the real CallId assigned by the backend reactor through the MakeCall reply into the public API: SipAccountHandle::make_call must return the same CallId the reactor registers in ClientState.calls, eliminating the hardcoded Ok(1) at src/api/public_api_design.rs:157 (STUB TS-001).

### Purpose
SipAccountHandle::make_call currently returns a fabricated id (1) that does not correspond to any CallEntry in ClientState.calls. Downstream operations (call_state, Hangup, Hold) cannot operate on the fabricated id. Threading the real CallId makes the returned value a valid key into the reactor's authoritative calls map, satisfying C046 and unblocking the call lifecycle (P6/P7).

### Motivation
Source ticket P3-2 defined CallEntry and the calls map but left make_call returning Ok(1) because the RuntimeCommand::MakeCall reply type was Result<(), ReactorError> and could not carry the id. This ticket resolves that deferred marker (TS-001, pending). Without this wiring no call can be addressed by the reactor — call_state(), Hangup, and Hold all need the real CallId.

### Constraints
- RuntimeCommand::MakeCall is a public command-enum change: reply Result<(), ReactorError> → Result<u64, ReactorError>; every match site (Display, from_runtime_command, Debug for DispatchCommand, RuntimeHandle::submit) must be updated in the same change.
- The reply must be sent exactly once on every outcome (reply discipline); a dropped receiver is logged, never silently ignored.
- CallId remains u64 in the public API — the NonZeroU64 newtype migration is P4-1 (out of scope).
- No live PJSIP in tests: MockBackend must supply deterministic incrementing ids so tests are stable; the PjsuaBackend path (pjsua-native feature, backend.rs:522-550) already returns (call_id, CallEntry).
scope: **Scope of changes (path → action → detail → before/after):**

- src/runtime/command.rs — MODIFY — widen RuntimeCommand::MakeCall.reply to Reply<Result<u64, ReactorError>> (before: Result<(), ReactorError>); add a dedicated DispatchCommand::MakeCall { account_id, request, reply } variant (analogous to AddAccount) because an Execute closure only sees &mut dyn SipBackend and cannot register the CallEntry in client_state.calls; update from_runtime_command mapping (line 387-397) and the Debug impl (add DispatchCommand::MakeCall arm).

- src/runtime/handle.rs — MODIFY — add RuntimeHandle::submit_make_call(account_id: u64, request: OutgoingCallRequest) -> Result<u64, ReactorError> typed helper (analogous to submit_add_account at handle.rs:264-283); add `DispatchCommand::MakeCall { .. } => unreachable!("use submit_make_call instead")` arm to submit() (handle.rs:122-210).

- src/runtime/reactor.rs — MODIFY — add DispatchCommand::MakeCall handling in the reactor loop mirroring AddAccount (reactor.rs:240-260): catch_unwind around backend.make_call(account_id as i32, &request); on Ok((_native_id, entry)) insert entry into client_state.calls via CallId::from_u64(entry.id) and reply Ok(entry.id); on Err reply Err; on panic reply Err(BackendError) and follow the existing terminate/continue behavior.

- src/api/public_api_design.rs — MODIFY — SipAccountHandle::make_call (line 137-158): delete the dummy `let (_tx, _rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel()` (line 145) and the hardcoded `Ok(1)` (line 157) with the TS-001 STUB marker (line 156); call self.client.handle().submit_make_call(self.id, request).await and map ReactorError → SipErrorKind::InviteFailed.

- src/runtime/backend.rs — MODIFY — MockBackend (line 140-163): add next_call_id: i32 (first = 1) and make_call_result: Option<Result<(i32, CallEntry), ReactorError>> (error-injection, precedent: send_dtmf_result); MockBackend::make_call (line 235-250) returns the incrementing (next_call_id, CallEntry { id, native_id, account_id, state: "Calling", media: "none" }) and short-circuits on make_call_result; replace the production expect() at line 244 with AccountId::from_u64(...).map_err(ReactorError::BackendError)?.

**API contract change:** RuntimeCommand::MakeCall reply becomes Result<u64, ReactorError> (the assigned CallId). SipAccountHandle::make_call keeps its public signature Result<u64, SipError> — the u64 changes meaning from the fabricated 1 to the real reactor-assigned CallId. SipBackend::make_call trait signature is unchanged (already Result<(i32, CallEntry), ReactorError>).
**Data schema change:** none — CallEntry fields (id, native_id, account_id, state, media) and ClientState.calls BTreeMap<CallId, CallEntry> are unchanged; conf_port_id is NOT added to CallEntry.
**Config/env change:** none — no new configuration or environment variables.
**Dependency change:** none — no new crates.
**Out of scope (item → why):**

- pjsua_call_make_call FFI call implementation (P8-20 / P4+) → the FFI backend_calls::make_call already exists under the pjsua-native feature; this ticket wires the returned id through the reactor, it does not implement the FFI call itself (separate ticket scope).
- CallId NonZeroU64 newtype migration (C013 / P4-1) → the public API keeps CallId as u64 by explicit scope decision; the newtype migration is tracked in P4-1.
**Affected areas (component → nature → response):**

- src/runtime/command.rs + handle.rs + reactor.rs + backend.rs + src/api/public_api_design.rs → Nature: public enum shape change (MakeCall reply type) + reactor dispatch + facade return-value semantics. Response: all match sites updated within this ticket; downstream consumers (tests/verify_spec_p9_1.rs make_call_flow_dials, examples/make_call.rs, client.rs spec_examples) keep compiling unchanged because the public make_call signature is stable.

- Call lifecycle (P6/P7) → Nature: downstream consumer; Hangup/Hold/call_state now receive a valid CallId that is a real key into client_state.calls. Response: no code change needed in P6/P7; the fabricated id 1 is removed.
testUnit: UT: [C070 Normal] make_call returns the backend-assigned CallId — MockBackend::make_call_result = Some(Ok((42, CallEntry { id: 42, native_id: 42, account_id, state: "Calling", media: "none" }))) makes SipAccountHandle::make_call(request) return Ok(42); assert_eq!(call_id, 42) and assert the reactor inserted CallEntry id 42 into client_state.calls.

UT: [C027 Normal] make_call with a mock reactor replying Ok(42) returns 42 — the first make_call through a fresh SipClient + MockBackend returns the deterministic incrementing id (first call = 1); the returned u64 equals the CallId the reactor registered in client_state.calls under CallId::from_u64(entry.id).
UT: [Normal] Consecutive make_call calls return distinct CallIds — two sequential make_call(request) calls return id1 != id2 because MockBackend's next_call_id increments; assert_ne!(id1, id2).

UT: [C046 Normal] The returned CallId equals the CallEntry.id present in the reactor ClientState — after make_call, handle.query_state().await contains a CallEntry whose id == the returned u64 and whose account_id == the handle's account id.

UT: [C070 Error] make_call with a mock reactor replying Err(...) returns Err(SipError) with SipErrorKind::InviteFailed — MockBackend::make_call_result = Some(Err(ReactorError::BackendError("invite rejected"))) makes make_call return Err with kind InviteFailed and registers no CallEntry in client_state.calls.

UT: [C070 Error] A dropped reply channel makes make_call return an Err mapped from the oneshot recv error — after client.shutdown() the reactor is down; submit_make_call's rx.await fails with RecvError and make_call surfaces Err(SipErrorKind::InviteFailed) instead of a hardcoded value.

UT: [C070 Boundary] Backend-assigned CallIds are unique and start at 1 — MockBackend's next_call_id begins at 1 (NonZeroU64 lower bound); the third consecutive make_call returns 3 and client_state.calls holds three distinct keys 1, 2, 3.

UT: [C027 Boundary] max_calls — each successful MakeCall adds exactly one CallEntry to client_state.calls and never overwrites an existing CallId key; this unique-assignment property is the precondition that the max_calls admission control (P6/P7 lifecycle) later bounds.

UT: [C046 Boundary] CallEntry registration with zero-safe CallId — when the backend returns CallEntry.id == 0 the reactor replies the id but skips the map insert (CallId::from_u64(0) is Err) without panicking; when the id is >= 1 the entry is registered under the returned CallId.

UT: [C012 Invariant] make_call API is Send+Sync — compile-time assertions `fn assert_send_sync<T: Send + Sync>() {}` over SipAccountHandle and over the Result<u64, SipError> return type of make_call; the RuntimeCommand::MakeCall payload (account_id u64, Box<OutgoingCallRequest>, Reply<Result<u64, _>>) stays Send across the reactor MPSC channel.

UT: [C046 Invariant] read().await snapshots — the CallEntry created by make_call is observable through handle.query_state().await (never blocking_read); ClientStateSnapshot::read()/write() retain the async lock discipline (write().await only on the reactor thread).

UT: [C046 Invariant] CallEntry has no conf_port_id field — constructing CallEntry { id, native_id, account_id, state, media } compiles only if the struct has exactly these five fields (compile-time verification); conf_port_id lives in PjsuaBackend::resolve_conf_port (backend.rs), never in CallEntry.

UT: [C070 Invariant] MakeCall reply is sent exactly once — a panic inside backend.make_call (caught by catch_unwind) resolves the oneshot with Err(ReactorError::BackendError) and the reactor loop continues to the next command; the sender is never double-sent.

UT: [C070 Invariant] A failed MakeCall never fabricates a CallId — when backend.make_call returns Err, the reactor replies Err and the public make_call returns Err(SipError); the hardcoded Ok(1) is removed from the entire make_call path.
testIntegration: IT: [Reactor round-trip] Submit MakeCall, capture the returned CallId, then query_state()/call_state() contains a CallEntry with that id — full flow SipClient::new -> add_account -> SipAccountHandle::make_call(request) -> query_state().calls[&CallId] against the real reactor loop with MockBackend; assert the returned id is a key in client_state.calls and the entry.state == "Calling".

IT: [Disconnect] Hangup using the returned CallId succeeds against the reactor — make_call returns id N; RuntimeCommand::Hangup { call_id: N } dispatches backend.hangup(N) and returns Ok(()), proving the returned id is the one the reactor call lifecycle expects (the fabricated Ok(1) would be a no-op).

IT: [Consecutive calls] Two make_call invocations on the same account return distinct CallIds (1 then 2) and client_state.calls holds both CallEntry records under distinct keys — uniqueness across the MPSC command stream.

IT: [P9-1 compatibility] The existing Layer-5 integration test make_call_flow_dials (tests/verify_spec_p9_1.rs) still passes — account.make_call(request).await returns call_id >= 1; the public example examples/make_call.rs compiles and links.

IT: [Prerequisites] Requires the reactor running with MockBackend (the default in SipClient::new / CoreReactor::spawn); no live PJSIP or pjsua-native feature needed; every test must call client.shutdown().await to terminate the reactor cleanly (no leaked threads).

IT: [Related tickets] P3-2 (CallEntry/ClientState typing), P10-3 (SipAccountHandle facade), P7 (call state transitions consume the returned CallId), P4-1 (CallId NonZeroU64 newtype — out of scope, u64 kept).
testExceptions: Exception: The real pjsua_call_make_call native id assignment (PjsuaBackend under the pjsua-native feature) — we cannot test this path because it requires live PJSIP linkage (the pjsua library must be built and linked). Alternative verification: MockBackend supplies deterministic incrementing ids that exercise the identical reactor registration + reply path, and PjsuaBackend::make_call (backend.rs:522-550) already maps the native call_id into the same CallEntry shape. This is not a design defect: the native call boundary is an external-dependency seam abstracted by the SipBackend trait, and the wiring under test (reactor -> reply -> make_call facade) is backend-independent.

Exception: max_calls admission control (C027 invariant) — we cannot test this item because the MockBackend reports ClientCapabilities.max_calls = 0 and the reactor does not implement admission control yet; that enforcement is the call-lifecycle scope of P6/P7. Alternative verification: this ticket tests the preconditions of that bound — unique CallId assignment and exactly one CallEntry added per successful MakeCall. This is not an architectural defect: admission control is a separable feature tracked by P6/P7, not an untestable behavior of the MakeCall reply wiring implemented here.

Exception: The CallId NonZeroU64 newtype migration (C013 / P4-1) — we cannot test this item here because the public API deliberately keeps CallId as a raw u64 in this ticket's scope. Alternative verification: the NonZeroU64 invariants (zero rejected, uniqueness) are already covered by src/model/id_design_newtype.rs tests (call_id_from_u64_zero_rejected, call_id_from_u64_valid). This is not a design defect: the newtype migration is a tracked follow-up ticket (P4-1) and the u64 return type is a deliberate temporary contract.
acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path]** SipAccountHandle::make_call submits RuntimeCommand::MakeCall, awaits the reply via RuntimeHandle::submit_make_call, and returns the CallId assigned by the backend reactor (MockBackend returns 1, then 2, ...); the returned u64 equals the CallEntry.id registered in client_state.calls under CallId::from_u64(entry.id), so the hardcoded Ok(1) at src/api/public_api_design.rs:157 is gone.

**[Error case]** When the reactor replies Err(ReactorError) (backend rejection or a caught backend panic), make_call returns Err(SipError) with SipErrorKind::InviteFailed and never fabricates a CallId; when the reply channel is dropped before sending (reactor down), make_call surfaces an Err mapped from the oneshot recv failure instead of returning a hardcoded value.

**[Edge case]** Backend-assigned CallIds are unique across consecutive MakeCall commands (no two calls share an id); the first id is 1 (NonZeroU64 lower bound); the MakeCall reply is sent exactly once on every outcome (success, backend error, panic), preserving the RuntimeCommand reply discipline.

tickets.notes:
- [Implementation steps] (1) backend.rs: add MockBackend.next_call_id + make_call_result, replace the expect() at line 244 with map_err; (2) command.rs: widen RuntimeCommand::MakeCall.reply to Result<u64, _>, add DispatchCommand::MakeCall, update from_runtime_command + Debug; (3) handle.rs: add submit_make_call + the unreachable! arm in submit(); (4) reactor.rs: add DispatchCommand::MakeCall handler mirroring AddAccount; (5) public_api_design.rs: make_call awaits submit_make_call, maps errors to InviteFailed, deletes the TS-001 STUB marker. Keep the compiler green after each step (TDD: tests written first in the Red phase).
- [Risks] The reply-type widening is a public enum change — forgetting a match site (Display / from_runtime_command / Debug / submit) fails compilation, which is the intended safety net; do not silence it. The dedicated DispatchCommand::MakeCall variant must not regress the exactly-once reply discipline that Execute/AddAccount handlers already follow.
- [Caveats] CallId::from_u64(0) returns Err — the reactor must not panic when entry.id == 0; skip the map insert but still reply with the id. MockBackend's next_call_id is i32 and must be cast to u64 for CallEntry.id; the account_id conversion must not use expect(). The make_call_result injection is test-only and must default to None in production paths.
- [Open items] max_calls admission control remains unimplemented (deferred to P6/P7); the reactor's client_state.calls map is the count source for that future bound. The PjsuaBackend path (pjsua-native) is compiled behind a feature flag and is not exercised by the default test build.
- [Future improvements] P4-1 replaces the public u64 CallId with the CallId NonZeroU64 newtype; a typed CallHandle returned by make_call could carry the id and account id together (deferred).
Implementation summary:
- Changed files: src/api/public_api_design.rs, src/runtime/command.rs, src/runtime/backend.rs, src/runtime/handle.rs, src/runtime/reactor.rs

tickets.investigation:
## Source code evidence (verified 2026-08-07)

- src/api/public_api_design.rs:135-158 — SipAccountHandle::make_call: validates CallMediaConstraints::validate_strict (line 142), creates a dummy `let (_tx, _rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel()` (line 145) whose receiver is dropped immediately, submits RuntimeCommand::MakeCall via handle.submit (line 147-151), maps dispatch errors to SipErrorKind::InviteFailed (line 153-155), then returns hardcoded `Ok(1)` guarded by `// [::STUB::] P12-1` at lines 156-157 (TS-001). The reactor's reply is never read.
- src/runtime/command.rs:136-140 — RuntimeCommand::MakeCall { account_id: u64, request: Box<OutgoingCallRequest>, reply: Reply<Result<(), ReactorError>> }. The reply type cannot carry a CallId.
- src/runtime/command.rs:387-397 — from_runtime_command maps MakeCall → DispatchCommand::Execute closure `backend.make_call(account_id as i32, &request)?; Ok(())` — the returned `(i32, CallEntry)` tuple is discarded by `?`, so the reactor never registers the entry and never replies with an id.
- src/runtime/backend.rs:61-65 — SipBackend::make_call already returns `Result<(i32, CallEntry), ReactorError>`; the native call id is already produced at the trait boundary.
- src/runtime/backend.rs:235-250 — MockBackend::make_call returns hardcoded `(1, CallEntry { id: 1, native_id: 1, ... })`; it uses `AccountId::from_u64(...).expect(...)` at line 244 — a production expect() violating the Boy Scout rule.
- src/runtime/backend.rs:522-550 — PjsuaBackend::make_call (pjsua-native): `ffi::backend_calls::make_call` → map_pjsua_status → CallEntry { id: call_id as u64, native_id: call_id, ... } → Ok((call_id, entry)). The real backend already returns the correct id.
- src/runtime/reactor.rs:123-154 — DispatchCommand::Execute handler: catch_unwind(|| f(&mut *backend)); Ok(Ok(())) → send_reply(reply, Ok(())); Ok(Err(e)) → send_reply(reply, Err(e)); panic → reply Err(BackendError) + break. Execute closures cannot touch client_state (they only receive &mut dyn SipBackend).
- src/runtime/reactor.rs:240-260 — DispatchCommand::AddAccount handler — the exact model for MakeCall: catch_unwind(backend.add_account); on Ok((_native_id, entry)): `let entry_id = entry.id; if let Ok(account_id) = AccountId::from_u64(entry_id) { client_state.accounts.insert(account_id, entry); } let _ = reply.send(Ok(entry_id));`; on Err: reply Err; on panic: reply Err + break.
- src/runtime/handle.rs:122-210 — RuntimeHandle::submit injects a fresh (tx, rx) oneshot and awaits it; typed-reply commands (AddAccount / GetAccountInfo / AddAudioSource / QueryState) have `unreachable!("use submit_xxx instead")` arms and dedicated submit_* methods.
- src/runtime/handle.rs:264-283 — submit_add_account — the model for submit_make_call: is_terminated check → build DispatchCommand::AddAccount with a fresh Reply → sender.send → rx.await.map_err(|_| ReactorError::ReactorDown).
- src/runtime/state.rs:41-52 — ClientState.calls: BTreeMap<CallId, CallEntry>; CallEntry (75-86): id: u64, native_id: i32, account_id: AccountId, state: String, media: String — NO conf_port_id (C046/C048).
- src/model/id_design_newtype.rs — CallId(pub(crate) NonZeroU64); CallId::from_u64(u64) -> Result<Self, IdError> rejects 0 (test call_id_from_u64_zero_rejected).
- src/runtime/command.rs:521-529 — send_reply<T> logs "oneshot receiver dropped" when the receiver is gone — the exactly-once discipline is observable.
- tests/verify_spec_p9_1.rs:117-133 — make_call_flow_dials: `let call_id = account.make_call(request).await?; assert!(call_id >= 1, ...)` — the existing integration consumer that must keep passing after the wiring.
- src/client.rs:219-234 — SipClient::add_account facade — the model for the facade return (submit_add_account → SipAccountHandle::new).
- examples/make_call.rs — public example using account.make_call(request) — must keep compiling (client.rs spec_examples test asserts the API tokens).

## Design conclusion
MakeCall must become a dedicated DispatchCommand variant (analogous to AddAccount) because an Execute closure cannot register the CallEntry in client_state.calls. The reactor registers the returned entry under CallId::from_u64(entry.id) and replies Ok(entry.id); the facade awaits via a typed submit_make_call and returns the id. MockBackend must return deterministic incrementing ids (next_call_id) and allow error injection (make_call_result) so both the happy and error paths are testable without live PJSIP.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- Replace the discard pattern in SipAccountHandle::make_call (public_api_design.rs:145 `let (_tx, _rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel()`) with the typed RuntimeHandle::submit_make_call helper that owns the oneshot internally — the public API no longer touches oneshot primitives and cannot silently drop the reply receiver.
- Remove the fabricated Ok(1) and the TS-001 STUB marker (public_api_design.rs:156-157); the function reads as a verb phrase: "validate the media constraints, then submit MakeCall and return the assigned CallId".
- Document the MakeCall reply discipline (exactly-once send via send_reply) on the new DispatchCommand::MakeCall variant doc comment, mirroring the AddAccount doc.
- Remove the production `expect()` in MockBackend::make_call (backend.rs:244) — replace with Result propagation `AccountId::from_u64(...).map_err(ReactorError::BackendError)?`.
- Name MockBackend's incrementing field next_call_id (mirroring next_id for accounts) so the domain concept "call id" reads consistently across backend.rs.
- Extract the reactor MakeCall handler into a named helper (e.g. `fn handle_make_call(ctx: &mut MakeCallContext, account_id, request, reply)`) following the handle_send_dtmf pattern (reactor.rs), so the loop body stays translatable: "register the call entry in client_state, then reply with its id".
- Update every RuntimeCommand::MakeCall match site for the widened Result<u64, _> reply — no silent `Ok(())` / `Ok(1)` remains anywhere in the path; the Display impl already returns "MakeCall".

tickets.title: Implement startup account restoration by loading accounts via db.load_accounts() and calling sip_client.add_account() for each

contracts.precondition: ClientConfig is defined and validated before reactor spawn (SipClient::new calls config.validate() → Err(InvalidConfig) on empty sip_proxy_host). For P12-2 restoration, every restored AccountConfig must satisfy validate() before dispatch.
contracts.postcondition: AccountConfig specifies all 17 fields (display_name, username, auth_username, password, domain, registrar_uri, outbound_proxy, contact_params, transport, register_on_start, allow_outbound_without_register, registration_expires, codecs, dtmf, media, auto_reject_timer, headers). validate() enforces non-empty username/domain/password, ≥1 codec, ≥1 DTMF send/receive method, registration_expires > 0, and Opus range checks. add_account fails fast (C052) before submitting RuntimeCommand::AddAccount.
contracts.invariant: Validation rules are enforced at the facade boundary: an invalid config never reaches the reactor (test sip_client_add_account_rejects_invalid_before_dispatch proves no state mutation). Restoration must therefore skip (log+continue), never abort, rows whose config fails validate().

contracts.precondition: Standalone server mode (N0061) is configured; Axum router is built with shared AppState (Arc<SipClient> + Arc<DatabasePool>). For P12-2, build_router runs AFTER account restoration so restored accounts are immediately queryable via GET /api/v1/accounts.
contracts.postcondition: HTTP/WS protocol defines 18 REST API endpoints, 2 WebSocket endpoints (control+audio, audio-only), JSON text frame format (type/seq/payload), and binary audio frame format (AudioFrameHeader + PCM data). Axum router registers all routes. GET /api/v1/accounts reflects the reactor ClientState (C021) populated by the restoration step.
contracts.invariant: Event-audio correlation via sequence numbers is unchanged by restoration: SipEvent.meta.seq and AudioChunkPair.first_seq/last_seq share the same monotonically increasing global counter domain. A consumer can correlate seq=N event with first_seq=N audio chunk.

contracts.precondition: Standalone server mode (N0061) is configured; SQLite database path is specified in ServerConfig; DatabasePool::open(path) succeeds (mode=rwc creates the file). run_server MUST call init_schema() before load_accounts() so the accounts table exists even on a fresh DB.
contracts.postcondition: SQLite schema with 4 tables (accounts, transport_configs, client_settings, tls_configs) is created at startup via init_schema(). NEW (P12-2): DatabasePool::load_accounts() reads all rows of the accounts table as Vec<AccountEntity> ordered by id; empty table → empty Vec; missing table → Err(DbErr). Each AccountEntity maps to an AccountConfig (username, domain, display_name, auth_username, registrar_uri, transport, register_on_start, allow_outbound_without_register) for add_account. SeaORM migration files and Makefile targets remain available per C065.
contracts.invariant: rusqlite bundled feature ensures SQLite builds without system libsqlite3. DatabasePool uses a single connection (SQLite file-locked for writes) with busy timeout to avoid 'database is locked' errors. Startup restoration is idempotent: load_accounts is a pure SELECT (no writes) and re-running restoration cannot duplicate accounts; a saved account failing add_account is skipped with a warning, never fatal.

tickets.background:
【Goal】On standalone-server startup, restore every persisted SIP account from the SQLite accounts table so a restart re-registers the same identity set without manual re-entry.
【Purpose】run_server (src/api/standalone_server_config.rs:369-382) opens the DatabasePool but never reads it — saved accounts are silently not restored (P12-2 STUB at :382).
【Motivation】Persistence without restoration defeats the standalone-server contract: every restart drops all registered accounts. P4-3 defined the schema (C065) but left the read/restore path to this ticket.
【Constraints】Feature-gated behind sqlite-storage. load_accounts is read-only; password decryption and the full AccountEntity↔AccountConfig bijection belong to the persist path (out of scope). add_account is C052 fail-fast, so rows whose config fails validate() must be skipped, not fatal.

Before: no read path for accounts. After: callers can list all persisted accounts.

CHANGE src/model/sqlite_schema.rs — add private row→AccountEntity mapper (row_to_account_entity) handling NULL Option columns (display_name, auth_username, registrar_uri), INTEGER-as-bool flags (register_on_start, allow_outbound_without_register), and the password BLOB. Before: none. After: all 12 columns mapped.

testExceptions: The full run_server lifecycle (init -> restore -> bind -> serve) is not testable to completion because axum::serve blocks indefinitely. This is not a design defect: the restoration logic is extracted into the named function restore_accounts_from_db, which is fully tested against a real SipClient (MockBackend reactor) and a temp SQLite DB. The deterministic logic (load_accounts + add_account) has 100% coverage; only the blocking server loop is excluded from assertion.

Live SIP registration against a real SIP registrar is not testable without a network registrar. This is not a design defect: it is an external-network dependency. The restoration step's add_account is exercised through the real reactor dispatch path (RuntimeCommand::AddAccount -> MockBackend::add_account), so the entire command flow is verified without external network.

The exact AccountEntity <-> AccountConfig bijection (incl. password decryption) is not testable in this ticket because it depends on the persist/save path, which is out of scope for P12-2. This is not a design defect: it is a documented scope boundary owned by the persist-path ticket. load_accounts reads the encrypted password BLOB as-is, and the read-direction field mapping is unit-tested.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】run_server (sqlite-storage enabled) calls init_schema() then db.load_accounts() and sip_client.add_account() for each saved account BEFORE binding the listener; after startup sip_client.accounts() reports exactly the persisted accounts.
【Happy path】DatabasePool::load_accounts() returns the rows of the accounts table as AccountEntity values (ordered by id); an empty table yields an empty Vec.
【Error case】A DB error from load_accounts() surfaces as a typed startup SipError (NativeError) rather than silently starting with no accounts.
【Edge case】A fresh/empty accounts table starts the server with zero accounts and no error (guaranteed by init_schema() before load_accounts()).

【Edge case】Each AccountEntity maps to an AccountConfig (username, domain, transport, register_on_start, display_name) so the restored account is equivalent to the persisted one; an account that fails add_account is logged and skipped rather than aborting startup.
No account restoration occurs when the sqlite-storage feature is disabled.

contracts.precondition: Tokio async runtime must be initialized (tokio::runtime::Handle::current() succeeds). AudioWorkerTask must be spawned on Tokio blocking pool via tokio::task::spawn_blocking.
contracts.postcondition: AudioMixer struct created with lock-free queue boundary: crossbeam::ArrayQueue<Vec<i16>> out_queue separates AudioWorkerTask (async context) from RustMediaPort (PJSIP RT callback context). AudioWorkerTask runs process_frame loop in blocking pool.
contracts.invariant: No blocking operations (lock acquisition, dynamic memory allocation, syscall, .await) are permitted inside any function called from PJSIP RT callback thread (get_frame/put_frame). Only lock-free queue pop/push, memcpy, and zero-fill are allowed.
contracts.testPrecondition: testUnit validates: AudioMixer::new() creates struct with empty crossbeam::ArrayQueue. AudioWorkerTask::spawn succeeds when called from tokio::test context.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit validates: AudioWorkerTask::process_frame pushes mixed frame to out_queue. Mixer entry push operation does not panic.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit validates: crossbeam::ArrayQueue push from std::thread does not deadlock or panic. memcpy within callback context verified via mock port struct.

contracts.precondition: Rust FFI required to call C PJSUA library functions. Concurrency model defines reactor thread for serialized command execution.
contracts.postcondition: PJSIP FFI layer created with: (1) ffi::bindings module generated by bindgen build.rs with allowlist pattern, (2) PjOwnedStr safe wrapper for pj_str_t with Rust-owned Vec<u8> backing, (3) extern C callback functions enqueue NativeEvent, (4) runtime/ modules use only safe SipBackend trait.
contracts.invariant: All unsafe code isolated to ffi/ module. No unsafe keyword in runtime/, client.rs, or config/. Compile-time lint enforces unsafe isolation.
contracts.testPrecondition: testUnit: build.rs must exist with allowlist patterns. ffi::bindings module references pjsua_* types at compile time.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit: PjOwnedStr::new creates pj_str_t with ptr pointing to owned Vec<u8>. extern C callback compiles without panic.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit via compile-time: runtime/ directory grep for 'unsafe' returns 0 matches (excluding test code).

contracts.precondition: PJSUA C library uses pj_pool_t for memory allocation. Callback parameters valid only within callback scope.
contracts.postcondition: pj_str_t always has Rust-owned backing (Vec<u8>). Native callback pointers not held beyond callback scope. pj_pool_t memory never embedded in Rust structs.
contracts.invariant: pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory. Original PJSUA ptr only used as source for immediate copy, never stored.
contracts.testPrecondition: Deferred to P4-2/P5-2. P3-2 verifies only that PjOwnedStr ensures Rust-ownership.
contracts.testPostcondition: testUnit: PjOwnedStr::new copies input bytes to owned Vec<u8>. Dropping PjOwnedStr does not invalidate external pointers.
contracts.testInvariant: testUnit via compile-time: ffi/pj_str.rs contains no unsafe beyond initial pj_str_t construction.

tickets.background:
- 【Goal】Implement the memory-ownership model and default policies defined by RFC node N0056 (§47 Memory Ownership & §48 Default Policies) in src/model/memory_ownership_defaults.rs, replacing the empty `pub struct Model {}` stub, and re-export the new types through model/mod.rs.
- 【Purpose】Formalize who owns pj_str_t / pj_pool_t memory across the PJSIP FFI boundary: pj_str_t values always have Rust-owned backing, native callback pointers are valid only within callback scope, and pj_pool_t memory is never embedded in Rust structs (C057). Also record the RFC §48 system-wide default policies (transport, codec order, DTMF, audio delivery, raw SIP events, SRTP, ICE) as a typed data-model record.
- 【Motivation】P3-2 deferred the ownership model: memory_ownership_defaults.rs holds only `pub struct Model {}` + a P12-3 stub (line 23). Without the model, the FFI layer has no typed statement of which memory is safe to retain, inviting use-after-free bugs on pj_pool_t-backed strings. §48 defaults were likewise only prose in the RFC with no compilable representation, and the current config defaults already drift from §48 (e.g. AccountMediaConfig::default().ice == false vs §48 "ICE: enabled").
- 【Constraints】(1) Contract C057 is authoritative for ownership rules. (2) Contract C038: no unsafe in model/ — all unsafe stays isolated to ffi/. (3) Contract C034: classification helpers must be non-blocking (const fn) — usable from the RT-callback path. (4) No new bindgen bindings and no unsafe-code changes in runtime/. (5) The model layer must not depend on config/ (that would invert the layering — model is the lower data-model layer).

testExceptions:
EX: [C057] Live pj_pool_t lifetime semantics is impossible to test without a real PJSUA stack (not testable here).
Reason: verifying that a pj_pool_t-allocated pj_str_t becomes invalid after the pool is freed requires a live PJSIP installation (pjsua-native feature) and a running media stack; without it there is no pj_pool_t to allocate from. This is not a design defect (not an architectural defect): the ownership model is a data-model contract fully specified as type-level/documentation invariants, and every observable rule is verified against the concrete Rust-owned primitive (PjOwnedStr). The pool-lifetime rule is enforced by construction — PjOwnedStr exposes no raw-pointer constructor, so a pool-backed pj_str_t can never be adopted into a Rust struct.
Alternative: verify the mirror-image invariant instead — PjOwnedStr (the only pj_str_t holder in Rust) is Rust-owned and its classification is asserted in unit tests; the §47 doc-comments on MemoryOwnership::PjsuaPoolOwned carry the pool-lifetime warning.

EX: [C057] "pj_pool_t memory never embedded in Rust structs" cannot be tested by the Rust type system alone.
Reason: a C pointer (pj_pool_t-derived) is an opaque address; the borrow checker cannot prove where the pointee was allocated. Verifying this rule for every possible struct in the crate is not testable (impossible to test) — this is not a design defect (not an architectural defect): the crate enforces it architecturally by making PjOwnedStr the only safe holder of pj_str_t (a single choke point), which is itself covered by tests.
Alternative: a compile-time grep test asserts model/ and runtime/ contain no `unsafe` (C038), and a unit test asserts PjOwnedStr exposes no raw-pointer constructor, making pool-owned adoption unrepresentable.

EX: [§48] Applying the §48 default-policy record to a live PJSUA stack cannot be tested here.
Reason: DefaultPolicies is a data-model declaration (the source of truth for §48 defaults). Its application to actual transport/codec/SRTP/ICE configuration happens in the config and PjsuaBackend layers, which require a live PJSUA stack (pjsua-native) and are owned by other tickets. End-to-end application is not testable in this ticket — this is not a design defect (not an architectural defect): the model layer's contract is that the record matches §48, which is unit-tested.
Alternative: unit tests assert every DefaultPolicies field equals the §48 literal; a follow-up ticket aligns config defaults (e.g. AccountMediaConfig::ice currently false vs §48 enabled) with this record.
acceptanceCriteria:
- 【Happy path】memory_ownership_defaults.rs defines the ownership model (MemoryOwnership distinguishing Rust-owned vs PJSUA-pool-owned, plus NativePtrClassification and MemoryOwnershipTag) and the §48 DefaultPolicies record; the module compiles and the new types re-export through model/mod.rs.
- 【Happy path】The default policy matches C057: pj_str_t values outside FFI calls always point to Rust-owned memory (PjOwnedStr::classification() returns RustOwned); the original PJSUA ptr is only used as an immediate copy source, never stored (no raw-pointer constructor).
- 【Happy path】PjOwnedStr remains the concrete implementation of the Rust-owned backing (Vec<u8>) and satisfies the ownership model's Rust-owned policy via the MemoryOwnershipTag impl.

- 【Error case】The model forbids embedding pj_pool_t-owned memory in Rust structs (type-level/documentation invariant): CALLBACK_ONLY classification is pool-owned + callback-scope; PjOwnedStr exposes no raw-pointer constructor, so no owned pj_pool_t memory can enter a Rust struct.

- 【Edge case】Empty strings (slen=0, non-null ptr) and large inputs (>4096 bytes) remain valid and Rust-owned under the ownership model; classification helpers are const (no allocation) so the C034 non-blocking invariant holds on the RT path.

It is the concrete Rust-owned primitive the ownership model classifies.
- ffi/mod.rs declares pub mod bindings / pj_str / callback / backend_calls and documents the unsafe-isolation boundary (C038). model/mod.rs re-exports id/audio/aligner/resampler/media-bridge/raw-sip types and currently does NOT declare memory_ownership_defaults.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P3-2 specified the AudioWorkerTask and its per-call state (mixer, call_id, frame_duration). These fields are stored (src/runtime/audio_worker.rs:266-279) but marked #[allow(dead_code)] and never exposed. This work item adds inspection/query accessors so the runtime and diagnostics can read AudioWorker state, and wires call_id into logging/metrics correlation for when call lifecycle is active.

### Goal
Expose the per-call audio worker state (mixer, call_id, frame_duration) via read-only inspection accessors on AudioWorkerTask and AudioWorkerInner, remove the #[allow(dead_code)] attributes, and surface call_id in structured logging so diagnostics can correlate audio activity with a call.

### Purpose
AudioWorkerTask stores per-call state at spawn() (audio_worker.rs:288) but the fields are dead-code-gated and unreadable. Runtime diagnostics, metrics correlation, and future FFI thread inspection need a query surface to read which mixer/call/frame_duration a worker runs on.

### Motivation
P3-2 deferred the accessors as "reserved for future inspection". The re-implementation round (INSPECTION_FLAGGED) requires closing the gap: stored-but-unexposed state is dead code that masks the P12-4 stub (audio_worker.rs:266). Exposing it makes the state observable, removes the dead_code allows, and wires the first structured log lines into the otherwise-silent run loop.

### Constraints
(1) Read-only: accessors take &self and return immutable values/&references — no interior mutability, no write path (C046). (2) No unsafe in runtime/ (C038). (3) AudioWorkerInner is crate-private — its accessors are for in-crate/loop use only, not the public API. (4) The `handle` field (audio_worker.rs:279) belongs to P12-5 — untouched. (5) Metrics wiring is feature-gated and defers to a live call lifecycle (P8-13); this ticket only wires the log-line field. (6) No new dependencies — tracing = "0.1" already present (Cargo.toml:44).
scope:
**Scope of changes:**
  - src/runtime/audio_worker.rs (lines 265-280, 331-337): add `pub fn mixer(&self) -> &Arc<AudioMixer>`, `pub fn call_id(&self) -> u64`, `pub fn frame_duration(&self) -> Duration` on AudioWorkerTask (impl block at audio_worker.rs:283); add crate-visible equivalents on AudioWorkerInner (impl at audio_worker.rs:340).
  - Remove `#[allow(dead_code)]` on audio_worker.rs:269 (mixer), 272 (call_id), 275 (frame_duration), and 334 (AudioWorkerInner::call_id). The `handle` field (line 279) keeps its allow — owned by P12-5.
  - Add `tracing::info!(call_id, frame_ms, "audio worker spawned")` in spawn() and `tracing::trace!(call_id, frame_seq, "frame processed")` in run() (audio_worker.rs:342-347).
  - Before → After: state fields stored + #[allow(dead_code)] + silent run loop → state exposed via pure getters + structured log lines carrying call_id; no behavior change to process_frame/mixing.
  - API contract change: AudioWorkerTask gains three public read-only methods (additive; no existing signature changes). AudioWorkerInner gains crate-private read-only methods. runtime/mod.rs:23 re-export already exposes AudioWorkerTask, so the new methods surface automatically.
  - Data schema change: none.
  - Config/env change: none.
  - Dependency change: none added (tracing = "0.1" already in Cargo.toml:44).

**Out of scope:**
  - AudioMixer behavior changes, mix_i16_frame / process_frame logic — owned by P0-6/P8-1; unchanged by this ticket.
  - FFI capture/playback and the active JoinHandle — owned by P12-5 (audio_worker.rs:277) and P8-26; the `handle` field is not touched.
  - Real CallId from backend (src/api/public_api_design.rs:156) — owned by P12-1.
  - Call-lifecycle activation (P8-9/P8-13) and NativeEvent wiring (P12-7) — prerequisites for live metrics correlation, not this ticket.

**Affected areas:**
  - runtime::audio_worker module — accessor additions; purely additive, no behavior change.
  - runtime::mod re-export (src/runtime/mod.rs:23) — new public accessors surface via `pub use audio_worker::AudioWorkerTask`; only compile verification needed.
  - Diagnostics/metrics consumers — gain a read-only observation point (mixer/call_id/frame_duration) and a call_id-bearing spawn log line; no change required on their side.

UT: [C038] runtime/audio_worker.rs contains no unsafe keyword on non-comment lines (grep test) — the FFI/reactor safe-isolation invariant holds; no unsafe added by the accessors.

testExceptions: Exception entry: Live metrics correlation (call_id -> MetricsCounter/Gauge label) is not testable end-to-end without an active call lifecycle (P8-9/P8-13) plus a running metrics pipeline behind #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] — the metrics backend and call lifecycle are not implemented in this crate yet. This is not a design defect: the correlation logic itself (attaching the call_id field to a structured log line) is fully testable with a tracing subscriber that captures the `audio worker spawned` event (covered by IT: [Metrics]); only the metrics-backend round-trip is deferred. Alternative verification: the tracing-subscriber test asserts the call_id field on the spawn log line, and the accessor unit tests assert the value is directly readable.

Exception entry: Reading AudioWorkerInner state from outside the crate is not testable from an integration test because AudioWorkerInner is a private struct (audio_worker.rs:331) — by design (C046: no public write path; inner state is the worker loop's implementation detail). This is not an architectural defect: the same values are observable through the public AudioWorkerTask accessors, and in-crate unit tests (test_worker_inner, audio_worker.rs:860) construct AudioWorkerInner directly to verify its accessors. Alternative verification: in-crate unit tests cover inner accessors; the public API surface is covered by the AudioWorkerTask accessor tests.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】AudioWorkerTask exposes mixer() -> &Arc<AudioMixer>, call_id() -> u64, and frame_duration() -> Duration accessors returning the values passed to spawn().
【Happy path】AudioWorkerInner likewise exposes the same state (mixer, call_id, frame_duration) for the in-loop context.
【Happy path】After spawn(), call_id() returns the exact call_id argument (e.g., 42) and frame_duration() returns the exact Duration.
【Error case】Accessors are read-only - no mutation of mixer/call_id/frame_duration through inspection (accessors take &self and return immutable values/references).
【Edge case】A worker with frame_duration = 20ms reports the same Duration through frame_duration().
【Edge case】call_id is surfaced in worker log lines/metrics labels when present, with graceful absence when call lifecycle is not active.

【Happy path / concrete】spawn(mixer.clone(), 42, Duration::from_millis(20)) → worker.mixer() is Arc::ptr_eq(&mixer), worker.call_id() == 42, worker.frame_duration() == Duration::from_millis(20); the #[allow(dead_code)] attributes on audio_worker.rs:269/272/275/334 are removed; `make test` (cargo test) is green.

【Error case / concrete】No error path exists by design: all three accessors are infallible pure getters. Any attempt to mutate state through them fails at compile time (&self receiver + immutable return types). A test verifies that calling the accessors through a shared &AudioWorkerTask leaves is_running()/shutdown() behavior unchanged.

【Edge case / concrete】(1) frame_duration() with Duration::ZERO and call_id() with u64::MAX round-trip exactly. (2) State remains readable after shutdown() (shutdown only takes the JoinHandle at audio_worker.rs:318; fields are not cleared). (3) The `audio worker spawned` log line carries the call_id field; for a default/no-call worker (call_id = 0) the log still emits without falsely asserting an active call.

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- Replace the four #[allow(dead_code)] attributes (audio_worker.rs:269/272/275/334) with real accessors, making the fields live — the primary translatability win: fields become queryable instead of "stored but unused".

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P3-2 specified AudioWorkerTask with a Tokio JoinHandle for the blocking-pool worker. The handle is stored as `Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` (src/runtime/audio_worker.rs:279) and marked #[allow(dead_code)], so the worker's task lifecycle is not actively managed. This work item replaces the unused Option<JoinHandle> with a non-optional active JoinHandle and integrates shutdown so the handle is always awaited on shutdown.

### Goal
Replace the `#[allow(dead_code)] handle: Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` field in AudioWorkerTask (src/runtime/audio_worker.rs:273-275) with a bare non-optional `tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>`, and rewrite `shutdown()` so it always joins the worker task deterministically — logging a JoinError (worker panic) instead of silently discarding it. The worker lifecycle becomes fully managed: no 'no-handle' state is representable while the worker is alive, and shutdown guarantees the blocking-pool task has terminated when it returns.

### Purpose
AudioWorkerTask runs the per-call audio processing loop on the Tokio blocking pool. Its task handle is the only way to observe whether that loop is still alive and to deterministically join it on shutdown. The current Option-typed, `#[allow(dead_code)]` handle leaves a representable-but-invalid 'no handle' state, swallows the join result, and gives no compile-time guarantee that the worker is ever joined. Making the handle non-optional turns 'always own a live worker task' into a type-enforced invariant and makes shutdown's join behavior a guaranteed postcondition.

### Motivation
This is a flagged re-implementation round: the previous round left the Option<JoinHandle> + #[allow(dead_code)] in place, meaning the worker task lifecycle was not actively managed and a join error could be silently swallowed (`let _ = handle.await;`). The RFC contracts C034 (handle always present while worker alive) and C035 (shutdown stops frame production) require deterministic lifecycle management. Tech-debt driver: FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort) is still deferred, so now is the time to make the worker lifecycle robust before real media flows through it.

### Constraints
- Public API unchanged: `spawn(mixer: Arc<AudioMixer>, call_id: u64, frame_duration: Duration) -> Self`, `shutdown(&mut self)`, `is_running(&self)`, `mixer(&self)`, `call_id(&self)`, `frame_duration(&self)` keep their signatures; existing spawn/shutdown tests (src/runtime/audio_worker.rs tests + tests/runtime_audio_lifecycle.rs) must keep passing.
- No unsafe added — runtime/ must remain unsafe-free (C038); the change uses only safe Tokio/std primitives.
- FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort get_frame/put_frame) is explicitly out of scope until FFI audio integration is available; AudioMixer behavior is unchanged.
- The worker must be joinable exactly once and double-shutdown must be idempotent (the second `shutdown()` returns promptly without panic).
scope: **Scope of changes:**

- [src/runtime/audio_worker.rs:265-343] Action: modify — replace the `#[allow(dead_code)] handle: Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` field (lines 273-275) with a bare non-optional `handle: tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>` and delete the `#[allow(dead_code)]` attribute. Detail: `spawn()` (lines 284-314) stores the raw handle from `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` directly (`handle` instead of `handle: Some(handle)`); `shutdown()` (lines 317-322) is rewritten to always await the live handle with an idempotency guard. Before: `if let Some(handle) = self.handle.take() { let _ = handle.await; }` — a no-handle state is representable and the join result is silently discarded. After: `if self.shutdown_signal.swap(true, Ordering::AcqRel) { return; }` then `let live = std::mem::replace(&mut self.handle, completed_handle()); if let Err(e) = live.await { tracing::warn!(call_id, error = %e, "audio worker task panicked during shutdown") }` — the handle is always awaited exactly once and a JoinError is logged. API: unchanged (no signature changes). Schema: none. Config: none. Dep: none.

- [src/runtime/mod.rs:37] Action: verify — the `pub use audio_worker::{AsyncAudioSource, AudioMixer, AudioWorkerTask, MockAsyncAudioSource};` re-export must still compile; `AudioWorkerTask` remains `pub` with the same public methods.

- [src/runtime/audio_worker.rs] Action: add — a private `fn completed_handle() -> tokio::task::JoinHandle<()> { tokio::task::spawn(async {}) }` helper that yields an already-completed handle used to vacate the live-handle slot in `shutdown()`, so the real handle can be taken by value from `&mut self`. Detail: this keeps the field type a bare `JoinHandle<()>` while still allowing ownership transfer on join.

- [src/runtime/audio_worker.rs tests] Action: add — in-module tests `handle_is_non_optional_and_running_after_spawn`, `shutdown_joins_handle_and_stops_worker`, `double_shutdown_is_idempotent`, `shutdown_resolves_when_worker_panics`, `worker_keeps_producing_frames_until_shutdown`, plus the test-only `PanickingAudioSource` type. Before: the module had no tests asserting non-Option-ness or panic-tolerant shutdown. After: the compile-time non-Option proof and the panic path are pinned.
**Out of scope:**

- [FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort get_frame/put_frame)] Excluded — deferred until FFI audio integration is available; the worker lifecycle is verified with MockAsyncAudioSource only. Why: no real `pjmedia_port` exists yet (P8-7 cpal device I/O and the FFI audio integration are separate future tickets).

- [AudioMixer behavior / mix_i16_frame / source-gain-mute semantics] Excluded — the mixing algorithm and mixer API are unchanged; all existing mixer tests must stay green. Why: P12-5 scope is the worker task lifecycle only.

- [is_running() semantics for spontaneously-panicked tasks] Excluded — `is_running()` continues to reflect the shutdown signal only; detecting a task that panicked without shutdown is left as a future improvement. Why: the ticket's acceptance criteria only require `is_running() == false` after `shutdown()` returns.
**Affected areas:**

- [AudioWorkerTask consumers] Low impact — `src/runtime/mod.rs` re-export, `tests/runtime_audio_lifecycle.rs`, and design-model comments (src/model/media_bridge.rs, src/state/shutdown_specification.rs) reference the type; no caller depends on the Option-ness of the private handle field, so no caller change is required.
- [Shutdown behavior] Medium impact — `shutdown()` now deterministically joins the worker and logs JoinError; callers get a stronger guarantee (task terminated when shutdown returns) at no API cost.
- [CI / test surface] Low impact — new in-module tokio tests and the retained lifecycle integration tests run in the default `make test`; no feature matrix change.
- [FFI audio roadmap] No impact — this is a prerequisite hardening step; when FFI audio integration lands, the same lifecycle tests run against a real media port without API change.

acceptanceCriteria: **【Happy path】**

- After `spawn()`, the worker holds a non-optional `JoinHandle` — the in-module test `handle_is_non_optional_and_running_after_spawn` asserts `!worker.handle.is_finished()` right after spawn, which only compiles if the field is a bare `JoinHandle<()>` (no Option unwrap needed).

- `shutdown()` sets the shutdown flag and awaits the JoinHandle; after it returns, `is_running() == false` and the worker task has terminated — `shutdown_joins_handle_and_stops_worker` asserts both `!worker.is_running()` and `worker.handle.is_finished()`.

- A worker with active sources keeps producing mixed frames until shutdown, then stops cleanly — `worker_keeps_producing_frames_until_shutdown` asserts frames are produced while running and none are pushed after shutdown.
**【Error case】**
- `shutdown()` called twice is idempotent — `double_shutdown_is_idempotent` calls it twice and asserts the second call does not panic and returns promptly (the `swap` guard short-circuits).

- If the worker task panics, `shutdown()` still resolves — `shutdown_resolves_when_worker_panics` uses a panicking source and asserts the join returns `Err` which is logged, not re-panicked, and `shutdown()` returns normally.
**【Edge case】**

- `spawn()` from a tokio runtime context always yields a running `JoinHandle` (`handle.is_finished() == false` immediately after spawn) — asserted at t=0 by `handle_is_non_optional_and_running_after_spawn`.

- `Duration::ZERO` frame cadence and `u64::MAX` call_id do not deadlock or misroute shutdown — `boundary_values_round_trip_exactly` remains green and the zero-cadence loop still observes the shutdown signal within one iteration.

- Existing lifecycle integration tests (`audio_worker_spawns_and_produces_mixed_output`, `multiple_audio_workers_use_independent_mixers`) remain green with the non-optional handle — no regression in the multi-worker path.

tickets.invariants:
- AudioWorkerTask is spawned on the Tokio blocking pool via spawn_blocking and the JoinHandle is always present while the worker is alive (C034).
- The shutdown flag is set atomically; the worker loop exits on the next iteration after the flag is set; no new frames are pushed after shutdown (C035).
- No unsafe added; runtime/ remains unsafe-free (C038).

- [Normal condition] The `handle` field is a bare `tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>` (never `Option`) from `spawn()` until the first `shutdown()`; `handle.is_finished() == false` immediately after spawn (C034 precondition). `shutdown()` requires a live Tokio runtime context (`#[tokio::test]` or reactor) so the join can be awaited.
- [Error invariant] A JoinError from the joined task (worker panicked) must never propagate as a panic from `shutdown()` — it is logged via `tracing::warn!` and `shutdown()` returns normally. A second `shutdown()` after the first has completed must not touch the already-consumed handle (idempotency guard via `shutdown_signal.swap(true, Ordering::AcqRel)`), so no use-after-join or double-join is possible.
- [Internal state invariant] `shutdown_signal` is an `Arc<AtomicBool>`; it is set to `true` exactly once by the first `shutdown()` and read by `is_running()` (Acquire) and the worker loop (Acquire). While the signal is `false`, the worker loop keeps producing frames; once `true`, the loop exits after the current iteration and the task completes, making the handle finish.
- [Boundary invariant] `Duration::ZERO` frame cadence and `u64::MAX` call_id must not deadlock `shutdown()`; the loop observes the shutdown signal within one iteration even at zero cadence. The replacement handle slot after shutdown holds an already-completed task, so `handle.is_finished()` is `true` post-shutdown and remains a valid (non-Option) handle.

tickets.investigation:
- src/runtime/audio_worker.rs:273-275 — the `[::STUB::] P12-5` marker sits directly above `#[allow(dead_code)] handle: Option<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` (lines 274-275). `spawn()` (lines 284-314) creates the handle via `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` and stores `handle: Some(handle)` (line 312). `shutdown()` (lines 317-322) does `if let Some(handle) = self.handle.take() { let _ = handle.await; }` — the Option is partially used but still Option-typed and marked dead_code, leaving a 'no handle' state representable and the JoinError silently discarded.
- AudioWorkerInner.run() (lines 375-383) loops `while !self.shutdown_signal.load(Ordering::Acquire)` calling `process_frame()` then `tokio::time::sleep(self.frame_duration())`. process_frame (lines 392-434) snapshots source_ids from the DashMap, pulls each source via next_chunk, applies gain/mute, mixes with `mix_i16_frame` (i32 accumulation → saturating i16 clamp), and pushes to `out_queue`. The shutdown signal is the only mechanism that terminates the loop.
- is_running() (lines 325-327) returns `!self.shutdown_signal.load(Ordering::Acquire)` — it reflects the signal, not `handle.is_finished()`. After `shutdown()` the signal is true so is_running() is false.
- Tests already present: `audio_worker_spawn_and_shutdown`, `audio_worker_multiple_workers_independent_mixers`, `accessors_return_exact_spawn_args`, `state_remains_readable_after_shutdown`, `boundary_values_round_trip_exactly`, `spawn_log_carries_call_id_field`, the process_frame O-002 tests (`process_frame_pushes_mixed_frame`, `process_frame_two_sources_mixes`, `process_frame_skips_muted_source`, `process_frame_applies_gain`, `process_frame_zero_sources_silence`), and the grep tests (`audio_worker_has_no_unsafe_keyword`, `no_blocking_lock_patterns_introduced`). None currently assert non-Option-ness, panic-tolerant shutdown, or no-frames-after-shutdown.
- Design evidence: RFC §24 (N0033) specifies the two-layer architecture with the lock-free queue boundary; the worker must be spawned on the blocking pool (C034) and shutdown must stop frame production (C035). C038 requires runtime/ to stay unsafe-free — the fix uses only `tokio::task::JoinHandle`, `spawn_blocking`, `AtomicBool`, and `std::mem::replace`.
- JoinHandle ownership constraint: `JoinHandle::await` consumes the handle, so from `&mut self` the live handle must be moved out via `std::mem::replace`. Since `JoinHandle` has no `Default`, a sentinel is required — the chosen sentinel is `tokio::task::spawn(async {})` (an already-completed no-op task), kept private in `completed_handle()`. The `swap(true, AcqRel)` idempotency guard makes double-shutdown safe.
- FFI audio capture/playback (RustMediaPort get_frame/put_frame) is deferred: src/model/media_bridge.rs holds the design model only; there is no real `pjmedia_port` to test. P8-7 (cpal device I/O) is the future real-source ticket.

tickets.title: Upgrade the Weak<JoinHandle> to Arc and expose it for FFI thread lifecycle inspection once pjsua is linked

contracts.precondition: Rust FFI required to call C PJSUA library functions. Concurrency model defines the reactor thread (std::thread::Builder, reactor.rs:106-108) for serialized command execution; its JoinHandle is the only handle to that thread. The runtime/handle.rs change must not alter this thread model.

Additionally, RuntimeHandle exposes reactor-thread lifecycle inspection via Arc<JoinHandle<()>> without leaking any FFI type into runtime/.
contracts.invariant: All unsafe code isolated to ffi/ module. No unsafe keyword in runtime/, client.rs, or config/. The Weak→Arc upgrade in runtime/handle.rs introduces zero unsafe. Compile-time lint enforces unsafe isolation.

contracts.precondition: Reactor thread owns single source-of-truth ClientState. Tokio runtime provides async RwLock for snapshot sharing. The reactor thread is the SAME thread whose JoinHandle is stored in RuntimeHandle, so its lifecycle is observable from the handle.

CallEntry with id, native_id, account_id, state, media. conf_port_id NOT in CallEntry. RuntimeHandle::is_thread_alive()/thread_handle().is_finished() lets an observer correlate reactor-thread liveness with ClientState without a command round-trip (O-001 pattern).
contracts.invariant: Read-only snapshots via read().await (never blocking_read()). Updates via write().await (reactor only). Thread-lifecycle inspection is non-blocking (no lock, no await) and never mutates reactor state.

contracts.precondition: CoreReactor::spawn must obtain the reactor thread's JoinHandle BEFORE constructing RuntimeHandle (thread-first ordering, reactor.rs reorder). The thread is spawned via std::thread::Builder — never tokio::task::spawn.
contracts.postcondition: RuntimeHandle::new accepts Arc<JoinHandle<()>>; spawn stores the Arc and returns an Arc clone sharing the same underlying thread — verified by Arc::ptr_eq(handle.thread_handle(), &returned_arc) and Thread::id equality. An inspection accessor (thread_handle() -> &Arc<JoinHandle<()>> and/or is_thread_alive() -> bool) reports reactor-thread liveness via JoinHandle::is_finished().
contracts.invariant: RuntimeHandle remains Send + Sync and Clone. The join_handle field is always a live Arc<JoinHandle<()>> — never Weak, never Option, never a dangling handle; the #[allow(dead_code)] is removed because the accessor consumes the field. Dropping all handle clones does not terminate the reactor thread.

tickets.background:
### Goal
Upgrade the dead `Weak<JoinHandle<()>>` field in RuntimeHandle (handle.rs:30-32) to a live `Arc<JoinHandle<()>>` and expose a thread-lifecycle inspection accessor (`thread_handle()` / `is_thread_alive()`), so an FFI observer can query reactor-thread liveness once pjsua is linked.

### Purpose
The stored weak reference can never upgrade — reactor.rs:101 passes `std::sync::Weak::new()` while the real JoinHandle is returned to the caller at reactor.rs:461 — so the field is permanently None and carries zero information. An Arc that shares the caller's JoinHandle makes the reactor-thread lifecycle observable through the handle: the missing FFI thread-lifecycle query point identified in source ticket P3-2 (C038).

### Motivation
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::] This ticket was returned for re-implementation because the stub marker (handle.rs:30 `// [::STUB::] P12-6: ...`) and the `#[allow(dead_code)]` guard remain unresolved. P12-5 (commit d7750f77) already demonstrated the "non-optional live JoinHandle" pattern in audio_worker.rs; this ticket applies the same pattern to the reactor handle so FFI thread inspection (P8-5 bindgen / P8-21 callback registration) has a deterministic query point.

### Constraints
The reactor thread stays std::thread-based (never tokio::task::spawn) per the type assertion at reactor.rs:1087 and C002. No unsafe is introduced in runtime/ (C038 — unsafe confined to ffi/). RuntimeHandle stays Send + Sync + Clone (C012). The spawn return contract changes from `JoinHandle<()>` to `Arc<JoinHandle<()>>` because JoinHandle is not Clone — all destructuring call sites (client.rs:100, reactor.rs tests, tests/runtime_audio_lifecycle.rs) must update atomically.

Remove `use std::sync::Weak;` (handle.rs:5) once unused. Update the Send+Sync doc comment (handle.rs:17) from `- Weak<JoinHandle<()>>: Send + Sync.` to `- Arc<JoinHandle<()>>: Send + Sync.`

Spawn the std::thread (line 106-108), wrap the returned JoinHandle in `Arc::new(thread_join)`, pass `reactor_join.clone()` into `RuntimeHandle::new` (replacing `std::sync::Weak::new()` at line 101), and return `(handle, reactor_join)`. The thread closure captures `rx`/`backend`/`audio_mixer`/`terminated`/`client_event_buses`/`dtmf_sent_timeout_ms`/`timer_runtime` — NOT `tx` — so no sender clone is needed.
src/runtime/reactor.rs:461 — modify: spawn return type changes from `(RuntimeHandle, JoinHandle<()>)` to `(RuntimeHandle, Arc<JoinHandle<()>>)`.

Before → After: Before: `handle.rs:31-32` = `#[allow(dead_code)] join_handle: Weak<JoinHandle<()>>`; `RuntimeHandle::new(..., join_handle: Weak<JoinHandle<()>>, ...)`; `reactor.rs:101` = `std::sync::Weak::new()`; spawn returns `(RuntimeHandle, JoinHandle<()>)`. After: `join_handle: Arc<JoinHandle<()>>` (no allow); `new(..., join_handle: Arc<JoinHandle<()>>, ...)`; reactor spawns thread first, stores `Arc::new(thread_join)`, returns `(RuntimeHandle, Arc<JoinHandle<()>>)`; accessors `thread_handle()` + `is_thread_alive()` read the live Arc.

API contract change (Y): `CoreReactor::spawn` return type `JoinHandle<()>` → `Arc<JoinHandle<()>>` (JoinHandle is not Clone, so sharing the thread with the handle requires Arc). `RuntimeHandle::new` (pub(crate)) signature changes. New public accessors `RuntimeHandle::thread_handle() -> &Arc<JoinHandle<()>>` and `RuntimeHandle::is_thread_alive() -> bool`. Call sites updated: client.rs:100 (`let (handle, _join)`), spawn_reactor() helpers (reactor.rs:688, tests/runtime_audio_lifecycle.rs:28), shutdown_reactor (reactor.rs:1153), type assertion (reactor.rs:1087).
Data schema change: none — no serialized/deserialized data is touched; the change is purely in-memory (field type + accessors).
Config/env change: none — no new config keys, env vars, or CLI flags.
Dependency change: none added/removed — `std::sync::Arc` and `std::thread::JoinHandle` are std. The `use std::sync::Weak;` import (handle.rs:5) is removed as dead code.
Out of scope — item: PJSUA C linkage / bindgen (P8-5); FFI callback registration (P8-21); any actual FFI consumer of the exposed Arc (e.g. an extern C function reading is_thread_alive()).

Why excluded: those tickets own the pjsua-native linkage and callback registration; this ticket only prepares the runtime query point. Implementing the FFI observer here would couple this ticket to P8-5/P8-21 and violate ticket boundaries.

Affected component: SipClient::new (client.rs:100) destructures the spawn return; all test helpers that join the reactor (reactor.rs and tests/runtime_audio_lifecycle.rs); observability consumers that will read `is_thread_alive()`.
Nature of impact: API surface (spawn return type + new RuntimeHandle public accessors); no performance/security/data-format impact (Arc clone is a refcount bump; inspection is lock-free).

testExceptions: [Item] Actual OS-thread mid-life liveness (asserting the reactor thread is alive at an arbitrary instant) is not testable deterministically because is_finished() is inherently racy: the reactor thread may exit between the assertion and the observer read, and there is no scheduling point that guarantees "alive now" across platforms. This is not a design defect and not an architectural defect — the deterministic, testable contract is thread IDENTITY (Arc::ptr_eq / Thread::id) and the boundary states (alive-right-after-spawn, dead-after-join), which ARE fully covered by testUnit. The racy part is only timing, not the design.

[Item] FFI consumers of the exposed Arc<JoinHandle> (the actual extern-C observer that reads is_thread_alive()) are not testable in unit tests because they require the pjsua-native linkage (P8-5, bindgen) and callback registration (P8-21) that are not linked into the crate test binary. This is not a design defect and not an architectural defect — it is an external-dependency gap owned by P8-5/P8-21; this ticket's testable surface is the RuntimeHandle accessor itself, covered by testUnit.

[Item] Mid-life liveness across platform scheduling (the "thread is alive at time T" assertion) is impossible to test portably. [Alternative verification] Verify the deterministic boundary states instead: (1) "not finished immediately after spawn" — the reactor loop is alive right after thread::Builder::spawn returns (happens-before via spawn); (2) "finished after join" — the join barrier establishes happens-before, so is_finished() is guaranteed true. Both are scheduling-independent, replace the untestable mid-life assertion, and are already listed in testUnit; this is not a design defect and not an architectural defect.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】RuntimeHandle stores the reactor thread's JoinHandle as Arc<JoinHandle<()>> and exposes an inspection accessor (`thread_handle() -> &Arc<JoinHandle<()>>` and `is_thread_alive() -> bool`). CoreReactor::spawn (reactor.rs:58) passes the actual spawned thread's join handle into RuntimeHandle::new (thread-first ordering, reactor.rs:98-108), and the stored Arc is the same thread the caller joins at reactor.rs:461 — verified by Arc::ptr_eq(handle.thread_handle(), &returned_arc) and Thread::id equality.

【Happy path】RuntimeHandle remains Send + Sync and Clone after the change; the compile-time assert_send/assert_sync tests at handle.rs:415-421 stay green. The #[allow(dead_code)] on the join_handle field is removed once the Arc is consumed by the inspection accessor.

【Happy path】A cloned RuntimeHandle shares the same Arc<JoinHandle> allocation — `Arc::ptr_eq(clone.thread_handle(), original.thread_handle())` is true — so thread inspection from any clone reports the same underlying thread.

【Error case】A panicked reactor thread is observable: is_terminated() (AtomicBool, reactor.rs:262) and is_thread_alive()/is_finished() both report the dead state; the inspection accessor never panics on a dead thread (join() on a panicked thread returns Err but is_finished() stays safe).

【Edge case】Dropping all RuntimeHandle clones (last Arc strong ref) does NOT terminate the reactor thread — the OS thread's lifecycle is independent of the handle refcount and ends only on Shutdown/panic/channel-close. is_thread_alive() on a running reactor returns true; after Shutdown + join, it returns false (deterministic boundary states).

- 【Internal state invariant】The join_handle field is always a live Arc<JoinHandle<()>> — never Weak, never Option, never a dangling handle. Every RuntimeHandle has exactly one underlying reactor-thread identity; clones share the same Arc allocation (Arc::ptr_eq). The #[allow(dead_code)] attribute is removed because the thread_handle()/is_thread_alive() accessors consume the field.
- 【Boundary invariant】Dropping all RuntimeHandle clones (Arc refcount → 0) does NOT terminate the reactor thread — the OS thread's lifecycle is independent of the handle's Arc refcount and ends only on Shutdown/panic/channel-close. is_thread_alive() on any clone reports the same result as on the original (shared Arc, same is_finished state).

6. handle.rs:415-421 — compile-time `const fn assert_send<T: Send>() {}` / `assert_sync` with `assert_send::<RuntimeHandle>()` (@verifies C012) — must stay green.

9. reactor.rs:461 — `Ok((handle, thread_join))` returns the real JoinHandle to the caller; the caller (client.rs:100) currently discards it as `_join`.
