tickets.title: Wire dispatch_event and process_native_event (with its extract_event_ids helper) into the reactor loop so NativeEvents delivered by the FFI callback bridge are processed

contracts.precondition: PJSIP FFI layer exists with callback bridge functions (ffi/callback.rs register_callbacks installs the event queue). SipBackend trait defined (runtime/backend.rs MockBackend/PjsuaBackend). Multiple SipClient instances may share the PjsuaBackend singleton. Reactor owns a default_event_bus and a client_event_buses map (reactor.rs:85-92). Testable form: Box<dyn SipBackend> is constructible from MockBackend; RuntimeHandle exposes default_event_bus() and enqueue_native_event(). Covered by UT [Normal] reactor round-trip.
contracts.postcondition: Dual-client callback routing: a single Reactor receives all NativeEvents. RuntimeHandle::enqueue_native_event delivers the NativeEvent to the loop (DispatchCommand::NativeEvent); process_native_event converts it (registration via backend.get_account_info -> registration_status_to_payload; other P0 via convert_native_event_to_payload); dispatch_event resolves account_id and routes to the correct SipClient EventBus (matching client bus only; unmatched -> default; None -> default + all client buses). Testable form: enqueued RegistrationStateChanged yields RegistrationSucceeded on the default bus with meta.account_id set; a client-bus event reaches only that bus. Covered by UT [Normal] reactor round-trip, UT [Error], UT [Invariant] C039.
contracts.invariant: Single Reactor pattern preserved: all NativeEvents are processed serially on the one reactor thread (no second consumer). No event duplication across multiple clients: dispatch_event routes Some(account_id) to exactly one bus; None broadcasts by design to all buses but never duplicates a routed event. Testable form: dispatch_event_routes_to_matching_bus_only / dispatch_event_none_account_broadcasts_to_all / dispatch_event_unmatched_account_falls_back_to_default. Covered by UT [Normal]/[Invariant] C039 entries.

contracts.precondition: Reactor thread owns the single source-of-truth ClientState (reactor.rs:112 client_state; QueryState returns a clone at reactor.rs:479). Tokio runtime provides async snapshot sharing. Testable form: spawn_reactor() returns a RuntimeHandle; query_state() awaits and returns ClientState. Covered by UT [Invariant] C046.
contracts.postcondition: ClientState with initialized, accounts BTreeMap, calls BTreeMap, transports Vec, capabilities. AccountEntry with id, native_id, config, registration. CallEntry with id, native_id, account_id, state, media. conf_port_id NOT in CallEntry. NativeEvent processing reads client_state.calls to resolve the owning account for call-scoped events (reactor.rs:597-600) and never mutates it. Testable form: after submit_add_account + submit_make_call, query_state().accounts/calls reflect the entries; enqueued CallStateChanged CONFIRMED publishes CallConnected with the resolved account. Covered by UT [Normal] CallStateChanged, UT [Invariant] C046.
contracts.invariant: Read-only snapshots via read().await (never blocking_read()); updates via write().await (reactor only). In the current impl this means: QueryState returns a Clone on the reactor thread (never a shared mutable reference), and only the reactor loop mutates client_state (command handlers and the NativeEvent arm). Testable form: query_state() returns a snapshot independent of subsequent reactor mutations; no code path outside the reactor writes client_state. Covered by UT [Invariant] C046.

tickets.background:
- 【Goal】Wire dispatch_event, process_native_event, and extract_event_ids into the reactor loop so NativeEvents delivered by the FFI callback bridge are converted to SipEvents and routed to the correct EventBus — eliminating the three #[allow(dead_code)] markers (reactor.rs:532,570,618) and the [::STUB::] P12-7 marker at reactor.rs:531.
- 【Purpose】P3-2 specified the dual-client EventBus dispatch (C039) and the NativeEvent→SipEvent conversion pipeline, but left the three helpers as dead free functions with no call site because the FFI callback bridge that feeds NativeEvents to the reactor was not yet linked. This ticket completes the production event flow: PJSIP callbacks → enqueue_native_event → reactor loop → process_native_event → dispatch_event → SipClient EventBus.
- 【Motivation】Without the wiring, events published by the FFI callback bridge (ffi/callback.rs:63-74 enqueue_native_event to the global ArrayQueue) have no consumer: RegistrationStateChanged would never produce RegistrationSucceeded/Failed (O-001), CallStateChanged would never produce CallConnected (O-003), and the entire observable event stream of siprs would be silent. RFC §27.3 (N0038) callback-routing design depends on the reactor receiving and processing these events.
- 【Constraints】No unsafe code added to runtime/reactor.rs, command.rs, handle.rs (C038). The reactor stays a single std::thread with the MPSC channel as the sole ingestion path (C039 single-Reactor invariant). EventBus publish remains a loss-tolerant broadcast; DEFAULT_EVENT_BUS_CAPACITY=2048 (client.rs:111) preserved. FFI callback-bridge enqueue itself (P8-21) is out of scope — this ticket provides the reactor-side ingestion receiver only.
scope: - 【Change】src/runtime/command.rs — add `DispatchCommand::NativeEvent { event: NativeEvent }` variant to the internal dispatch enum (alongside the SendDtmf/AddAccount/MakeCall dedicated variants) so the reactor loop can reach the EventBus-owned process_native_event path. Update the Debug impl (command.rs:481-527) and add an `unreachable!("use enqueue_native_event instead")` arm in RuntimeHandle::submit (handle.rs:122-207). C011/C039.

- 【Change】src/runtime/handle.rs — add `RuntimeHandle::enqueue_native_event(&self, event: NativeEvent) -> Result<(), ReactorError>`: sends DispatchCommand::NativeEvent on the MPSC channel, fire-and-forget (no oneshot reply — events are observation-only per C021). Returns Err(ReactorDown) when terminated. This is the RFC §27.3 `Reactor::enqueue_native_event` ingestion receiver the FFI callback bridge (P8-21) will target.

- 【Change】src/runtime/reactor.rs loop (120-498) — add a `DispatchCommand::NativeEvent { event }` match arm that calls `process_native_event(&*backend, &client_event_buses, &default_event_bus, event, &client_state.calls)` on the reactor thread. Reads as prose: "on a native event, convert and publish it", mirroring the SendDtmf dedicated-variant pattern (reactor.rs:156-172).

- 【Change】src/runtime/reactor.rs:531 — remove the `// [::STUB::] P12-7` marker and the `#[allow(dead_code)]` on dispatch_event (532), process_native_event (570), extract_event_ids (618) once each has a live call site (dispatch_event←process_native_event, process_native_event←loop, extract_event_ids←process_native_event).

- 【Change】src/runtime/reactor.rs tests — add the reactor round-trip integration test (enqueue → loop → process → publish) and keep the existing O-001/O-003 dispatch/process tests green (reactor.rs:790-1151).
- 【Change】src/runtime/command.rs tests + handle.rs tests — add DispatchCommand::NativeEvent construct/Debug test and RuntimeHandle::enqueue_native_event send/receive + ReactorDown tests (C011).

- 【API】RuntimeHandle gains the public method `enqueue_native_event(&self, NativeEvent) -> Result<(), ReactorError>`. No RuntimeCommand variant is added (NativeEvent is not a user command). DispatchCommand gains a crate-internal variant. No SipBackend trait change; no public type signature changes elsewhere.
- 【Schema】No database/schema change. ClientState fields untouched; EventMeta/SipEvent/SipEventPayload/EventBus unchanged.
- 【Config】No new config. DEFAULT_EVENT_BUS_CAPACITY=2048 (eventbus_receiver.rs:29) and NATIVE_EVENT_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 (callback.rs:26) are already defined and unchanged.

No call site exists.
- reactor.rs:618-641 `extract_event_ids` is #[allow(dead_code)]: IncomingCall carries (acc_id, call_id); call-scoped variants (CallStateChanged/CallMediaStateChanged/DtmfDigit/IceTransportError/CallTsxStateChanged/CallRedirected/CallTransferStatus/CallReplaced) carry only call_id → (None, Some(call_id)); TransportStateChanged/NatDetected/RegistrationStateChanged → (None, None).

- The reactor already owns default_event_bus (reactor.rs:85-88, EventBus::new(DEFAULT_EVENT_BUS_CAPACITY=2048, None)) exposed on RuntimeHandle::default_event_bus() (handle.rs:92), and an empty client_event_buses HashMap (reactor.rs:92) — P11-6 laid the bus infrastructure; this ticket wires events into it.

- client.rs:111 creates a per-client EventBus(DEFAULT_EVENT_BUS_CAPACITY=2048) but nothing links it to the reactor's client_event_buses map (P9-6).

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged for rejection due to detection of implementation deficiencies, unresolved STUB markers, or other violations. It has been returned for re-implementation. A complete implementation free of all defects, STUB markers, and violations must be achieved in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

Source ticket P3-2 specified the call-state mapping where CallDirection (Outgoing/Incoming) discriminates CONNECTING into Trying vs Ringing, but left CallDirection and convert_call_state_with_previous with #[allow(dead_code)] and the reactor call-state processing (reactor.rs process_native_event) always emitting OutgoingCallTrying for CONNECTING. The FFI callback bridge (P8-21) now delivers NativeEvent::IncomingCall, so the reactor can resolve the direction from the call's origin. This work item resolves them by consuming CallDirection in the reactor path and calling convert_call_state_with_previous to discriminate Trying vs Ringing.

### Goal
Wire CallDirection into the reactor call-state processing so an inbound CONNECTING call publishes SipEventPayload::OutgoingCallRinging (instead of the current always-OutgoingCallTrying) and an outbound CONNECTING call continues to publish OutgoingCallTrying — while removing the #[allow(dead_code)] markers on CallDirection (src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs:48) and convert_call_state_with_previous (src/state/m20_callstate_mapping.rs:106) once they are consumed.

### Purpose
The CallDirection enum and convert_call_state_with_previous were introduced by P3-2 with the required Trying/Ringing discrimination logic but were never connected to production. Inbound callers currently see the wrong call state (Trying) because the reactor always applies the outgoing assumption. This change makes the published SipEventPayload reflect the true call direction, which is a prerequisite for correct UI state (ringing indicator) and for the P6 state-machine transition that updates CallState to Ringing.

### Motivation
The FFI callback bridge (P8-21) and the reactor event wiring (P8-29) now deliver NativeEvent::IncomingCall and CallStateChanged to the reactor loop, so the missing ingredient — the call's origin direction — is available. The previous make round was flagged for leaving the discrimination logic dead code (INSPECTION_FLAGGED); this round completes the wiring so inbound CONNECTING calls emit OutgoingCallRinging.

### Constraints
No new unsafe code outside ffi/ (C038). CallDirection is derived from the call's origin, never from the CallStateChanged payload. CallEntry (C046) keeps its exact field set (id, native_id, account_id, state, media; no conf_port_id) — direction is tracked in a reactor-owned call_directions map. The existing call-state conversion tests (m20_callstate_mapping.rs:156-224) and reactor process_native_event tests must stay green (the signature change is noted in scope). The on_incoming_call FFI callback already enqueues NativeEvent::IncomingCall (src/ffi/callback.rs:120-129) — no callback code change is required beyond verification.

tickets.invariants:
The CONNECTING to Trying/Ringing discrimination is deterministic given (call_id, state, direction). CallDirection is derived from the call's origin (on_incoming_call implies Incoming; make_call implies Outgoing), never from the event payload. No unsafe code is added outside ffi/ (C038). The existing call-state conversion tests (m20_callstate_mapping.rs:156-224) remain green.

- 【Normal establishment】Every CallStateChanged event whose state is pjsip_inv_state::CONNECTING is routed through convert_call_state_with_previous with a resolved CallDirection; Incoming yields OutgoingCallRinging, Outgoing yields OutgoingCallTrying. The resolution is total over (call_id, state, direction): every input maps to Some(payload) or None, never a panic.
- 【Invariant on error】When the reactor cannot resolve a direction (call absent from the call_directions map), CONNECTING falls back to convert_call_state's outgoing assumption (OutgoingCallTrying) — pre-P12-8 behavior preserved, no event dropped and no panic. A zero call_id or zero acc_id is skipped silently (existing sentinel behavior).
- 【Internal state invariant】The reactor-owned call_directions: BTreeMap<CallId, CallDirection> is populated only from NativeEvent::IncomingCall (→ Incoming) and the MakeCall command (→ Outgoing); it is never mutated from the CallStateChanged payload. CallEntry (C046) gains no new field — conf_port_id remains absent and the direction map is reactor-internal, not snapshotted.
- 【Boundary invariant】The five pjsip_inv_state constants (NULL=0, CALLING=1, CONNECTING=4, CONFIRMED=5, DISCONNECTED=6) are the only recognized values; CONNECTING is the only value that consults the direction. Non-CONNECTING states delegate to convert_call_state unchanged for both directions. #[allow(dead_code)] is removed from CallDirection and convert_call_state_with_previous only after both are consumed by the reactor path.

tickets.title: Implement PhaseTimeout handling for per-call timeout tracking during shutdown

contracts.precondition: SipClient has been initialized (initialize() completed successfully); reactor is running and accepting commands
contracts.postcondition: ShutdownSpec orchestrates idempotent shutdown: (1) atomic is_shutdown_started swap prevents re-entry, (2) all active calls are BYE/CANCELed, (3) accounts unregistered, (4) audio worker drained, (5) backend.shutdown() called, (6) reactor loop exits
contracts.invariant: Shutdown is idempotent: first call executes full sequence and returns Ok(()); second and subsequent calls return Ok(()) immediately without executing the sequence again

contracts.precondition: ShutdownSpec.is_shutdown_started() returns true after first atomic swap
contracts.postcondition: ShutdownCommandRouter.classify() correctly routes commands during shutdown: GetAccountInfo → Permit, ConfConnect/ConfDisconnect → Reject(InvalidState), all others → Reject(InvalidState). Reactor applies this routing before command execution.
contracts.invariant: GetAccountInfo is always Permitted during shutdown (read-only state check). ConfConnect and ConfDisconnect are always Rejected during shutdown (media mutation is unsafe during teardown).

contracts.precondition: ShutdownSpec constructed with a finite timeout Duration; execute_sequence invoked with non-empty call_ids or account_ids
contracts.postcondition: Each phase runs under the configured per-phase budget: a phase that exceeds it returns ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout { phase, timeout } carrying the exact configured timeout; the remaining phases still execute and execute_sequence returns the first error
contracts.invariant: The timeout field is always consumed (no #[allow(dead_code)]); the timeout path never re-enters execute_sequence; a zero timeout degrades to an immediate PhaseTimeout without panic for a phase with work

Source ticket P4-3 (Shutdown, Media Bridge, HTTP/WS Protocol & SQLite Schema) specified ShutdownSpec as an idempotent phase-ordered shutdown orchestrator with a per-phase timeout, but the timeout field is stored in the struct (shutdown_specification.rs:144-146) and never read, and ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout (lines 87-90) is never constructed. This marker was left as a stub because CancelCalls iterates calls with no deadline and no per-call timeout accounting. This work item resolves it by implementing PhaseTimeout handling for per-call timeout tracking during shutdown.

### Goal
Consume ShutdownSpec.timeout and make ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout reachable: every shutdown phase runs under the configured per-phase budget, with per-call deadline tracking in CancelCalls/UnregisterAccounts, so a stuck backend can no longer hang shutdown indefinitely.

### Purpose
P4-3 specified ShutdownSpec as an idempotent phase-ordered shutdown orchestrator with a per-phase timeout, but the timeout field was stored (shutdown_specification.rs:144-146) and never read, and PhaseTimeout (87-90) was never constructed. CancelCalls iterates calls with no deadline — an unbounded per-call wait. This ticket closes that gap so timeouts are enforced and observable.

### Motivation
The previous implementation round left the timeout as dead code (flagged by inspection for re-implementation). A stuck backend currently hangs shutdown forever; the fix makes shutdown bounded and observable, and unblocks downstream wiring (P8-33 Layer 5 tests consume shutdown) that relies on bounded shutdown.

### Constraints
Scope is limited to src/state/shutdown_specification.rs — the SipBackend trait (synchronous FFI surface, backend.rs:21) is not changed; the per-phase timeout is enforced with tokio::time::timeout plus per-call deadline checks that work with the existing synchronous backend. tokio time + test-util are already enabled (Cargo.toml:40). C044 idempotency and continue-on-error must be preserved. ShutdownCommandRouter (C045) and audio drain (C050) are out of scope.

【Edge case】The timeout is applied per phase boundary (per-call deadline plus an overall phase deadline), not as an unbounded per-call wait.
【Edge case】A zero or very small timeout does not panic — it degrades to an immediate PhaseTimeout for slow backends.

- [Implementation steps] (1) Remove #[allow(dead_code)] and the P12-9 STUB marker on timeout (lines 144-146); (2) add ShutdownSpec::ensure_within_phase_deadline helper; (3) in execute_sequence, wrap each execute_phase call in tokio::time::timeout(self.timeout, ...), mapping Elapsed → PhaseTimeout; (4) in execute_phase, compute phase_deadline and add per-call deadline checks + tokio::task::yield_now().await in CancelCalls/UnregisterAccounts; (5) add Clone/PartialEq/Eq derives to ShutdownError; (6) write the deterministic #[tokio::test] cases (pause/advance/spawn) — RED first, confirm they fail before implementation; (7) cargo fmt + make test.

- [Caveats] The per-call deadline cannot preempt an already-blocking synchronous FFI call (e.g., a PJSUA hangup that blocks on a mutex); it bounds the phase at the per-call boundary. Preempting a truly-blocking sync FFI requires moving the backend off the async executor — documented as future work.

4. src/runtime/reactor.rs: Shutdown dispatch (458-462) calls backend.shutdown() directly and sets is_terminated; it does NOT yet call execute_sequence — the wiring gap is a future ticket (P8-33). Deterministic timeout tests use tokio::time::pause() + tokio::time::advance(Duration) (e.g., 1640-1673), proving the mock-clock pattern is established.

5. Cargo.toml:40: tokio = { features = ["sync", "rt", "rt-multi-thread", "time", "macros", "net", "test-util"] } — tokio::time::timeout, tokio::time::Instant, tokio::time::pause()/advance() are all available with no new dependencies.

6. src/config/client_config_spec.rs: TimeoutConfig.shutdown_timeout: Duration (111) defaults to 15s (124) — the eventual source of the ShutdownSpec timeout when wired (future).

7. src/client.rs:493 already wraps client.shutdown() in tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), ...) — precedent for timeout-bounding shutdown at the client boundary.

8. src/error/m20_shutdown_routing.rs: ShutdownCommandRouter::classify (C045) exists with tests (143-197) — the router contract is already implemented; P12-9 references it for coverage, not implementation.

Design conclusion: enforce the per-phase timeout in execute_sequence with tokio::time::timeout(self.timeout, execute_phase(...)), map Elapsed → PhaseTimeout, and add per-call deadline checks (tokio::time::Instant) with yield_now checkpoints in CancelCalls/UnregisterAccounts so the timeout is observable at per-call granularity and deterministically testable with the mock clock.
tickets.boyScoutPlan:
Translatability improvements for code touched by this ticket:

1. Remove the #[allow(dead_code)] and the dead timeout-field comment (lines 144-146) — dead annotations are lies; after this ticket the field is read.
2. Extract the per-call deadline check into a private method ensure_within_phase_deadline(phase, deadline) so execute_phase reads as prose: 'for each call, ensure within deadline, yield, hang up'.
3. Extract the timeout-mapping in execute_sequence into a small helper run_phase_with_timeout(phase, ...) -> Result<(), ShutdownError> so the phase loop reads as 'for each phase, run it under the timeout' — the match on tokio::time::error::Elapsed is contained in one named place.
4. Add Clone/PartialEq/Eq to ShutdownError so tests assert on error equality instead of string matching — the codebase already derives these on ReactorError (command.rs:7).
5. Per-project style: keep function names as verb phrases (ensure_within_phase_deadline, run_phase_with_timeout), keep the existing phase.label() human-readable names, and avoid magic numbers in tests (use Duration::from_millis constants or named consts).

changes.after: ShutdownSpec.timeout is consumed by run_phase_with_timeout (tokio::time::timeout per phase) and per-call deadline checks (ensure_within_phase_deadline) in execute_phase; ShutdownError::PhaseTimeout is constructed and returned; CancelCalls/UnregisterAccounts/InvokeDestroy never start backend work past the phase deadline

tickets.title: Implement Layer 5 integration tests with MockBackend (P1-3) for isolated testing, Axum TestResponse for routes, and WS test helpers for event handlers

contracts.precondition: A test router is built with a shared AppState backed by siprs::runtime::backend::MockBackend; the router registers the 18 REST + 2 WS paths from siprs::api::http_ws_protocol (PATH_AUTH_TOKEN … PATH_WS_AUDIO). The tests run in the siprs-server crate context, PJSIP-free.
contracts.postcondition: HTTP/WS protocol types round-trip: WsTextFrame {type:"event", seq, payload} serializes/deserializes as JSON text; AudioFrameHeader is a 30-byte big-endian to_bytes()/from_bytes() round-trip; WsBinaryFrame::encode()/decode() round-trips header+PCM and returns None on <30-byte input; SequenceGenerator yields monotonically increasing u64. Axum TestResponse drives each exercised REST route to the expected status + JSON shape; WS helpers deliver text and binary frames.
contracts.invariant: Event-audio correlation via sequence numbers: WsTextFrame.seq and AudioFrameHeader.sequence_number are drawn from the same SequenceGenerator domain, so a seq=N event frame correlates with an audio frame whose header.sequence_number == N. (RFC §54.5 names these SipEvent.meta.seq and AudioChunkPair.first_seq/last_seq; the implemented surface exposes them as WsTextFrame.seq / AudioFrameHeader.sequence_number — EventMeta.event_id is the in-client event counter and AudioChunkPair carries timestamp-paired chunks without per-chunk seq.)

contracts.precondition: The HTTP/WS API protocol (N0062) defines the endpoints and message formats; the auth mode is selectable — LocalhostOnly is the default when no JWT secret is configured, JWT mode when a secret is set. The test harness builds the router with the chosen mode.
contracts.postcondition: Auth-protected routes reject requests without a valid Bearer token in JWT mode; /api/v1/auth/token issues a JWT for valid SIP credentials (validated against MockBackend.accounts) and returns 401 for invalid credentials; in LocalhostOnly mode localhost requests pass without a token.
contracts.invariant: Default auth mode is LocalhostOnly: with no JWT secret configured, 127.0.0.1 requests are accepted without a token and non-localhost (e.g. 10.0.0.1) requests are rejected; with a JWT secret configured, non-localhost requests require a valid Bearer token.

tickets.background:
- 【Goal】Replace the compile-time-only test_apilayer5.rs stub with a real Layer 5 integration test suite that drives the HTTP/WS API surface through an Axum TestResponse router backed by MockBackend, plus WebSocket test helpers for the control+audio and audio-only event streams — running in the siprs-server crate without any live PJSIP dependency.
- 【Purpose】P4-3 (N0062/N0063/N0064) specified the HTTP/WS protocol, JWT auth model, and SQLite schema but deferred the Layer 5 integration tests to the siprs-server crate context. The siprs-side test_apilayer5.rs carries only test_crate_license (C061). This ticket closes that gap so the Layer 5 surface (route shapes, auth-mode behavior, JSON/binary frame formats, event-audio seq correlation) has deterministic, CI-runnable regression coverage.
- 【Motivation】The Layer 5 surface is currently untested: any regression in path constants, frame serialization, seq correlation, or auth gating would ship silently. Because the production handlers are P4-3 stubs, the tests must be self-contained around MockBackend (P1-3, N0053) — the isolation RFC §57 prescribes. Re-implementation round: prior inspection flagged this ticket for the unimplemented stub at test_apilayer5.rs:25.
- 【Constraints】Test-only scope: no changes to P4-3-owned protocol endpoint, JWT middleware, or SQLite schema implementations. Tests run in the siprs-server crate (axum 0.7, tokio full, tokio-tungstenite 0.21, jsonwebtoken 9); siprs-server dev-dependencies (tower, http-body-util, futures) must be added to drive TestResponse/WS. All tests must be PJSIP-free and CI-runnable.
scope: - 【Change】src/tests/test_apilayer5.rs:25 — action: replace stub. Replace the `// [::STUB::] P12-10:` marker with real Layer 5 test modules: keep test_crate_license (C061); add route-path mirror assertions over the 18 REST + 2 WS PATH_* constants; add protocol-type unit tests (WsTextFrame round-trip, AudioFrameHeader 30-byte round-trip, WsBinaryFrame encode/decode, SequenceGenerator monotonicity).
- 【Change】src/tests/mod.rs — action: verify (already wired). `pub mod test_apilayer5;` already exists; update the module doc comment to P12-10 provenance and confirm no duplicate wiring.
- 【Change】siprs-server/Cargo.toml — action: add dev-dependencies tower (ServiceExt::oneshot), http-body-util (BodyExt::collect), futures (WS stream split) for TestResponse/WS driving.

- 【Change】siprs-server/tests/common/mod.rs (new) — action: add. Shared TestApp harness: build_test_app() constructs MockBackend, wraps it in an AppState, registers PATH_* routes with thin MockBackend-backed test handlers (health, auth token, accounts list/create, ws control+audio, ws audio-only), and exposes get/post/ws helpers returning axum::response::Response / TestResponse.
- 【Change】siprs-server/tests/api/health_test.rs — action: implement. GET /api/v1/health → 200, JSON body {"status":"ok"} via TestApp (C063).

- 【Change】siprs-server/tests/api/auth_test.rs — action: implement. /api/v1/auth/token: valid SIP credentials (pre-seeded MockBackend.accounts) → 200 JWT; invalid → 401; protected route without Bearer → 401 in JWT mode (C064).

- 【Change】siprs-server/tests/api/accounts_test.rs — action: implement. POST /api/v1/accounts (add via MockBackend.add_account) and GET /api/v1/accounts (list from MockBackend.accounts) round-trip through TestResponse (C063/C064).

- 【Change】siprs-server/tests/ws/event_stream_test.rs — action: implement. WS test helpers connect_ws_control() (text frames type/seq/payload) and connect_ws_audio() (binary AudioFrameHeader+PCM); assert the ClientInitialized event frame and event-audio seq correlation (C063 invariant).

- 【Before → After】test_apilayer5.rs: only test_crate_license (C061) → test_crate_license + protocol-type + route-mirror unit tests; siprs-server tests: stub comments → green TestResponse/WS integration tests. No production API/signature change.
- 【API contract change】None — the tests consume the already-exported siprs::api::http_ws_protocol types and PATH constants; no siprs production signature is altered.
- 【Data schema change】None — SQLite schema (C065) is explicitly out of scope (P4-3).
- 【Config/env change】None — the auth-mode switch is exercised via the TestApp configuration, not new environment variables.
- 【Dependency added】siprs-server dev-deps: tower ^0.4, http-body-util ^0.1, futures ^0.3 (pinned to axum 0.7 compatibility).

- 【Non-change】HTTP/WS protocol endpoint implementation (P4-3/C063), JWT middleware (P4-3/C064), SQLite schema/entities (P4-3/C065), DatabasePool.load_accounts (P5-1, TS-001) — separate delivery tickets; P12-10 only adds tests that consume the already-exported protocol types.

- 【Impact】siprs crate protocol types (http_ws_protocol.rs) — consumed, not modified; regression risk limited to test compilation. siprs-server crate — tests + dev-deps only. Impact nature: test coverage / CI; no production API surface or data-format change.
- 【Impact response】No corresponding production change required; when P4-3 lands, the TestApp may switch from test handlers to siprs_server::routes::build_router (tracked in notes-open).
testUnit: UT: [C063-Pre] Route-path mirror — assert the 18 REST PATH_* constants (PATH_AUTH_TOKEN … PATH_SHUTDOWN) plus PATH_WS and PATH_WS_AUDIO exist in siprs::api::http_ws_protocol and equal the expected /api/v1/... strings; assert the siprs-server tests/api/{health,auth,accounts}_test.rs and tests/ws/event_stream_test.rs layout matches the exercised route set.

UT: [C063-Post] WsTextFrame JSON round-trip — construct WsTextFrame { msg_type:"event", seq:42, payload:json!({"kind":"ClientInitialized"}) }; serde_json::to_string/from_str preserves msg_type/seq/payload and serializes msg_type under the JSON key "type".

UT: [C063-Post] AudioFrameHeader 30-byte wire round-trip — build AudioFrameHeader { sequence_number:1, timestamp_ms:1000, frame_ms:20, sample_rate:48000, channels:1, bits_per_sample:16, call_id:7, reserved:[0;4] }; to_bytes() -> [u8;30]; from_bytes() -> equal header; WsBinaryFrame::encode/decode round-trips header+data.
UT: [C063-Post] WsBinaryFrame decode boundary — decode() on a byte slice shorter than 30 returns None (no panic); decode on 30-byte header + PCM returns Some with the correct header and data.

UT: [C063-Inv] SequenceGenerator monotonicity & reservation — new() starts at 1; next() returns 1,2,3 strictly increasing; with_start(100) issues 100 then 101; reserve(5) returns a start whose range [start,start+5) is disjoint from a subsequent next(); current() reflects the last issued value; wrap from u64::MAX to 0 preserves uniqueness.

UT: [C063-Inv] Event-audio seq correlation — one SequenceGenerator feeds both a WsTextFrame.seq and an AudioFrameHeader.sequence_number; assert the audio header seq is drawn from the same domain (audio_seq > event_seq when the audio chunk follows the event) and that a seq=N event frame pairs with an audio frame whose header.sequence_number == N.
UT: [C064-Pre] Auth-mode selection — a ServerConfig with jwt_secret:None yields AuthMode::LocalhostOnly; with a secret it yields AuthMode::Jwt (mode derived from the configured secret).

UT: [C064-Post] Token issuance & validation — issue_token for valid SIP credentials present in MockBackend.accounts returns a JWT; a JwtValidator built with the same secret validates it; invalid/unknown credentials are rejected.

UT: [C064-Inv] LocalhostOnly default — validate_request("127.0.0.1", None, LocalhostOnly) is Ok; validate_request("10.0.0.1", None, LocalhostOnly) is Err; with JWT mode a valid Bearer token is required for non-localhost requests.
testIntegration: IT: [health_test.rs] GET /api/v1/health via Axum TestResponse — build TestApp(MockBackend); GET PATH_HEALTH returns 200 and JSON body {"status":"ok"}; no auth required (C063).

IT: [accounts_test.rs] POST then GET /api/v1/accounts — add_account through MockBackend (incrementing id, AccountEntry persisted in MockBackend.accounts); list_accounts returns the added account; round-trip through the Axum router via TestResponse with a valid Bearer token in JWT mode (C063/C064).

IT: [auth_test.rs] /api/v1/auth/token — valid SIP credentials pre-seeded in MockBackend.accounts issue a JWT (200); invalid credentials return 401; a protected route without an Authorization header returns 401 in JWT mode (C064).

IT: [event_stream_test.rs] WS control+audio and audio-only — connect ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/v1/ws (control+audio) and receive a text frame {type:"event",seq,payload:{kind:"ClientInitialized"}} with seq>0; connect /api/v1/ws/audio (audio-only) and receive a binary frame whose AudioFrameHeader.sequence_number correlates with the event seq (C063 invariant).
testExceptions: Full 18-REST + 2-WS route conformance — (1) Why it is not testable: siprs-server production route handlers (routes.rs, ws.rs, auth.rs, db.rs) are P4-3 STUBs not yet delivered; P12-10 is test-only and builds a TestApp with thin MockBackend-backed test handlers, so endpoints whose production handlers are absent cannot be exercised end-to-end. It is impossible to test routes that do not exist yet. (2) This is not a design defect and not an architectural defect: the protocol types (PATH constants, WsTextFrame, AudioFrameHeader, WsBinaryFrame, SequenceGenerator) are fully unit-tested in the siprs crate, and the gap closes automatically when P4-3 ships build_router — the TestApp then switches to siprs_server::routes::build_router. — Alternative verification: siprs-crate unit tests cover all protocol types; the TestApp route set covers the exercised subset (health, token, accounts, ws, ws/audio).

Live TLS / JWT-secret production handshake — (1) Why it is not testable: it requires a configured secret and a real network listener; the auth-mode switch (LocalhostOnly default vs JWT) is asserted at the predicate level (validate_request against 127.0.0.1 vs 10.0.0.1) rather than over a real TLS handshake. It is impossible to test a production handshake without a production certificate/secret setup. (2) This is not a design defect and not an architectural defect: it is a configuration/environment boundary, and the auth behavior is deterministic and asserted directly via the mode predicate and TestResponse 401 checks. — Alternative verification: auth-mode predicate tests in testUnit plus TestApp-level 401 assertions in auth_test.rs.

Live PJSIP stack end-to-end call flow — (1) Why it is not testable: Layer 5 is defined PJSIP-free (MockBackend only) by RFC §57; a live SIP call is Layer 3/4 scope (Docker Asterisk, real PBX interop), which would make the suite non-CI-runnable and contradict the isolation goal. It is impossible to test a live PJSIP call in a PJSIP-free Layer 5 suite. (2) This is not a design defect and not an architectural defect: the PJSIP-free isolation is the RFC-mandated design; the live-stack behavior is intentionally covered by the Layer 3/4 suites instead. — Alternative verification: Layer 3 (Docker SIP) and Layer 4 (interop) suites cover the live stack; this suite stays deterministic and CI-runnable.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Each REST route in siprs-server/tests/api/ is exercised through Axum TestResponse against a TestApp built on MockBackend: GET /api/v1/health → 200 {"status":"ok"}; POST/GET /api/v1/accounts round-trip; POST /api/v1/auth/token issues a JWT for valid SIP credentials (C063/C064).

【Happy path】WS test helpers open control+audio (/api/v1/ws) and audio-only (/api/v1/ws/audio) connections and assert the JSON text frame format {type:"event",seq,payload} per C063, receiving a ClientInitialized event with seq > 0.
【Happy path】All Layer 5 tests run in the siprs-server crate context without a live PJSIP stack (MockBackend only); the siprs-side test_apilayer5.rs suite passes as unit tests.
【Error case】Auth-protected routes without a Bearer token are rejected with 401 in JWT mode; invalid SIP credentials at /api/v1/auth/token return 401 (C064).
【Error case】WsBinaryFrame::decode on a <30-byte payload returns None (no panic); a truncated frame is rejected deterministically.
【Edge case】Event-audio correlation: a seq=N event frame correlates with an audio frame whose AudioFrameHeader.sequence_number == N, both drawn from one SequenceGenerator (C063 invariant).
【Edge case】The stub marker at test_apilayer5.rs:25 is removed only when the real test modules replace it and the full suite (make test) passes green.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】All Layer 5 tests construct MockBackend (siprs::runtime::backend) and build the Axum router with a shared AppState; no live PJSIP stack is required (RFC §57 Layer 5 is PJSIP-free). The protocol types round-trip: WsTextFrame {type,seq,payload} and the 30-byte AudioFrameHeader wire format.
- 【Invariant on error】Auth failures never leak credentials: an invalid/missing Bearer token yields 401 (JWT mode) without exposing internal errors; invalid SIP credentials at /api/v1/auth/token yield 401, never a 200. WsBinaryFrame::decode on a <30-byte payload returns None rather than panicking.
- 【Internal state invariant】MockBackend.accounts is the single source of truth for account list/create; sequence numbers come from one SequenceGenerator so WsTextFrame.seq and AudioFrameHeader.sequence_number never collide across the event/audio domains within a test session.
- 【Boundary invariant】SequenceGenerator.next() never decreases within a session (wrap from u64::MAX to 0 preserves uniqueness); the audio header wire size is exactly 30 bytes (RFC §54.4 notes 24, but the implementation — http_ws_protocol.rs:62-63 — corrects it to 30).

tickets.title: Add cpal as an optional dependency behind the cpal-input feature and implement device-backed capture returning Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError> with an integration test

contracts.precondition: cpal is an optional dependency reachable only through the `cpal-input` feature (default build graph contains no cpal). The RFC §40 signature exists behind #[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")]: `pub async fn open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>`. The input `format` is a validated AudioFormat (AudioFormat::new succeeded; sample_rate ∈ {Hz8000, Hz16000, Hz24000, Hz48000}, bit_depth ∈ {I16, F32}, channel_layout ∈ {Mono, StereoInOut}, frame_ms ∈ {10, 20, 40, 60}).
contracts.postcondition: When a default input device exists and its native sample format is convertible to the i16 pipeline contract, open_default_microphone_source returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) whose next_chunk fills the caller's &mut [i16] buffer with captured PCM and returns the written sample count. Device-open, format-mismatch, build-stream, and play failures surface as Err(SipError) (SipErrorKind::NativeError for device/stream errors; SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats) — never a panic.
contracts.invariant: The returned source is AsyncAudioSource + Send and can be stored as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> in AudioMixer (ErasedAudioSource auto-derived via blanket impl). Sample conversion clamps into the valid i16 range (no wraparound). With `cpal-input` disabled, the function, the CpalMicrophoneSource type, and the cpal crate are compiled out of the build.

contracts.precondition: Audio subscribe uses sources — AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>; AsyncAudioSource trait is defined as #[async_trait::async_trait] pub trait AsyncAudioSource: Send { async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize; }.
contracts.postcondition: ErasedAudioSource blanket impl auto-derived for all T: AsyncAudioSource + Send; SyncAudioSource trait and SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> provided for synchronous sources; any new concrete source (e.g. CpalMicrophoneSource) implementing AsyncAudioSource + Send automatically gains ErasedAudioSource.
contracts.invariant: ErasedAudioSource auto-derived for every AsyncAudioSource implementor — blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> ErasedAudioSource for T must compile. SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send. CpalMicrophoneSource must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send so it is usable as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed (O-001, major). This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Resolve O-001 and finalize the real cpal device-backed microphone source: keep `open_default_microphone_source` (src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:173-179) returning `Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` backed by the platform default microphone behind the `cpal-input` feature, and close the ABC gap by unit-testing every error path (map_default_config_error / map_supported_configs_error / map_build_stream_error / map_play_error) and the unsupported-sample-format arm of build_input_stream, with the feature-gated integration test retained.

### Purpose
The `cpal-input` feature has been wired since P8-7 (Cargo.toml: `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]`), and the microphone source is the only RFC-required audio source that is device-backed. Downstream consumers (AudioMixer via P5-2, the audio_tap example via P8-6, AI TTS source insertion) rely on opening the default microphone as an AsyncAudioSource. The ABC inspection confirmed the happy-path machinery is complete but the error-contract (never-panic / typed-Err) is not enforced by any test — O-001 must be closed so the contract is provable.

### Motivation
P8-4 delivered the AsyncAudioSource adapter machinery under a no-new-dependencies constraint; P8-7 landed the cpal dependency and real capture, resolving the `[::STUB::] P8-7` marker. What remains is the ABC-mandated O-001 closure: cpal 0.18.1 exposes publicly constructible `cpal::Error` and `SupportedStreamConfig`, so the error paths are unit-testable without a device — the omission is a test-coverage defect, not an architectural limit. This ticket removes that defect and re-proves C051/C033.

### Constraints
- cpal must be an optional dependency reachable only via `cpal-input`; default builds must not pull the cpal crate (feature-additive invariant). Cargo.toml:40 already declares `check-cfg = ['cfg(feature, values("cpal-input"))']`.
- MSRV is 1.95; pin a cpal version whose API is stable and documented — cpal 0.18.1 (Cargo.lock) requires an explicit `stream.play()` after build and pins the sample rate/config explicitly.
- The public `open_default_microphone_source` signature must not change (C051 precondition); the returned source must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send.
- No panics on device failure — all errors map to SipError (NativeError for device/stream, AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats). The O-001 unit tests must make a regression detectable.
- CI without audio hardware must not run the device integration test by default (#[ignore] + SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO=1 gate).

- [What specifically changes] Add `cpal = { version = "0.18", optional = true }` to [dependencies]; change `cpal-input = []` to `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]`; update the `[::STUB::] P1-3 (N0050)` comment that says 'Full implementation requires the cpal crate (P8-4)'. Current Cargo.toml already declares `check-cfg = ['cfg(feature, values("cpal-input"))']`.
- [Before → After] Before: `cpal-input = []` (empty feature, no cpal). After: `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]` (feature pulls cpal; default build unchanged).
- [File/module path] src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — open_default_microphone_source + CpalMicrophoneSource + error-mapping helpers + test module

- [Action] MODIFY (resolve O-001) — extract the sample-format-match logic from `build_input_stream` (lines 419-474) into a pure helper `select_sample_format_handler(cpal::SampleFormat, SampleQueue) -> Result<SampleFormatHandler, SipError>` so the `other =>` AudioFormatUnsupported arm (lines 466-471) becomes unit-testable without a cpal::Device; add the 5 O-001 unit tests (4 map_*_error helpers + select_sample_format_handler accept/reject) to the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block.

After: the format decision is a pure function; every non-convertible format returns Err(SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported) and is asserted in tests.

- [API contract change] None breaking — the public RFC §40 signature and C051 pre/post conditions are unchanged; behavior changes from always-Err placeholder (P8-4) to real capture (P8-7 already landed) and the O-001 tests now pin the typed-Err postcondition.

- **Out of scope:**
- [Excluded item] AudioMixer auto-wiring of the microphone and real PJSIP media conf-port bridging (P3-2 N0050)

- [Why excluded] Mixer integration already accepts any AsyncAudioSource (P5-2); conf-port wiring is a separate PJSIP-media ticket; this ticket resolves only the device-source adapter, its error paths, and the feature gate.
- [Excluded item] Sample-rate resampling inside the adapter

- [Why excluded] Converting the device's native rate to an arbitrary requested rate belongs to model::audio_resampler; this adapter uses the device's default config when the requested format is not natively supported.
- **Affected areas:**
- [Affected component] src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs (test module + build_input_stream refactor), Cargo.toml, tests/verify_spec_p8_7.rs, Cargo.lock
- [Nature of impact] Additive optional dependency; default builds pull no cpal crate; the `cpal-input` feature becomes real (was empty); the O-001 refactor is internal and behavior-preserving.
- [Corresponding change needed] Y — CI jobs that enable `cpal-input` need audio device access or must rely on the #[ignore] device test; `make test` (default) runs the feature-off build.

testExceptions: Item: Asserting specific PCM sample values from the real microphone is not testable in CI because captured samples depend on physical microphone input and OS audio routing — a non-deterministic external dependency, not a code defect. Reason: deterministic logic (sample conversion, queue drain, FIFO order, error mapping) is extracted into pure functions (convert_f32_sample_to_i16, convert_u16_sample_to_i16, SampleQueue, map_*_error, select_sample_format_handler) and covered by unit tests; the integration test asserts only that >= 1 frame is produced. This is not a case of 'deterministic yet fundamentally untestable' (an architectural defect): the deterministic core is fully extracted and unit-tested. Alternative verification: unit tests on the pure helpers; #[ignore] device test.

Item: Cross-platform device enumeration differences cannot test deterministically because cpal device availability, names, and default-device selection differ per OS (CoreAudio, ALSA, WASAPI) and change with user audio settings — an external, non-deterministic environment. Reason: the device layer is a thin boundary and all deterministic logic (select_input_config preference, sample-format match, error mapping, queue handoff) is covered by synthetic SampleQueue / pure-helper unit tests. This is not an architectural defect: the nondeterminism lives only at the device boundary, not in the crate's own logic. Alternative verification: error-mapping functions are unit-tested; the device integration test is #[ignore] where no default device exists.

Item: Forcing the 'no default input device' condition is impossible to test inside a unit test because cpal exposes no mock seam for Host/Device and device presence is environment-dependent — an external dependency, not a code defect. Reason: the device-open logic is thin and every non-environmental decision (sample-format match, error mapping, queue handoff) is extracted into unit-testable functions; cpal::Error and SupportedStreamConfig are publicly constructible so the error paths are exercised without a device. This is not a design defect: the only untestable residue is the OS-level device probe itself, whose absence path is covered by the #[ignore] no-device integration test. Alternative verification: the #[ignore] no-device integration test on a host without an audio backend.
acceptanceCriteria: - 【Happy path】With `--features cpal-input`, open_default_microphone_source(format) opens the platform default input device and returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>) whose next_chunk fills an i16 buffer with captured PCM (>= 1 sample on a real device, verified by the #[ignore] integration test). The returned source is AsyncAudioSource + Send and can be stored as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> in AudioMixer (compile-time check). The O-001 unit tests pass: the 4 map_*_error helpers return NativeError with their prefixes for constructible cpal::Error values, and select_sample_format_handler accepts {I16,F32,U16} and rejects the other 12 SampleFormat variants with AudioFormatUnsupported.

- 【Error case】When no default input device exists, open_default_microphone_source returns Err(SipError) with a clear message (SipErrorKind::NativeError) instead of panicking (C051-Post typed-Err). When the requested AudioFormat cannot be matched by the device (non-convertible sample format), the function returns Err(SipError) describing the format mismatch (SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported) — asserted by the select_sample_format_handler unit tests, so a regression to panic!() or a wrong SipErrorKind fails CI.

- 【Edge case】With the feature disabled (default), the function and CpalMicrophoneSource are compiled out and the crate builds without cpal — no device capture is attempted and `cargo tree -e normal` shows no cpal (feature-additive invariant). Sample conversion clamps at i16 boundaries; an empty queue / zero-length buffer returns 0 without panicking. A 65536-sample buffer (AudioMixer boundary) drains without overflow.

tickets.notes:
- 【Implementation steps】(1) TDD Red — add the 5 O-001 unit tests to the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block of src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs: four `map_*_error` tests constructing `cpal::Error::with_message(ErrorKind, "...")` and asserting `SipErrorKind::NativeError` + prefix, and two `select_sample_format_handler` tests (accept {I16,F32,U16} / reject the other 12 `SampleFormat` variants with `AudioFormatUnsupported`). These fail Red because the pure helper does not exist yet. (2) Green — extract `select_sample_format_handler(cpal::SampleFormat, SampleQueue) -> Result<SampleFormatHandler, SipError>` from `build_input_stream` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:419-474), keeping build behavior identical; `cargo test --features cpal-input` must pass. (3) Verify the default feature-off build: `make test` and `cargo tree -e normal` (no cpal). (4) On a host with a mic, run the device test: `cargo test --features cpal-input --test verify_spec_p8_7 -- --ignored` with `SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO=1`.
- 【Risks】cpal API drift (0.15/0.16/0.18 differ — v0.18 requires explicit `stream.play()` and pins sample rate/config); ALSA/WASAPI/CoreAudio device availability differs; a real-device test cannot run in CI without audio hardware — it must be #[ignore] and must never gate `make test`.
- 【Caveats】The captured stream runs on a cpal callback thread; the sample queue must be Send+Sync (Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<i16>>>) and bounded to avoid unbounded growth when next_chunk is slower than the device. tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal condition】With `cpal-input` enabled and a default input device present, open_default_microphone_source returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) and next_chunk fills the i16 buffer with device PCM. The cpal crate compiles only under the feature (Cargo.toml: cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]). select_input_config prefers a supported config matching the requested channel count and sample rate and falls back to the device default otherwise (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:387-413).
- 【Invariant on error】Device-open, default-config, build-stream, and play failures never panic — they surface as Err(SipError). Sample formats outside the convertible set {I16, F32, U16} map to SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported via select_sample_format_handler; other device errors map to SipErrorKind::NativeError via the map_*_error helpers. The 5 O-001 unit tests pin these kind mappings so a violation (panic or wrong kind) fails CI.
- 【Internal state invariant】CpalMicrophoneSource holds an Option<cpal::Stream> plus an Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<i16>>> sample queue; the queue grows only from the cpal callback thread (push_i16) and shrinks only via next_chunk (drain_to); next_chunk returns 0 when the queue is empty (end-of-stream). A poisoned mutex is recovered via into_inner() so the callback never unwinds across the audio boundary.
- 【Boundary invariant】Sample conversion is bijective at the extremes and clamped in between: u16::MAX↔i16::MAX, 0↔i16::MIN, 0x8000↔0 (convert_u16_sample_to_i16, DC-offset preserved); f32 in [-1.0, 1.0] maps linearly via F32_TO_I16_SCALE=32768.0 with clamping (never wraps). A zero-length buffer returns 0 without panicking; a 65536-sample buffer (AudioMixer boundary) drains without overflow.

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Complete the RFC §40 device-backed microphone source (`open_default_microphone_source`, src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:173-179) behind the `cpal-input` feature and close the sole remaining ABC violation (O-001): add an automated test that verifies the feature-additive invariant — the default build graph resolves no cpal crate while `--features cpal-input` pulls `cpal v0.18.1`. The device-capture implementation itself already landed in P8-7 (CpalMicrophoneSource / SampleQueue / sample conversion) and its error paths in P13-1; the re-make must prove every C051/C033 contract with failing-test enforcement.

### Purpose
The microphone source is the only RFC-required audio source that must be device-backed; downstream consumers (AudioMixer via P5-2, the audio_tap example via P8-6, AI TTS source insertion) open the default microphone as an AsyncAudioSource. The `cpal-input` feature gate keeps the default crate light, and the O-001 build-graph test guarantees that gate is never silently broken (e.g., by dropping `optional = true` from Cargo.toml).

### Motivation
P8-4 delivered the AsyncAudioSource adapter machinery under a no-new-dependencies constraint; P8-7 wired cpal 0.18 behind `cpal-input` and implemented the source; P13-1 closed the error-path O-001. The ABC inspection found the remaining O-001: the feature-off build graph had no automated assertion — the `#![cfg(feature = "cpal-input")]` gate on tests/verify_spec_p8_7.rs only proves the *code* is compiled out, not that the *dependency graph* excludes cpal. Removing `optional = true` from Cargo.toml:73 would silently pull cpal into the default build with zero failing tests. This ticket adds that failing-test enforcement.

### Constraints
- cpal must stay an optional dependency reachable only via `cpal-input` (C051-Pre); default builds must resolve no cpal crate. Cargo.toml:33 already declares `check-cfg = ['cfg(feature, values("cpal-input", "pjsua-native"))']`.

- No panics on device failure — all errors map to SipError (NativeError for device/stream, AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats).
- CI without audio hardware must not run the device integration test by default (#[ignore] + SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO gate); the O-001 build-graph test must run in the default feature-off build (no audio hardware required).

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal condition】With `cpal-input` enabled and a default input device present, open_default_microphone_source returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) whose next_chunk fills the i16 buffer with device PCM. The cpal crate compiles only under the feature (Cargo.toml:26 `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]`; Cargo.toml:73 `cpal = { version = "0.18", optional = true }`); the default build graph resolves no cpal package — enforced by tests/verify_feature_additive_build.rs running `cargo tree -e normal` (O-001 closure).
- 【Invariant on error】Device-open, default-config, build-stream, and play failures never panic — they surface as Err(SipError) (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:264-300 error-mapping helpers). Sample formats outside the convertible set {I16, F32, U16} map to SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:433-446); other device errors map to SipErrorKind::NativeError. A poisoned queue mutex is recovered via into_inner() so the cpal callback never unwinds across the audio boundary.
- 【Internal state invariant】CpalMicrophoneSource holds an Option<cpal::Stream> plus a shared SampleQueue (Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<i16>>>); the queue grows only from the cpal callback thread (push_i16) and shrinks only via next_chunk (drain_to); next_chunk returns 0 when the queue is empty (end-of-stream). The stream is None only in the #[cfg(test)] from_queue constructor.
- 【Boundary invariant】Sample conversion is bijective at the extremes and clamped in between: u16::MAX↔i16::MAX, 0↔i16::MIN, 0x8000↔0; f32 in [-1.0, 1.0] maps linearly with clamping (named constants F32_TO_I16_SCALE=32768.0, U16_DC_OFFSET=0x8000). A zero-length buffer returns 0 without panicking; a 65536-sample buffer (AudioMixer boundary) drains without overflow.

The O-001 build-graph test adds no logging — it asserts and returns.
- 【Metrics】No new counters in this ticket; the existing metrics feature is untouched. The capture path is device-driven and not a hot counter; frames-per-second metrics for the audio pipeline are deferred to the audio_pipeline tickets.
- 【Error tracking】Every device failure path maps to a distinct, greppable SipError message prefix: no_default_input_device / default_input_config_failed / supported_input_configs_failed / unsupported_sample_format / build_stream_failed / play_failed (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:324-328, 264-293, 441-444). All errors use SipErrorKind::NativeError (device/stream) or SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported (sample format) and are returned — never swallowed or converted to a panic. The O-001 test surfaces its own failures as assertion failures with the cargo tree output embedded in the message.
- 【Health check】The source exposes no explicit health method; liveness is inferred from next_chunk returning > 0 samples. A failing stream surfaces via the cpal error callback (input_stream_error, asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:298-300), which logs at tracing::error without unwinding across the callback boundary.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed. This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Resolve the five `[::STUB::] P9-1` markers by turning the example binaries (account_register, audio_tap, client_init, make_call, tts_source) from documentation stubs into runnable reference clients that parse CLI args and drive the real SipClient public API per RFC §41, backed by Layer 5 integration tests.

### Purpose
The examples are the crate's Layer 5 API documentation surface (N0052/N0065) — end users and the zasso ecosystem need runnable reference binaries showing how to initialize a client, register an account, place a call, tap audio, and inject a TTS source. Without them, the public API has no executable usage demonstration and the ABC inspection gaps (documented-but-unrunnable flows) cannot close.

### Motivation
Source ticket P1-3 deferred the example bodies because the CLI/PJSIP runtime was not yet available. That deferral produced INSPECTION_FLAGGED stubs. The required public types (SipClient, ClientConfig, AccountConfig, SipAccountHandle, OutgoingCallRequest, AsyncAudioSource) and the runtime command path (RuntimeHandle) now exist, so the examples can be made real. This is the final re-implementation round demanded by the inspection flag.

### Constraints
Examples consume the public API only (no internal-module reach-around beyond the documented RuntimeHandle command path). The `spec-examples` required-features gate stays for audio_tap until P9-2 provides subscribe_audio/AudioTapHandle. No new runtime dependencies for the examples (shared CLI parser uses std::env::args; clap stays behind the `cli` feature for the server binary). All five example main functions return Result and never panic (C056). `make test` must stay green.

### Goal
Resolve the ABC-inspection omission O-001 in the already-implemented example binaries: add a source-inspection test (examples_have_result_returning_main) that pins every example main's return type to `Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>` (contract C056-Post), and update the C056-Post contract wording to match the actual pinned type. Additionally refactor the examples to use the now-landed public `SipClient::add_account` facade (P10-3, src/client.rs:219) and remove the stale "lands in P10-3" deferral comment in examples/common/client.rs.

### Purpose
The ABC inspection (criteria A/B/C) confirmed that contract C056-Post ("every example main returns Result so errors propagate to the top level with a user-facing message and never panic") is unpinned: examples_have_no_unwrap (tests/verify_spec_p9_1.rs:194) only scans for unwrap/expect/panic tokens and would NOT fail if a main regressed to a ()-returning signature that swallows errors. The examples are the crate's Layer 5 API documentation surface (N0052/N0065), so their error-propagation contract must be empirically pinned to make the documented-but-unrunnable gap undetectable no more.

### Motivation
The prior P9-1 round deferred `SipClient::add_account` and `subscribe_audio` because their dependency tickets (P10-3, P9-2) had not landed. Both have now landed (src/client.rs:219 `pub async fn add_account`, src/client.rs:349 `pub async fn subscribe_audio`), so the RuntimeHandle::submit_add_account workaround and the stale "a facade SipClient::add_account lands in P10-3" comment in examples/common/client.rs are now tech debt. The re-implementation round closes O-001 and cleans up the deferred workaround in one pass.

### Constraints
Examples consume the public API only. The refactor replaces the RuntimeHandle::submit_add_account workaround with the public `SipClient::add_account` facade (RFC §41.2) and keeps the RuntimeHandle command path only for audio-source injection (`submit_add_audio_source`/`submit_set_audio_source_gain`), for which no SipClient facade exists. The main return type is pinned as `Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>` (NOT `Result<(), SipError>`) to match the actual implementation and the Rust application-main idiom — the O-001 recommendation explicitly permits pinning the exact return type. `make test` must stay green.

- Item: Running the examples against a live PJSIP/SIP endpoint (e.g. an actual PBX).
  - Reason: This item is not testable in the default environment (we cannot test it without a reachable SIP server): it requires a reachable SIP server and a real media path; the default `make test` environment uses MockBackend (Layer 2/5) and cannot assume a network SIP endpoint — CI does not provision a SIP server for `make test`. This is an external-dependency limitation, not a design defect (not an architectural defect) — the flow is deterministic and fully testable once a SIP server is available.
  - Alternative verification: Layer 3 (Docker Asterisk) and Layer 4 (real PBX) are defined in test_strategy_4layer.rs and run out-of-band (N0054 Docker job); this ticket's Layer 5 tests assert example flows against MockBackend, and the example binaries are runnable by the user against a live endpoint.

- Item: Real microphone capture in audio_tap (RFC §41.4 device/WAV source).
  - Reason: This item is not testable (we cannot test it without audio hardware): device capture requires the optional `cpal-input` feature (P8-7, reviewed) and physical audio hardware; the default build has the feature off and CI/dev hosts have no audio device. This is a hardware-dependency limitation, not a design defect (not an architectural defect) — the AsyncAudioSource contract is deterministic and testable with an injected source.
  - Alternative verification: the example runs headless with an injected MockAsyncAudioSource/TtsStreamSource; the device-backed path is covered by P8-7's feature-gated tests (#[ignore] without audio hardware).

- Item: Verifying exact PJSIP call-state timing in make_call.
  - Reason: This item is not testable (we cannot test wall-clock SIP timing): ringing/connect timing depends on the live stack and network; the reactor's make_call returns a hardcoded call_id (P12-1) and SipCall lifecycle is pending P9-3/P8-9. This is an external/non-deterministic-timing limitation, not a design defect (not an architectural defect) — event ordering is deterministic and assertable with MockBackend.
  - Alternative verification: integration tests assert event ordering (OutgoingCallRinging then CallConnected) with MockBackend, not wall-clock SIP behavior; the example is runnable against a live endpoint where timing is real.

- Item: Verifying real AudioChunkPair media streaming through audio_tap's subscribe_audio against a live call.
  - Reason: This item is not testable in the default environment (we cannot test it without a live SIP media path): AudioChunkPair IN/OUT frames are produced by the backend media engine, which only runs under Layer 3 (Docker SIP server + PJSUA media) or Layer 4 (real PBX). MockBackend (Layer 2/5) accepts subscribe_audio and returns an AudioTapHandle but does not generate real audio frames; the default make test environment has no media engine. acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Each of the five example binaries (account_register, audio_tap, client_init, make_call, tts_source) parses CLI args and runs against a real SipClient, performing its named operation instead of returning immediately.
【Happy path】account_register constructs an AccountConfig from CLI args and calls account.register(), exiting after registration completes or fails cleanly.
【Happy path】client_init constructs SipClient with transports/STUN per RFC §41.1 and reports the client capabilities.
【Happy path】make_call dials an OutgoingCallRequest to the CLI target URI and waits for OutgoingCallRinging / CallConnected / CallRejected events per RFC §41.3.
【Happy path】audio_tap subscribes to call audio via subscribe_audio and reads AudioChunkPair frames through AudioTapHandle::recv per RFC §41.4.
【Happy path】tts_source implements a TtsStreamSource (AsyncAudioSource over an mpsc receiver), adds it via add_audio_source, and sets gain per RFC §41.5.
【Error case】Each example exits non-zero with a user-facing error message when the SIP endpoint is unreachable, registration fails, or credentials are invalid — never panics.
【Edge case】Missing or invalid CLI args print a usage message to stderr and exit non-zero.
【Invariant】Every example main returns Result and propagates errors with `?`; no unwrap() in the example production paths (panic policy C056).

**[Happy path] — Confirm this ticket is complete:**
  - client_init: `cargo run --example client_init -- --host sip.example.com` prints the ClientInitialized capabilities (event_bus_capacity, max_calls) and exits 0 after shutdown.
  - account_register: `cargo run --example account_register -- --host <host> --username alice --domain example.com --password s3cret!` registers the account (RegistrationStateChanged observed) and exits 0.
  - make_call: `cargo run --example make_call -- --host <host> --target sip:bob@example.com` dials and observes OutgoingCallRinging then CallConnected (or CallRejected) then exits 0.
  - tts_source: `cargo run --example tts_source -- --host <host>` injects a TtsStreamSource via submit_add_audio_source, sets gain 0.6, and exits 0.
  - audio_tap: the CLI/init/error flow runs; the subscribe_audio segment is gated on P9-2.
  - All five example binaries parse CLI args and run against a real SipClient, performing their named operation instead of returning immediately. `make test` passes including tests/verify_spec_p9_1.rs.

**[Error case] — Error scenarios the feature must handle:**
  - Missing or invalid CLI args print the shared usage message to stderr and exit non-zero (CLI determinism invariant).
  - Unreachable SIP endpoint: SipClient::new or the named operation returns Err(SipError); the example prints a user-facing error and exits non-zero — never panics (C056).
  - Registration failure / invalid credentials: account_register observes RegistrationStateChanged::Failed (or returns Err) and exits non-zero with the failure reason.
  - Call rejection: make_call observes CallRejected and exits non-zero with the rejection status code.
  - The reactor is shut down before non-zero exit when it was started.

**[Edge case] — Boundary or exception scenarios to verify:**
  - --host "", --target "", --username "" are rejected before any network call (CliArgs::validate runs first; SipClient::new is never invoked).
  - --port 0 and --port 65536 are rejected; --port 1 and --port 65535 are accepted.
  - Empty argv (no args) prints the usage message and exits non-zero for every example (identical prefix — CLI determinism).
  - AudioFormat frame_ms outside {10,20,40,60} is rejected by AudioFormat::new.
  - Audio source gain is clamped to [0.0, 2.0] by the runtime.
  - Broadcast RecvError::Lagged is tolerated (no panic on slow-consumer lag).
  - Source-level test asserts zero unwrap()/expect()/panic!() in the examples' production paths (C056).

**[Happy path] — O-001 re-implementation round complete:**
  - examples_have_result_returning_main passes: all five examples (client_init, account_register, make_call, audio_tap, tts_source) declare `async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>`; a deliberately ()-returning main fails the test (red).
  - The refactored account_register/make_call examples use the public SipClient::add_account facade (RFC §41.2) and still register/dial against MockBackend; examples/common/client.rs no longer references the unlanded facade.
  - make test passes (green) including the new O-001 test and the existing 5 Layer 5 flow tests.

**[Error case] — O-001 re-implementation error scenarios:**
  - A regression that removes the Result return type from any example main (`async fn main() { ... }`) is caught by examples_have_result_returning_main with a message naming the file and line — the O-001 failure mode is now detectable.
  - SipClient::add_account with an invalid AccountConfig (empty username/domain) returns Err(SipError) from config.validate() before any network I/O; the example propagates it with `?` and exits non-zero.

**[Edge case] — O-001 re-implementation boundary scenarios:**
  - The source-inspection test normalizes whitespace before matching, so a reflowed signature (`async fn main()
    -> Result<...>`) is still detected.
  - The C056-Post contract wording and the test agree on the exact pinned type (Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>), preventing wording/test drift.

- 【Implementation steps】1) Add examples/common/cli.rs — CliArgs struct + parse() + validate() + USAGE_TEMPLATE constant. 2) Rewrite client_init.rs (host/port/stun → ClientConfig → SipClient::new → await ClientInitialized → print capabilities → shutdown). 3) Rewrite account_register.rs (args → config → SipClient::new → RuntimeCommand::AddAccount via client.handle() → client.accounts() → SipAccountHandle::new → register() → await RegistrationStateChanged → shutdown). 4) Rewrite make_call.rs (args → config → SipClient::new → AddAccount → account.make_call(OutgoingCallRequest) → subscribe_account → await OutgoingCallRinging/CallConnected/CallRejected → shutdown). 5) Rewrite tts_source.rs (TtsStreamSource over mpsc → submit_add_audio_source → submit_set_audio_source_gain → shutdown). 6) Rewrite audio_tap.rs CLI/init/error flow; keep the subscribe_audio segment gated on P9-2. 7) Update Cargo.toml — drop autoexamples=false; remove the spec-examples gate for the four achievable examples; keep it for audio_tap. 8) Add tests/verify_spec_p9_1.rs with one #[tokio::test] per example flow. 9) Resolve/justify the audio_tap subscribe stub; run make check-be and make test.

The reactor AddAccount reply is a dummy oneshot, so the account id is obtained via client.accounts() (O-004) rather than the reply.

- 【Open items】Confirm whether the `cli` feature (clap) should be enabled for the examples; the current design uses std::env::args to avoid a dependency. Decide the fate of the `spec-examples` feature declaration once audio_tap lands (remove it entirely).
- 【Future improvements】After P9-2/P9-3/P10-1/P12-1 land, the audio_tap gate is removed, registration_state() becomes assertable, and make_call can correlate events by real call_id. A later ticket may switch the shared CLI parser to clap for richer flag parsing.

evaluations.reason: Contract C056-Post requires 'every example main returns Result<(), SipError> so errors propagate to the top level with a user-facing message and never panic'. All five example mains do return Result (e.g. examples/client_init.rs:19 `async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>`, examples/make_call.rs:25, examples/tts_source.rs:52), but no test asserts this: examples_have_no_unwrap (tests/verify_spec_p9_1.rs:194) only scans for unwrap()/expect()/panic!() tokens and never checks the main return type. The Test Plan planned an assertion that every example main returns Result, but it was not implemented. Note also the contract literally says Result<(), SipError> while the implementation uses Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> — neither the type nor its propagation is pinned by a test.

If any example main were changed to return () (e.g. `async fn main() { ... }` swallowing errors), no existing test would fail: examples_have_no_unwrap only rejects unwrap/expect/panic tokens, and a ()-returning main can still compile without those tokens. A violation of the C056-Post 'errors propagate to the top level' requirement is therefore undetectable by the current suite.

tickets.background:
### Goal
The PJSIP build-detection surface for the crate is complete and contract-covered: the detection routine detect_pjsip, feature-flag resolver resolve_feature_flags, CI-matrix consumer run_ci_matrix, and the RFC §28.4 OS-dependency hints already exist in src/build/build_strategy_os_deps.rs (P10-2). P13-4 is the ABC-flagged re-implementation round whose mandatory deliverable is closing O-001 — os_dependency_hint (lines 162-167) has zero unit tests — so that every contract (C040 prebuilt-first/source-fallback with build-strategy diagnostics, C055 3-OS CI matrix) is pinned by a failing test and the with-PJSIP / without-PJSIP build surface is fully diagnosed.
### Purpose
The crate must build in two modes per RFC §4/§28: with a system PJSIP install (the pjsua-native feature path — bindgen output from P8-5 replaces the stub aliases, build.rs emits link directives) and without one (stub-alias fallback keeps cargo build/test green on PJSIP-free CI). src/build/build_strategy_os_deps.rs makes build-time detection real so the feature surface (tls/srtp flags, ClientCapabilities.tls_available/srtp_available, TransportConfig::Tls) is grounded in what the build actually found. The detection result type (PjsipDetection), backend trait (DetectionBackend), resolver, and CI-matrix consumer already exist; P13-4 verifies the complete surface is guarded by tests, with O-001 the one unguarded function.
### Motivation
This ticket is [::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::] — the prior implementation round (P10-2) was rejected by the ABC Inspection Pipeline. Source ticket P3-1 specified the public API and config surface but left the Build Strategy node (N0039) unmapped; P10-2 implemented the detection, feature wiring, and CI-matrix consumption, but the inspection confirmed O-001: os_dependency_hint returns the RFC §28.4 OS-package install hints yet has zero test references — if the Ubuntu hint dropped libsrtp2-dev or the Windows hint dropped vcpkg libsrtp, no test would fail. Downstream tickets (P8-5/P11-5 bindgen, P8-20 FFI call sites, P8-21 callback registration) all depend on pjsua-native existing and on detection being real, so the OS-dependency diagnostics that unblock them must be pinned by a failing test.
### Constraints
- Must not implement bindgen generation (P8-5/P11-5), runtime FFI call sites (P8-20), or callback registration (P8-21) — those are separate tickets that consume this ticket's detection result.
- The pjsua-native feature name must stay canonical — src/ffi/bindings.rs:25, src/ffi/mod.rs:10, build.rs, and Cargo.toml:17 all reference it; no rename.
- The crate must still compile and its test suite must still pass with all build features disabled (no PJSIP installed) — the no-PJSIP build is a first-class mode; default = ["serde", "tls"] stays unchanged.
- Feature flags derived from detection must be deterministic for a given environment and must keep cfg!(feature = "tls")/cfg!(feature = "srtp") semantics that observability_metrics.rs:127,131 already rely on.
- TDD Red-Green-Refactor is mandatory: the O-001 fix (os_dependency_hint tests) is written first and confirmed failing only if the hint strings regress; tests may not be weakened to pass.
