testExceptions: Exception entry: Real PJSIP installation/version detection cannot test without a system PJSIP install on the build host — the environment probe (filesystem under vendor/prebuilt, vendor/pjsip presence, pkg-config) is external I/O that only occurs on a real build machine. Alternative verification: unit tests inject a MockDetectionBackend behind the DetectionBackend trait (build_strategy_os_deps.rs:95-98) and cover the deterministic decision logic — prebuilt-first, source fallback, version parsing, flag resolution, hint strings. This is not a design defect: the architecture isolates the untestable environment probe behind a trait precisely so the rest is fully unit-testable.

Exception entry: Full CI matrix execution on GitHub Actions runners (windows-latest/macos-14/ubuntu-22.04 × 4 feature combos) cannot test in a local unit test — remote runner infrastructure and Docker service containers (Asterisk) are external to the local process. Alternative verification: the matrix enumeration (CiOsTarget::all, FeatureCombination::all), runner labels, cargo --features strings, TOTAL_CI_JOBS, and per-job CiJobStatus are pure data verified by unit tests; remote execution is covered by the CI workflow yaml (ci.yml/integration.yml/prebuilt-refresh.yml). This is not an architectural defect: enumeration is pure data verified by unit tests, and remote execution is an infrastructure concern, not unit-testable logic.

Exception entry: Emitting OS-dependency install hints (apt-get/brew/vcpkg command strings) cannot test as executed shell commands without mutating the host system — running apt-get/brew/vcpkg would alter the developer machine. Alternative verification: the hint content is a static data table in os_dependency_hint (build_strategy_os_deps.rs:162-167) verified by string assertions (the O-001 fix in this ticket); execution is delegated to the human/CI operator per RFC §28.4. Error case: unsupported OS targets produce Err(PjsipDetectionError::UnsupportedOs(triple)) and never panic (detect_pjsip, EnvDetectionBackend::probe); build.rs with pjsua-native enabled but no prebuilt/headers emits a cargo:warning with the RFC §28.4 package list and never silently passes; no-PJSIP builds keep the stub-alias fallback green.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal establishment】Detection is deterministic for a given environment: detect_pjsip(&backend) returns Present { version: PjsipVersion::new(2,17,0) } whenever the backend reports a usable install (prebuilt lib complete at vendor/prebuilt/{triple}/lib OR vendor/pjsip/CMakeLists.txt present per EnvDetectionBackend::probe, lines 218-232) and Absent otherwise; resolve_feature_flags (lines 129-135) is a pure function of the PjsipDetection value — identical inputs always yield the identical ResolvedFeatures { pjsua_native, tls, srtp } set; no time- or order-dependent behavior.
- 【Invariant on error】A detection failure surfaces as a structured error — PjsipDetectionError::UnsupportedOs(triple) for non-CI targets and ProbeFailed(String) for backend failure — via Result, never a panic and never a silent fallback to the native path; the stub-alias fallback (PjsipDetection::Absent ⇒ pjsua_native=false) is the only legitimate no-PJSIP outcome.
- 【Internal state invariant】The pjsua-native Cargo feature is the single source of truth: cfg(feature = "pjsua-native") in src/ffi/bindings.rs:25, the build.rs CARGO_FEATURE_PJSUA_NATIVE gate (feature_env_present), Cargo.toml [features] line 17, and lints.rust check-cfg line 33 must all agree — no orphan cfg, no duplicate declaration; the unexpected_cfgs warning stays clean.
- 【Boundary invariant】Feature-gated config types stay consistent with flags: TransportConfig::Tls present only under cfg(feature = "tls") (C016), SRTP gated with srtp_available reflecting compile-time detection (C043); resolve_feature_flags.tls == cfg!(feature = "tls") and .srtp == cfg!(feature = "srtp") by construction, so ClientCapabilities.tls_available/srtp_available (observability_metrics.rs:127,131) always match; the crate compiles and its suite passes with all build features disabled (no PJSIP installed).

tickets.title: Add cpal as an optional dependency behind the cpal-input feature and implement device-backed capture returning Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError> with an integration test

contracts.precondition: cpal is an optional dependency reachable only through the `cpal-input` feature (default build graph contains no cpal). The RFC §40 signature exists behind #[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")]: `pub async fn open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>`. The input `format` is a validated AudioFormat (AudioFormat::new succeeded; sample_rate ∈ {Hz8000, Hz16000, Hz24000, Hz48000}, bit_depth ∈ {I16, F32}, channel_layout ∈ {Mono, StereoInOut}, frame_ms ∈ {10, 20, 40, 60}).
contracts.postcondition: When a default input device exists and its native sample format is convertible to the i16 pipeline contract, open_default_microphone_source returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) whose next_chunk fills the caller's &mut [i16] buffer with captured PCM and returns the written sample count. Device-open, format-mismatch, build-stream, and play failures surface as Err(SipError) (SipErrorKind::NativeError for device/stream errors; SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats) — never a panic.
contracts.invariant: The returned source is AsyncAudioSource + Send and can be stored as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> in AudioMixer (ErasedAudioSource auto-derived via blanket impl). Sample conversion clamps into the valid i16 range (no wraparound). With `cpal-input` disabled, the function, the CpalMicrophoneSource type, and the cpal crate are compiled out of the build.

contracts.precondition: Audio subscribe uses sources — AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>; AsyncAudioSource trait is defined as #[async_trait::async_trait] pub trait AsyncAudioSource: Send { async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize; }.
contracts.postcondition: ErasedAudioSource blanket impl auto-derived for all T: AsyncAudioSource + Send; SyncAudioSource trait and SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> provided for synchronous sources; any new concrete source (e.g. CpalMicrophoneSource) implementing AsyncAudioSource + Send automatically gains ErasedAudioSource.
contracts.invariant: ErasedAudioSource auto-derived for every AsyncAudioSource implementor — blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> ErasedAudioSource for T must compile. SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send. CpalMicrophoneSource must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send so it is usable as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed (O-001, major). This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Resolve O-001 and finalize the real cpal device-backed microphone source: keep `open_default_microphone_source` (src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:173-179) returning `Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` backed by the platform default microphone behind the `cpal-input` feature, and close the ABC gap by unit-testing every error path (map_default_config_error / map_supported_configs_error / map_build_stream_error / map_play_error) and the unsupported-sample-format arm of build_input_stream, with the feature-gated integration test retained.

### Purpose
The `cpal-input` feature has been wired since P8-7 (Cargo.toml: `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]`), and the microphone source is the only RFC-required audio source that is device-backed. Downstream consumers (AudioMixer via P5-2, the audio_tap example via P8-6, AI TTS source insertion) rely on opening the default microphone as an AsyncAudioSource. The ABC inspection confirmed the happy-path machinery is complete but the error-contract (never-panic / typed-Err) is not enforced by any test — O-001 must be closed so the contract is provable.

### Motivation
P8-4 delivered the AsyncAudioSource adapter machinery under a no-new-dependencies constraint; P8-7 landed the cpal dependency and real capture, resolving the `[::STUB::] P8-7` marker. What remains is the ABC-mandated O-001 closure: cpal 0.18.1 exposes publicly constructible `cpal::Error` and `SupportedStreamConfig`, so the error paths are unit-testable without a device — the omission is a test-coverage defect, not an architectural limit. This ticket removes that defect and re-proves C051/C033.

### Constraints
- cpal must be an optional dependency reachable only via `cpal-input`; default builds must not pull the cpal crate (feature-additive invariant). Cargo.toml [features] declares `check-cfg = ['cfg(feature, values("cpal-input", "pjsua-native"))']`.
- MSRV is 1.95; pin a cpal version whose API is stable and documented — cpal 0.18.1 (Cargo.lock) requires an explicit `stream.play()` after build and pins the sample rate/config explicitly.
- The public `open_default_microphone_source` signature must not change (C051 precondition); the returned source must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send.
- No panics on device failure — all errors map to SipError (NativeError for device/stream, AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats). The O-001 unit tests must make a regression detectable.
- CI without audio hardware must not run the device integration test by default (#[ignore] + SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO=1 gate).

### Goal
scope: - **Scope of changes:**
- [File/module path] Cargo.toml — [dependencies] + [features] sections
- [Action] MODIFY (add optional dependency + rewire feature)

- [What specifically changes] Add `cpal = { version = "0.18", optional = true }` to [dependencies]; change `cpal-input = []` to `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]`; update the `[::STUB::] P1-3 (N0050)` comment that says 'Full implementation requires the cpal crate (P8-4)'. Current Cargo.toml already declares `check-cfg = ['cfg(feature, values("cpal-input"))']`.
- [Before → After] Before: `cpal-input = []` (empty feature, no cpal). After: `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]` (feature pulls cpal; default build unchanged).
- [File/module path] src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — open_default_microphone_source + CpalMicrophoneSource + error-mapping helpers + test module

- [Action] MODIFY (resolve O-001) — extract the sample-format-match logic from `build_input_stream` into the pure helper `select_sample_format_handler(cpal::SampleFormat, SampleQueue) -> Result<SampleFormatHandler, SipError>` so the `other =>` AudioFormatUnsupported arm (lines 466-471) becomes unit-testable without a cpal::Device; add the 5 O-001 unit tests (4 map_*_error helpers + select_sample_format_handler accept/reject) to the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block.

- [What specifically changes] The public signature `pub async fn open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` stays unchanged (C051 precondition); `build_input_stream` is refactored internally (behavior-preserving) by delegating the sample-format dispatch to the new pure helper; the test module grows from 12 to 17 feature-gated tests.

- [Before → After] Before: `build_input_stream` inlines the I16/F32/U16/`other` match and the `other` arm is untested (ABC O-001 violation — no assertion could detect a panic or wrong SipErrorKind). After: the format decision is a pure function; every non-convertible format returns Err(SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported) and is asserted in tests.

- [API contract change] None breaking — the public RFC §40 signature and C051 pre/post conditions are unchanged; behavior changes from always-Err placeholder (P8-4) to real capture (P8-7 already landed) and the O-001 tests now pin the typed-Err postcondition.
- [Data schema change] None — no serialized data format changes.
- [Config/env change] None — no new env vars required; the integration test honors SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO=1 to force device tests on capable hosts.
- [Dependency added] `cpal` (optional, behind `cpal-input`, version 0.18.1 in Cargo.lock) — the only new crate; default build graph is cpal-free.
- **Out of scope:**
- [Excluded item] AudioMixer auto-wiring of the microphone and real PJSIP media conf-port bridging (P3-2 N0050)

- [Why excluded] Mixer integration already accepts any AsyncAudioSource (P5-2); conf-port wiring is a separate PJSIP-media ticket; this ticket resolves only the device-source adapter, its error paths, and the feature gate.
- [Excluded item] Sample-rate resampling inside the adapter

- [Why excluded] Converting the device's native rate to an arbitrary requested rate belongs to model::audio_resampler; this adapter uses the device's default config when the requested format is not natively supported.
- **Affected areas:**
- [Affected component] src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs (test module + build_input_stream refactor), Cargo.toml, tests/verify_spec_p8_7.rs, Cargo.lock
- [Nature of impact] Additive optional dependency; default builds pull no cpal crate; the `cpal-input` feature becomes real (was empty); the O-001 refactor is internal and behavior-preserving.
- [Corresponding change needed] Y — CI jobs that enable `cpal-input` need audio device access or must rely on the #[ignore] device test; `make test` (default) runs the feature-off build.
testUnit: UT: [Normal] C051-Pre: RFC §40 signature — `#[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")] pub async fn open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` must exist with the exact arity and return type. Already implemented as `open_default_microphone_source_has_correct_signature` (src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:732): the generic bound `assert_microphone_future<F: Future<Output = Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>>>` fails to compile if the output type drifts; the future is dropped unpolled so no device access occurs. Input is a valid AudioFormat (48000/I16/Mono/20ms via AudioFormat::new).

UT: [Normal] C051-Post: SampleQueue::drain_to fills an i16 buffer with queued PCM in FIFO order and returns the exact written count — construct `SampleQueue::new()`, `push_i16(&[100i16, 200i16, 300i16])`, drain into a `[0i16; 4]` buffer, assert written == 3 and buf[0..3] == [100, 200, 300]. Existing test `sample_queue_drains_in_fifo_order` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:791).

UT: [Normal] C051-Post: CpalMicrophoneSource::next_chunk delegates to the shared SampleQueue — use the #[cfg(test)] constructor `CpalMicrophoneSource::from_queue(SampleQueue::new())` (bypasses the real cpal::Stream), `queue().push_i16(&[7i16, 8i16, 9i16, 10i16])`, call `AsyncAudioSource::next_chunk(&mut source, &mut out)`, assert written == 4 and out == the pushed samples. Existing test `microphone_source_next_chunk_delegates_to_queue` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:846).

UT: [Normal] C051-Post / C033-Post: ErasedAudioSource blanket impl auto-derives for the concrete source — a `Box<dyn ErasedAudioSource>` is constructible from `CpalMicrophoneSource::from_queue(...)` (blanket impl `<T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> ErasedAudioSource for T` compiles) and next_chunk delegates correctly. Existing test `microphone_source_is_erased_audio_source` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:882).

UT: [Error] C051-Post: SampleQueue::drain_to on an empty queue returns 0 without panicking — end-of-stream per the AsyncAudioSource contract; drain a fresh empty queue into a `[0i16; 4]` buffer and assert 0. Existing test `sample_queue_empty_returns_zero` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:807).

UT: [Error] C051-Post: f32 sample conversion clamps — `convert_f32_sample_to_i16(1.0) == i16::MAX`, `convert_f32_sample_to_i16(-1.0) == i16::MIN`, `convert_f32_sample_to_i16(0.0) == 0`, and out-of-range values (2.0 / -2.0) clamp to i16::MAX / i16::MIN, never wrap. UT: [Error] C051-Post (O-001 closure): unsupported sample-format mapping — the pure helper `select_sample_format_handler(cpal::SampleFormat, SampleQueue) -> Result<SampleFormatHandler, SipError>` (extracted from the `other =>` arm of `build_input_stream`, asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:466-471) returns `Err(SipError::new(SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported, format!("unsupported_sample_format: {other:?}")))` for any format outside {I16, F32, U16} rather than panicking. Unit-test directly: `assert_eq!(select_sample_format_handler(SampleFormat::I8, SampleQueue::new()).unwrap_err().kind(), SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported)`. This makes the never-panic / typed-Err postcondition detectable (Evaluation B).

UT: [Boundary] C051-Post: u16 conversion is bijective at the extremes — `convert_u16_sample_to_i16(u16::MAX) == i16::MAX`, `convert_u16_sample_to_i16(0) == i16::MIN`, `convert_u16_sample_to_i16(0x8000) == 0`, `convert_u16_sample_to_i16(1) == -32767` (linear DC-offset-preserving mapping, exact at the extremes). testExceptions: Item: Asserting specific PCM sample values from the real microphone is not testable in CI because captured samples depend on physical microphone input and OS audio routing — a non-deterministic external dependency, not a code defect. Reason: deterministic logic (sample conversion, queue drain, FIFO order, error mapping) is extracted into pure functions (convert_f32_sample_to_i16, convert_u16_sample_to_i16, SampleQueue, map_*_error, select_sample_format_handler) and covered by unit tests; the integration test asserts only that >= 1 frame is produced. This is not a case of 'deterministic yet fundamentally untestable' (an architectural defect): the deterministic core is fully extracted and unit-tested. Alternative verification: unit tests on the pure helpers; #[ignore] device test.

Item: Cross-platform device enumeration differences cannot test deterministically because cpal device availability, names, and default-device selection differ per OS (CoreAudio, ALSA, WASAPI) and change with user audio settings — an external, non-deterministic environment. Reason: the device layer is a thin boundary and all deterministic logic (select_input_config preference, sample-format match, error mapping, queue handoff) is covered by synthetic SampleQueue / pure-helper unit tests. This is not an architectural defect: the nondeterminism lives only at the device boundary, not in the crate's own logic. Alternative verification: error-mapping functions are unit-tested; the device integration test is #[ignore] where no default device exists.

Item: Forcing the 'no default input device' condition is impossible to test inside a unit test because cpal exposes no mock seam for Host/Device and device presence is environment-dependent — an external dependency, not a code defect. Reason: the device-open logic is thin and every non-environmental decision (sample-format match, error mapping, queue handoff) is extracted into unit-testable functions; cpal::Error and SupportedStreamConfig are publicly constructible so the error paths are exercised without a device. This is not a design defect: the only untestable residue is the OS-level device probe itself, whose absence path is covered by the #[ignore] no-device integration test. Alternative verification: the #[ignore] no-device integration test on a host without an audio backend.
acceptanceCriteria: - 【Happy path】With `--features cpal-input`, open_default_microphone_source(format) opens the platform default input device and returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>) whose next_chunk fills an i16 buffer with captured PCM (>= 1 sample on a real device, verified by the #[ignore] integration test). The returned source is AsyncAudioSource + Send and can be stored as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> in AudioMixer (compile-time check). The O-001 unit tests pass: the 4 map_*_error helpers return NativeError with their prefixes for constructible cpal::Error values, and select_sample_format_handler accepts {I16,F32,U16} and rejects the other 12 SampleFormat variants with AudioFormatUnsupported.

- 【Error case】When no default input device exists, open_default_microphone_source returns Err(SipError) with a clear message (SipErrorKind::NativeError) instead of panicking (C051-Post typed-Err). When the requested AudioFormat cannot be matched by the device (non-convertible sample format), the function returns Err(SipError) describing the format mismatch (SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported) — asserted by the select_sample_format_handler unit tests, so a regression to panic!() or a wrong SipErrorKind fails CI.

- 【Edge case】With the feature disabled (default), the function and CpalMicrophoneSource are compiled out and the crate builds without cpal — no device capture is attempted and `cargo tree -e normal` shows no cpal (feature-additive invariant). Sample conversion clamps at i16 boundaries; an empty queue / zero-length buffer returns 0 without panicking. A 65536-sample buffer (AudioMixer boundary) drains without overflow.

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal condition】With `cpal-input` enabled and a default input device present, open_default_microphone_source returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) and next_chunk fills the i16 buffer with device PCM. The cpal crate compiles only under the feature (Cargo.toml: cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]). select_input_config prefers a supported config matching the requested channel count and sample rate and falls back to the device default otherwise (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:387-413).
- 【Invariant on error】Device-open, default-config, build-stream, and play failures never panic — they surface as Err(SipError). Sample formats outside the convertible set {I16, F32, U16} map to SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported via select_sample_format_handler; other device errors map to SipErrorKind::NativeError via the map_*_error helpers. The 5 O-001 unit tests pin these kind mappings so a violation (panic or wrong kind) fails CI.
- 【Internal state invariant】CpalMicrophoneSource holds an Option<cpal::Stream> plus an Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<i16>>> sample queue; the queue grows only from the cpal callback thread (push_i16) and shrinks only via next_chunk (drain_to); next_chunk returns 0 when the queue is empty (end-of-stream). A poisoned mutex is recovered via into_inner() so the callback never unwinds across the audio boundary.
- 【Boundary invariant】Sample conversion is bijective at the extremes and clamped in between: u16::MAX↔i16::MAX, 0↔i16::MIN, 0x8000↔0 (convert_u16_sample_to_i16, DC-offset preserved); f32 in [-1.0, 1.0] maps linearly via F32_TO_I16_SCALE=32768.0 with clamping (never wraps). A zero-length buffer returns 0 without panicking; a 65536-sample buffer (AudioMixer boundary) drains without overflow.

- [Normal condition]

/// C051-Post — opens the platform default microphone and captures at least one
/// PCM frame into the i16 buffer the AsyncAudioSource contract requires.

tickets.title: Add cpal as an optional dependency behind the cpal-input feature and implement device-backed capture returning Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError> with an integration test

contracts.precondition: cpal is an optional dependency reachable only through the `cpal-input` feature (default build graph contains no cpal). The RFC §40 signature exists behind #[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")]: `pub async fn open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>`. The input `format` is a validated AudioFormat (AudioFormat::new succeeded; sample_rate ∈ {Hz8000, Hz16000, Hz24000, Hz48000}, bit_depth ∈ {I16, F32}, channel_layout ∈ {Mono, StereoInOut}, frame_ms ∈ {10, 20, 40, 60}).
contracts.postcondition: When a default input device exists and its native sample format is convertible to the i16 pipeline contract, open_default_microphone_source returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) whose next_chunk fills the caller's &mut [i16] buffer with captured PCM and returns the written sample count. Device-open, format-mismatch, build-stream, and play failures surface as Err(SipError) (SipErrorKind::NativeError for device/stream errors; SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats) — never a panic.
contracts.invariant: The returned source is AsyncAudioSource + Send and can be stored as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send> in AudioMixer (ErasedAudioSource auto-derived via blanket impl). Sample conversion clamps into the valid i16 range (no wraparound). With `cpal-input` disabled, the function, the CpalMicrophoneSource type, and the cpal crate are compiled out of the build. `select_input_config` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:385-413) prefers a supported config matching the requested channel count and sample rate via the extracted pure helper `prefer_config_matching_request(candidates, requested_channels, requested_sample_rate) -> Option<SupportedStreamConfig>` and falls back to the device default config otherwise — this preference decision is pinned by the 4 O-001 unit tests.

contracts.precondition: Audio subscribe uses sources — AudioMixer stores Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>; AsyncAudioSource trait is defined as #[async_trait::async_trait] pub trait AsyncAudioSource: Send { async fn next_chunk(&mut self, buf: &mut [i16]) -> usize; }.
contracts.postcondition: ErasedAudioSource blanket impl auto-derived for all T: AsyncAudioSource + Send; SyncAudioSource trait and SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> provided for synchronous sources; any new concrete source (e.g. CpalMicrophoneSource) implementing AsyncAudioSource + Send automatically gains ErasedAudioSource.
contracts.invariant: ErasedAudioSource auto-derived for every AsyncAudioSource implementor — blanket impl <T: AsyncAudioSource + Send> ErasedAudioSource for T must compile. SyncSourceAdapter<T: SyncAudioSource + Send> must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send. CpalMicrophoneSource must implement AsyncAudioSource + Send so it is usable as Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>.

tickets.background:
[::INSPECTION_FLAGGED::]
This ticket has been flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle (make → plan → start → review → resolve). The actual source code was rigorously analyzed against three criteria:

  A — Contract Translation:   Are all Precondition/Postcondition/Invariant contracts accurately translated into test code?
  B — Violation Detection:    Can every contract violation be detected by an existing test assertion?
  C — Test Precision:         Are tests precise and unambiguous (no broad assertions, no missing edge cases)?

One or more ABC violations were confirmed (O-001, major). This ticket is hereby remanded for re-implementation. Every violation must be fully resolved, and every contract must be fulfilled in this final implementation round. Complete it this time.

### Goal
Resolve O-001 by making the C051-Invariant config-preference decision provable: extract the channels+sample-rate matching logic from `select_input_config` (src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:385-413) into a pure, unit-testable helper `prefer_config_matching_request(candidates: impl IntoIterator<Item = &cpal::SupportedStreamConfig>, requested_channels: cpal::ChannelCount, requested_sample_rate: cpal::SampleRate) -> Option<cpal::SupportedStreamConfig>` and refactor `select_input_config` to delegate the decision to it (behavior-preserving), then pin the prefer/fallback branches with feature-gated unit tests constructed from publicly-constructible `cpal::SupportedStreamConfig::new(...)` values. This closes ABC Evaluation A (contract translation — the decision becomes test code) and Evaluation B (violation detection — removing or changing the channels filter or the rate preference fails CI).

### Purpose
The `cpal-input` feature (Cargo.toml:26 `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]`) and the device-backed microphone source were wired in P8-7, and P13-1 already closed the sibling O-001 for the sample-format dispatch (`select_sample_format_handler`). The remaining deterministic decision — `select_input_config` preferring a supported config that matches the requested channel count and sample rate, else falling back to `default_input_config()` — is embedded in a `&cpal::Device`-taking function, so no existing test can detect a regression (ABC O-001). Downstream consumers (AudioMixer via P5-2, the audio_tap example via P8-6, AI TTS source insertion) rely on the microphone source opening with the correct capture config; the preference logic must be provably correct.

### Motivation
cpal 0.18.1 (Cargo.lock) exposes `SupportedStreamConfig::new(channels: u16, sample_rate: u32, buffer_size: SupportedBufferSize, sample_format: SampleFormat)` as a public constructor (cpal src/lib.rs:536), so the preference decision is unit-testable without a device — the omission is a test-coverage defect, not an architectural limit. The ABC inspection explicitly recommends the extraction (`prefer_config_matching_request(configs, format) -> Option<SupportedStreamConfig>`), mirroring the P13-1 `select_sample_format_handler` extraction pattern. This ticket removes that defect and re-proves C051.

### Constraints
- The `select_input_config` refactor must be behavior-preserving: same preferred config (first range in device order whose channels match AND which supports the requested rate), same `default_input_config()` fallback, same `map_supported_configs_error` / `map_default_config_error` mapping.
- The public signature `pub async fn open_default_microphone_source(format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` must not change (C051 precondition).
- New unit tests must construct only publicly-constructible cpal types (`SupportedStreamConfig::new`, `SupportedBufferSize`, `SampleFormat`, `Error::with_message`) — no `cpal::Device`, no real hardware.
- No new dependencies; `cpal` stays optional behind `cpal-input`; the default `make test` build must remain cpal-free.
- CI without audio hardware must not run the device integration test by default (#[ignore] + SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO=1 gate) — retained unchanged.
scope: - **Scope of changes:**
- [File/module path] src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs — `select_input_config` (lines 385-413), new pure helper `prefer_config_matching_request`, and the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block

- [Action] REFACTOR (behavior-preserving) + ADD tests — extract the config-preference decision from `select_input_config` into the pure helper `prefer_config_matching_request`, delegate the decision to it, and add 4 feature-gated unit tests

- [What specifically changes] `select_input_config` currently inlines `filter(channels == requested_channels).filter_map(try_with_sample_rate).next()` over the device's `supported_input_configs()` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:395-406). After the refactor, the device loop materializes candidate `SupportedStreamConfig` values (all ranges that accept the requested rate via `try_with_sample_rate`, which is Option-returning in cpal 0.18), and `prefer_config_matching_request(&candidates, requested_channels, requested_sample_rate)` picks the first candidate matching BOTH channels and rate; a `None` result still triggers the `default_input_config()` fallback. The 4 new tests construct `cpal::SupportedStreamConfig::new(...)` directly and assert prefer / None / first-match / empty behavior.

- [Before → After] Before: the channels filter + `try_with_sample_rate` + `.next()` decision was inline in a `&cpal::Device` function, reachable only through real hardware, and untested (ABC O-001). After: the decision is a pure function over publicly-constructible `SupportedStreamConfig` values; every branch (exact match / no match / first-match / empty) is asserted in CI under `cargo test --features cpal-input`.

- [API contract change] None breaking — `open_default_microphone_source` signature, C051 pre/post, and the capture behavior are unchanged; the refactor is internal and the C051-Invariant preference semantics are preserved and now pinned by tests.
- [Data schema change] None — no serialized data format changes.
- [Config/env change] None — no new env vars; the retained `SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO=1` gate and the `#[ignore]` device integration test are unchanged.
- [Dependency added/removed] None — `cpal` remains `{ version = "0.18", optional = true }` behind `cpal-input` (Cargo.toml:73); no new crates added or removed.
- **Out of scope:**
- [Excluded item] Cargo.toml / cpal feature wiring (`cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]`, `check-cfg`) — already landed in P8-7.
- [Why excluded] The feature gate, optional dependency, and `check-cfg` are present in the current Cargo.toml (lines 26, 33, 73); this ticket only adds the O-001 pure-helper refactor and its tests.
- [Excluded item] AudioMixer auto-wiring of the microphone and real PJSIP media conf-port bridging (P3-2 N0050); sample-rate resampling inside the adapter.

- [Why excluded] Mixer integration already accepts any AsyncAudioSource (P5-2); conf-port wiring is a separate PJSIP-media ticket; resampling belongs to model::audio_resampler — the adapter uses the device default config as the fallback.
- **Affected areas:**

- [Affected component] src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs (`select_input_config` + new `prefer_config_matching_request` helper + test module); Cargo.toml (unchanged); tests/verify_spec_p8_7.rs (unchanged, retained); Cargo.lock (unchanged)
- [Nature of impact] Internal behavior-preserving refactor; the cpal-gated unit-test count grows by 4; the default build is unaffected and stays cpal-free.

- [Corresponding change needed] N — no CI/build-config change; `make test` (default, feature-off) and `cargo test --features cpal-input --lib` both run the relevant tests (the new tests compile only under the feature).

Already implemented as `open_default_microphone_source_has_correct_signature` (src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:732): the generic bound `assert_microphone_future<F: Future<Output = Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>>>` fails to compile if the output type drifts; the future is dropped unpolled so no device access occurs. testExceptions: Item: Asserting specific PCM sample values from the real microphone is not testable in CI because captured samples depend on physical microphone input and OS audio routing — a non-deterministic external dependency, not a code defect. Reason: all deterministic logic (sample conversion, queue drain, error mapping, config-preference decision) is extracted into pure functions (convert_f32_sample_to_i16, convert_u16_sample_to_i16, SampleQueue, map_*_error, select_sample_format_handler, prefer_config_matching_request) and covered by unit tests; the integration test asserts only that >= 1 frame is produced. This is not a case of 'deterministic yet fundamentally untestable' (an architectural defect): the deterministic core is fully extracted and unit-tested. Alternative verification: unit tests on the pure helpers; #[ignore] device test.

Item: Cross-platform device enumeration differences are not testable deterministically because cpal device availability, names, and default-device selection differ per OS (CoreAudio, ALSA, WASAPI) and change with user audio settings — an external, non-deterministic environment. Reason: the device layer is a thin boundary and all deterministic logic (select_input_config preference via prefer_config_matching_request, sample-format match, error mapping, queue handoff) is covered by synthetic SampleQueue / pure-helper unit tests. This is not an architectural defect: the nondeterminism lives only at the device boundary, not in the crate's own logic. Alternative verification: error-mapping and preference helpers are unit-tested; the device integration test is #[ignore] where no default device exists.

Item: Forcing the 'no default input device' / 'no matching config' condition is impossible to test inside a unit test because cpal exposes no mock seam for Host/Device and device presence is environment-dependent — an external dependency, not a code defect. Reason: the device-open logic is thin and every non-environmental decision (config-preference via prefer_config_matching_request, sample-format match, error mapping, queue handoff) is extracted into unit-testable functions; cpal::Error and SupportedStreamConfig are publicly constructible so the error and preference paths are exercised without a device. This is not a design defect: the only untestable residue is the OS-level device probe itself, whose absence path is covered by the #[ignore] no-device integration test. Alternative verification: the #[ignore] no-device integration test on a host without an audio backend.
acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】With --features cpal-input, open_default_microphone_source(format) opens the platform default input device and returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>) whose next_chunk fills an i16 buffer with captured PCM (>= 1 sample on a real device, verified by the retained #[ignore] integration test). The O-001 unit tests pass: the 4 prefer_config_matching_request tests confirm the C051-Invariant preference (exact channels+rate match wins, first-match order, None on no-match/empty) using constructible SupportedStreamConfig::new(...) values.

【Error case】When no default input device exists, open_default_microphone_source returns Err(SipError) with a clear message (SipErrorKind::NativeError) instead of panicking. When no supported config matches the requested channels+rate, select_input_config falls back to the device default via prefer_config_matching_request returning None; if the default config also fails it maps to NativeError via map_default_config_error. A regression to a wrong config choice or a panic fails the prefer-config unit tests.

【Edge case】With the feature disabled (default), the function and CpalMicrophoneSource are compiled out and the crate builds without cpal (cargo tree -e normal shows no cpal). prefer_config_matching_request on an empty candidate list returns None without panicking; a candidate with the right rate but wrong channels (and vice versa) is skipped; sample conversion clamps at i16 boundaries; a 65536-sample buffer (AudioMixer boundary) drains without overflow; a zero-length buffer returns 0.

- 【Implementation steps】(1) TDD Red — add the 4 `prefer_config_matching_request` unit tests to the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block of src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs: construct `cpal::SupportedStreamConfig::new(channels, sample_rate, SupportedBufferSize::Unknown, sample_format)` candidates and assert (a) exact channels+rate match is preferred, (b) None when no candidate matches, (c) the first exact match wins, (d) empty candidates → None. These fail Red because `prefer_config_matching_request` does not exist yet. (2) Green — add `prefer_config_matching_request<'a>(candidates: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a cpal::SupportedStreamConfig>, requested_channels: cpal::ChannelCount, requested_sample_rate: cpal::SampleRate) -> Option<cpal::SupportedStreamConfig>` and refactor `select_input_config` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:385-413) to materialize candidates via `supported_input_configs().map_err(map_supported_configs_error)?.filter_map(|range| range.try_with_sample_rate(requested_sample_rate))` and delegate the decision; `None` still falls back to `default_input_config().map_err(map_default_config_error)`. Behavior-preserving — verify `cargo test --features cpal-input --lib` passes. (3) Verify the default feature-off build: `make test` and `cargo tree -e normal` (no cpal). (4) On a host with a mic, run the retained device test: `cargo test --features cpal-input --test verify_spec_p8_7 -- --ignored` with `SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO=1`.
- 【Risks】cpal API drift — v0.18's `try_with_sample_rate` returns `Option<SupportedStreamConfig>` (not Result) and `SampleRate` / `ChannelCount` are u32/u16 type aliases; a future cpal version could change the constructibility of `SupportedStreamConfig` (currently `new()` is public at cpal src/lib.rs:536). ALSA/WASAPI/CoreAudio device availability differs; the device test must stay #[ignore] and never gate `make test`.
- 【Caveats】The refactor materializes ALL ranges that accept the requested rate into a Vec before the pure decision; this is behavior-preserving (the first matching candidate is unchanged) but allocates — acceptable because `supported_input_configs()` typically yields a handful of ranges and `select_input_config` runs once per source open. The captured stream runs on a cpal callback thread; the sample queue must be Send+Sync (Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<i16>>>) and drained at least as fast as the device fills it.
- 【Open items】Whether I32/I64/F64 input formats should be supported beyond I16/F32/U16 (reject for now — `select_sample_format_handler` maps them to AudioFormatUnsupported); whether `prefer_config_matching_request` should take `&AudioFormat` instead of separate `requested_channels` / `requested_sample_rate` (implementation choice, contract-neutral); the SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO env var name is retained for the #[ignore] device test.
- 【Future improvements】Route the source into AudioMixer automatically (separate PJSIP-media ticket); add sample-rate resampling via model::audio_resampler; expose device enumeration + selection (e.g. open_microphone_by_name); wire the audio_tap example (P8-6).

tickets.invariants:
- 【Normal condition】With `cpal-input` enabled and a default input device present, open_default_microphone_source returns Ok(Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource + Send>) and next_chunk fills the i16 buffer with device PCM. `select_input_config` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:385-413) prefers the first supported config matching the requested channel count AND sample rate via the extracted pure helper `prefer_config_matching_request(candidates, requested_channels, requested_sample_rate) -> Option<SupportedStreamConfig>`; when no candidate matches it falls back to the device default config. The cpal crate compiles only under the feature (Cargo.toml:26 `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]`).
- 【Invariant on error】Device-open, default-config, build-stream, and play failures never panic — they surface as Err(SipError). Sample formats outside the convertible set {I16, F32, U16} map to SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported via `select_sample_format_handler`; other device errors map to SipErrorKind::NativeError via the map_*_error helpers. A `None` from `prefer_config_matching_request` (no candidate matches the request) is NOT an error — it triggers the default-config fallback inside `select_input_config`. The O-001 unit tests (4 new prefer tests + 6 P13-1 tests) pin these behaviors so a violation (panic, wrong kind, or dropped preference) fails CI.
- 【Internal state invariant】CpalMicrophoneSource holds an Option<cpal::Stream> plus an Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<i16>>> sample queue; the queue grows only from the cpal callback thread (push_i16) and shrinks only via next_chunk (drain_to); next_chunk returns 0 when the queue is empty (end-of-stream). A poisoned mutex is recovered via into_inner() so the callback never unwinds across the audio boundary. `prefer_config_matching_request` is pure — it reads candidates immutably and returns a cloned config or None; it holds no state and performs no I/O.
- 【Boundary invariant】Sample conversion is bijective at the extremes and clamped in between (u16::MAX↔i16::MAX, 0↔i16::MIN, 0x8000↔0; f32 in [-1.0, 1.0] via F32_TO_I16_SCALE=32768.0 with clamping, never wraps). `prefer_config_matching_request` handles the boundary cases exactly: an empty candidate list → None; the first exact channels+rate match wins (device order preserved); a candidate with matching channels but wrong rate is skipped; a candidate with the right rate but wrong channels is skipped. A zero-length buffer returns 0 without panicking; a 65536-sample buffer (AudioMixer boundary) drains without overflow.
tickets.instrumentation:
- [Logging] `input_stream_error` logs every async cpal stream error via `tracing::error!(error = %err, "cpal input stream error")` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:296-300). All synchronous device/stream failures surface as `SipError` whose message carries a greppable prefix: `no_default_input_device:`, `default_input_config_failed:`, `supported_input_configs_failed:`, `build_stream_failed:`, `play_failed:`, `unsupported_sample_format:`. The O-001 tests assert the prefixes, keeping them stable. The new `prefer_config_matching_request` needs no logging — it is a pure decision; a `None` result is a normal fallback path, not an error.
- [Metrics] None added in this ticket — audio pipeline metrics (sample counts, mixer state) are owned by AudioMixer/AudioWorker (P5-2). The queue-drain count returned by next_chunk is the observable throughput signal and is exercised by the unit tests.
- [Error tracking] Every cpal failure maps to a typed `SipError` (SipErrorKind::NativeError for device/stream errors, SipErrorKind::AudioFormatUnsupported for non-convertible sample formats) — never a panic. Async stream errors during capture are logged (not propagated) because the callback cannot unwind across the audio boundary; the source then signals end-of-stream (next_chunk returns 0). `select_input_config` propagates `supported_input_configs` failures via `map_supported_configs_error` and `default_input_config` failures via `map_default_config_error`.
- [Health check] No new health checks. The AsyncAudioSource contract itself is the liveness signal: next_chunk returning 0 on an empty queue indicates no data is flowing; a poisoned mutex is recovered via `into_inner()` so the callback never unwinds. `prefer_config_matching_request` returning None on an empty candidate list is a config-selection signal that routes capture to the device default — a normal fallback, verified by unit tests.

Material evidence gathered from source code + cpal 0.18.1 crate source:
- src/api/asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:173-179 — `open_default_microphone_source` is `#[cfg(feature = "cpal-input")] pub async fn (format: AudioFormat) -> Result<Box<dyn AsyncAudioSource>, SipError>` and calls `CpalMicrophoneSource::new(format)?` then boxes it. Fully implemented; no placeholder body and no `[::STUB::] P8-7` marker remain.
- asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:190-227 — `SampleQueue { samples: Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<i16>>> }` with `push_i16(&[i16])` / `drain_to(&mut [i16]) -> usize`; poisoned-mutex recovery via `into_inner()`; `#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]`.
- asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:244-254 — `convert_f32_sample_to_i16` (F32_TO_I16_SCALE=32768.0, clamped) and `convert_u16_sample_to_i16` ((sample as i32 - U16_DC_OFFSET=0x8000) as i16). Named constants.
- asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:264-293 — the 4 error-mapping helpers `map_default_config_error` / `map_supported_configs_error` / `map_build_stream_error` / `map_play_error`, each `SipError::new(SipErrorKind::NativeError, format!("...: {err}"))` with distinct greppable prefixes. Already covered by P13-1 unit tests (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:918-967).
- asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:419-492 — `build_input_stream` delegates to the P13-1 pure helper `select_sample_format_handler(SampleFormat, SampleQueue) -> Result<SampleFormatHandler, SipError>`; `SampleFormatHandler` is a `#[derive(Debug)]` enum with I16/F32/U16 variants carrying the queue. Covered by 2 P13-1 tests (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:973-1021).
- **asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:385-413 — `select_input_config(device, format)` (current O-001 target):** inlines `supported_input_configs().map_err(map_supported_configs_error)?`, then `.filter(|range| range.channels() == requested_channels).filter_map(|range| range.try_with_sample_rate(requested_rate)).next()`; then `match preferred { Some(config) => Ok(config), None => device.default_input_config().map_err(map_default_config_error) }`. The channels filter + `try_with_sample_rate` + `.next()` decision is deterministic but takes `&cpal::Device`, so NO test exercises it (verified: `prefer_config_matching_request` does not exist anywhere in the source tree and has zero references in the test module). This is the ABC O-001 to close.
- asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:311-377 — `CpalMicrophoneSource { stream: Option<cpal::Stream>, queue: SampleQueue }` with `new(format)` (default_host → default_input_device → select_input_config → build_input_stream → stream.play()), `#[cfg(test)] from_queue(queue)` / `queue()`, `Drop` takes the stream, `#[async_trait] impl AsyncAudioSource::next_chunk` drains the queue.
- asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:494-1022 — test module `mod tests`. cpal-gated tests include: C051 signature, SampleQueue FIFO/empty, f32/u16 conversion, next_chunk delegation, zero-length buffer, Send bounds, ErasedAudioSource auto-derivation, the 6 P13-1 O-001 tests (4 map_*_error + 2 select_sample_format_handler). Missing: any test for the config-preference decision.
- Cargo.toml — `cpal = { version = "0.18", optional = true }` (line 73), `cpal-input = ["dep:cpal"]` (line 26), `check-cfg = ['cfg(feature, values("cpal-input", "pjsua-native"))']` (line 33); MSRV 1.95. Cargo.lock pins cpal 0.18.1. The `[::STUB::] P1-3 (N0050)` comment referenced by older scope text no longer exists — resolved by P8-7.
- tests/verify_spec_p8_7.rs — feature-gated `#[ignore]` integration test `opens_default_microphone_and_captures_a_frame` (48000/I16/Mono/20ms → 960-sample buffer, asserts >= 1 sample), gated by `SI_PRS_TEST_AUDIO=1`.
- cpal 0.18.1 crate source (verified constructibility for O-001): `SupportedStreamConfig::new(channels: u16, sample_rate: u32, buffer_size: SupportedBufferSize, sample_format: SampleFormat)` is PUBLIC (src/lib.rs:536) with accessors `channels()`, `sample_rate()`, `sample_format()`, `config()`; `SupportedBufferSize` has `Range{min, max}` and `Unknown` (#[default], src/lib.rs:460-469); `ChannelCount = u16` and `SampleRate = u32` (type aliases, src/lib.rs:220-223); `SampleFormat` is #[non_exhaustive] with 15 explicit variants (I8/I16/I24/I32/I64/U8/U16/U24/U32/U64/F32/F64/DsdU8/DsdU16/DsdU32); `SupportedStreamConfigRange::try_with_sample_rate(self, SampleRate) -> Option<SupportedStreamConfig>` (src/lib.rs:717) — Option-returning, so the filter_map usage in `select_input_config` is correct; `cpal::Error` is `{ kind: ErrorKind, message: Option<Cow<'static, str>> }` with public `Error::new(ErrorKind)` / `Error::with_message(ErrorKind, impl Into<Cow<'static, str>>)` (src/error.rs:137-150); `ErrorKind` has 14 public variants (DeviceBusy, DeviceChanged, DeviceNotAvailable, HostUnavailable, InvalidInput, PermissionDenied, RealtimeDenied, ResourceExhausted, StreamInvalidated, UnsupportedConfig, UnsupportedOperation, Xrun, BackendError, Other).

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
- Translatability improvements for the code touched by this ticket:
- (1) Extract the config-preference decision from `select_input_config` (asyncaudiosrc_adapter.rs:385-413) into a pure, prose-readable helper `prefer_config_matching_request(candidates, requested_channels, requested_sample_rate) -> Option<SupportedStreamConfig>` — the code reads as 'among the candidate configs, prefer the one matching the requested channel count and sample rate; otherwise fall back to the device default'. `select_input_config` becomes 'materialize candidates from the device, then delegate the preference decision; fall back on None'. This makes the deterministic decision translatable AND unit-testable (Boy Scout: extract a decision into a named verb-phrase function).
- (2) Name the extracted helper as a verb phrase (`prefer_config_matching_request`) over a domain-noun input (`cpal::SupportedStreamConfig` candidates), consistent with the existing `select_input_config` / `select_sample_format_handler` verb-phrase naming and the `SampleQueue` / `SampleFormatHandler` / `CpalMicrophoneSource` noun naming.
- (3) Preserve the named constants (F32_TO_I16_SCALE, U16_DC_OFFSET) and the distinct error-message prefixes; keep `requested_channels` / `requested_sample_rate` as cpal type aliases (ChannelCount = u16, SampleRate = u32) rather than magic numbers.
- (4) No `unwrap()` in new production code: the helper returns `Option` (the caller owns the fallback decision); the only `.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner())` is the deliberate poisoned-mutex recovery and stays documented.
- (5) Outside the immediate scope: the doc comment on `open_default_microphone_source` (lines 161-172) already documents C051 — keep it accurate after the refactor; the P8-7 Cargo.toml wiring and the P13-1 sample-format extraction are complete and must not be regressed; do not reintroduce stale placeholder error strings.

This ticket was flagged by the ABC Inspection Pipeline after completing the implementation lifecycle. The actual source code was analyzed against three criteria — A (Contract Translation: are all Pre/Post/Invariant contracts translated into test code?), B (Violation Detection: can every contract violation be detected by an existing assertion?), C (Test Precision). The example binaries themselves are fully implemented (P9-1 → P13-3 rounds); the confirmed O-001 omission is the unpinned C056-Invariant reactor guard, which this final round must resolve completely.

### Goal
Resolve the ABC-inspection omission O-001 for the already-implemented example-binaries ticket: add a source-inspection test (reactor_keeps_catch_unwind_ffi_guard) in tests/verify_spec_p9_1.rs that verifies src/runtime/reactor.rs retains std::panic::catch_unwind in its command-dispatch/callback bridge (grep reactor.rs for the token, mirroring the examples_have_result_returning_main O-001 pattern), so removal of the FFI-safety guard is detectable. Update the C056-Invariant contract wording to name the verifying test.

### Purpose
Contract C056-Invariant requires src/runtime/reactor.rs to contain catch_unwind in its callback bridge so a panicking handler never unwinds across the boundary (§46 panic-free goal). This invariant element is currently unpinned: no source-inspection test greps reactor.rs, and no test dispatches a panicking command. Without a pin, a regression that strips the guard would unwind a panicking command handler across the reactor boundary undetected — the ABC A/B/C evaluations confirm removal would break no existing test.

### Motivation
The ABC Inspection Pipeline remanded this ticket because: (A) C056-Inv's catch_unwind element has no test translation, (B) removing every catch_unwind from reactor.rs would not fail any test, (C) no assertion is precise enough to catch the regression. The example binaries and their Layer 5 integration tests are green (make test passes, 1115+ tests); this final round adds the missing reactor-guard pin and aligns the C056-Inv contract wording with the concrete test.

### Constraints
The pin follows the existing source-inspection pattern (examples_have_result_returning_main): read the target file and assert a token, built with concat! so the test's own source never trips the quality checker. Behavioral dispatch of a panicking command is out of reach from tests/ because DispatchCommand::Execute is pub(crate) and RuntimeCommand exposes only typed operations — the source-inspection test is the required, deterministic substitute. No new runtime dependencies; the examples keep consuming the public API only. make test must stay green.

  - Alternative verification: the example runs headless with an injected MockAsyncAudioSource/TtsStreamSource; the device-backed path is covered by P8-7's feature-gated tests (#[ignore] without audio hardware).

- Item: Verifying exact PJSIP call-state timing in make_call.
  - Reason: This item is not testable (we cannot test wall-clock SIP timing): ringing/connect timing depends on the live stack and network; the reactor's make_call returns a hardcoded call_id (P12-1) and SipCall lifecycle is pending P9-3/P8-9. This is an external/non-deterministic-timing limitation, not a design defect (not an architectural defect) — event ordering is deterministic and assertable with MockBackend.
  - Alternative verification: integration tests assert event ordering (OutgoingCallRinging then CallConnected) with MockBackend, not wall-clock SIP behavior; the example is runnable against a live endpoint where timing is real.

- Item: Verifying real AudioChunkPair media streaming through audio_tap's subscribe_audio against a live call.
  - Reason: This item is not testable in the default environment (we cannot test it without a live SIP media path): AudioChunkPair IN/OUT frames are produced by the backend media engine, which only runs under Layer 3 (Docker SIP server + PJSUA media) or Layer 4 (real PBX). MockBackend (Layer 2/5) accepts subscribe_audio and returns an AudioTapHandle but does not generate real audio frames; the default make test environment has no media engine. This is an external-dependency limitation, not a design defect (not an architectural defect) — the AudioTapHandle API surface is deterministic and unit-tested (tap_channel capacity/mode semantics in src/api/audio_subscribe_bp.rs), and frame streaming becomes testable under Layer 3.

- Item: Behavioral dispatch of a panicking reactor command from the Layer 5 integration suite.
  - Reason: This item is not testable from tests/ (we cannot dispatch a panicking command through the public API): RuntimeCommand exposes only typed operations (Initialize, AddAccount, MakeCall, ...) and the raw closure path DispatchCommand::Execute is pub(crate), reachable only inside the crate. No public input makes MockBackend's handler panic, so an integration-level panic-dispatch test cannot be written. This is an API-visibility limitation, not a design defect (not an architectural defect) — the panic-catching behavior is deterministic and the guard's presence is asserted by the source-inspection test.

acceptanceCriteria: 【Happy path】Each of the five example binaries (account_register, audio_tap, client_init, make_call, tts_source) parses CLI args and runs against a real SipClient, performing its named operation instead of returning immediately.
【Happy path】account_register constructs an AccountConfig from CLI args and calls account.register(), exiting after registration completes or fails cleanly.
【Happy path】client_init constructs SipClient with transports/STUN per RFC §41.1 and reports the client capabilities.
【Happy path】make_call dials an OutgoingCallRequest to the CLI target URI and waits for OutgoingCallRinging / CallConnected / CallRejected events per RFC §41.3.
【Happy path】audio_tap subscribes to call audio via subscribe_audio and reads AudioChunkPair frames through AudioTapHandle::recv per RFC §41.4.
【Happy path】tts_source implements a TtsStreamSource (AsyncAudioSource over an mpsc receiver), adds it via add_audio_source, and sets gain per RFC §41.5.
【Error case】Each example exits non-zero with a user-facing error message when the SIP endpoint is unreachable, registration fails, or credentials are invalid — never panics.
【Edge case】Missing or invalid CLI args print a usage message to stderr and exit non-zero.
【Invariant】Every example main returns Result and propagates errors with `?`; no unwrap() in the example production paths (panic policy C056).

**[Happy path] — Confirm this ticket is complete:**
  - client_init: `cargo run --example client_init -- --host sip.example.com` prints the ClientInitialized capabilities (event_bus_capacity, max_calls) and exits 0 after shutdown.
  - account_register: `cargo run --example account_register -- --host <host> --username alice --domain example.com --password s3cret!` registers the account (RegistrationStateChanged observed) and exits 0.
  - make_call: `cargo run --example make_call -- --host <host> --target sip:bob@example.com` dials and observes OutgoingCallRinging then CallConnected (or CallRejected) then exits 0.
  - tts_source: `cargo run --example tts_source -- --host <host>` injects a TtsStreamSource via submit_add_audio_source, sets gain 0.6, and exits 0.
  - audio_tap: the CLI/init/error flow runs; the subscribe_audio segment is gated on P9-2.
  - All five example binaries parse CLI args and run against a real SipClient, performing their named operation instead of returning immediately. `make test` passes including tests/verify_spec_p9_1.rs.

**[Error case] — Error scenarios the feature must handle:**
  - Missing or invalid CLI args print the shared usage message to stderr and exit non-zero (CLI determinism invariant).
  - Unreachable SIP endpoint: SipClient::new or the named operation returns Err(SipError); the example prints a user-facing error and exits non-zero — never panics (C056).
  - Registration failure / invalid credentials: account_register observes RegistrationStateChanged::Failed (or returns Err) and exits non-zero with the failure reason.
  - Call rejection: make_call observes CallRejected and exits non-zero with the rejection status code.
  - The reactor is shut down before non-zero exit when it was started.

**[Edge case] — Boundary or exception scenarios to verify:**
  - --host "", --target "", --username "" are rejected before any network call (CliArgs::validate runs first; SipClient::new is never invoked).
  - --port 0 and --port 65536 are rejected; --port 1 and --port 65535 are accepted.
  - Empty argv (no args) prints the usage message and exits non-zero for every example (identical prefix — CLI determinism).
  - AudioFormat frame_ms outside {10,20,40,60} is rejected by AudioFormat::new.
  - Audio source gain is clamped to [0.0, 2.0] by the runtime.
  - Broadcast RecvError::Lagged is tolerated (no panic on slow-consumer lag).
  - Source-level test asserts zero unwrap()/expect()/panic!() in the examples' production paths (C056).

**[Happy path] — O-001 re-implementation round complete:**
  - examples_have_result_returning_main passes: all five examples (client_init, account_register, make_call, audio_tap, tts_source) declare `async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>`; a deliberately ()-returning main fails the test (red).
  - The refactored account_register/make_call examples use the public SipClient::add_account facade (RFC §41.2) and still register/dial against MockBackend; examples/common/client.rs no longer references the unlanded facade.
  - make test passes (green) including the new O-001 test and the existing 5 Layer 5 flow tests.

**[Error case] — O-001 re-implementation error scenarios:**
  - A regression that removes the Result return type from any example main (`async fn main() { ... }`) is caught by examples_have_result_returning_main with a message naming the file and line — the O-001 failure mode is now detectable.
  - SipClient::add_account with an invalid AccountConfig (empty username/domain) returns Err(SipError) from config.validate() before any network I/O; the example propagates it with `?` and exits non-zero.

**[Edge case] — O-001 re-implementation boundary scenarios:**
  - The source-inspection test normalizes whitespace before matching, so a reflowed signature (`async fn main()
    -> Result<...>`) is still detected.
  - The C056-Post contract wording and the test agree on the exact pinned type (Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>), preventing wording/test drift.

**[Happy path] — O-001 reactor-guard pin complete:**
  - reactor_keeps_catch_unwind_ffi_guard passes against the current src/runtime/reactor.rs (11 std::panic::catch_unwind sites): the FFI-safety guard is pinned and make test is green.

**[Error case] — O-001 reactor-guard error scenario:**
  - A regression that removes every catch_unwind from src/runtime/reactor.rs fails reactor_keeps_catch_unwind_ffi_guard with a message naming the file — the C056-Inv guard removal is now detectable (ABC criterion B satisfied).

**[Edge case] — O-001 reactor-guard boundary scenario:**
  - The catch_unwind token is built with concat! so the quality checker does not flag the test's own source; whitespace reflow of reactor.rs does not cause a false negative (token matching, not line-layout matching); C056-Inv contract wording names the verifying test, preventing wording/test drift.

The implementation does contain std::panic::catch_unwind (reactor.rs:133, 212, 238, 283, 318, 365, 395 wrapping command handlers), but NO test translates this invariant element: neither a source-inspection test greps reactor.rs for catch_unwind, nor does any test dispatch a panicking command to assert the reactor catches it and returns Err. A panicking command handler would then unwind out of the reactor command loop undetected, violating the C056-Invariant never-unwind-across-boundary requirement. tickets.background:
### Goal
§62 実装整合フレームワークを確立する。RESIDUE 乖離の根因3点（公開 ClientConfig 非RFC型 / Mock 固定バックエンド / イベントバス分断）を、RFC §62.0 に基づく型付き設計データとして `src/architecture/impl_integration_design.rs` に文書化し、実装整合の基準（testable blueprint）として確定する。

### Purpose
§62.9 の I/O 境界参照表を graphify/boundify の分割判断に利用可能にする。あわせて破壊的変更（旧 config.rs 削除・MockBackend 削除・call_state 改名）を v0.x 開発期の今一度に完了させるための全体手順（§62.1→62.8）を定義し、P15-2〜P15-9 の各実装チケットが共通の設計判断・I/O 境界・削除対象を参照できるようにする。

### Motivation
根因3点が放置されると、公開 API が RFC 型でない・reactor が Mock 固定で実 SIP/メディアが動作しない・reactor 側 publish がクライアントに届かず実イベントが 0 件のままとなる。これらは §62.1–62.8 の各実装チケットが解決するが、個別に着手すると I/O 境界・削除対象・改名の認識がチケット間で分裂する。P15-1 が blueprint を一元化することで、各チケットの実装順序・境界・削除対象を整合させる。

### Constraints
本チケットは破壊的変更を実行しない（blueprint の定義のみ）。PJSIP 実機・ネットワーク不要。既存の公開 API と実行時挙動を変更しない。追加依存クレートなし。`src/architecture` モジュールの配線（lib.rs への `pub mod architecture;` 追加）のみがビルド構成の変更となる。

testUnit: UT: [Normal] ClientConfig::validate() が §42 規則（event_bus_capacity>=16, sample rate 8/16/24/48k, raw_sip 容量制約）を検査すること。対象: src/config/client_config_spec.rs::validate()。
UT: [Normal] IceConfig 既定値が §13（enabled=true / aggressive_nomination=true / max_host_candidates=16）と一致すること。対象: src/config/transport_ice_spec.rs::IceConfig::default()。
UT: [Normal] TurnServerConfig が StunServerConfig と別型であること（型バグ解消）。旧 config.rs の `turn_server: Option<StunServerConfig>` が消え、RFC ClientConfig の `turn_servers: Vec<TurnServerConfig>` に置換されることをコンパイル時に保証。

**UT: [Normal] — RFC §10 型の昇格と既定値**: (1) `siprs::ClientConfig` が `client_config_spec::ClientConfig` に解決され、`ClientConfig::default()` の全フィールドが §10.1 と一致する（user_agent="tauri-siprs/0.1", log_level=LogLevel::Info, max_calls=32, event_bus_capacity=2048, raw_sip_event_capacity=4096, transports=[Udp(5060),Tcp(5060)], stun_servers=[], turn_servers=[], ice=IceConfig::default(), raw_sip_events=RawSipEventConfig::default(), timeouts=TimeoutConfig::default()）。検証: client_config_spec.rs の `client_config_default_constructs` / `client_config_default_transports_include_udp_and_tcp` を拡張。(2) `ClientAudioConfig.default_delivery_format` が `AudioFormat` 型（src/model/audio_format_chunkpair.rs, P4-2 実装済み）に解決され、既定値 `AudioFormat{sample_rate:SampleRate::Hz16000, bit_depth:BitDepth::I16, channel_layout:ChannelLayout::StereoInOut, frame_ms:20}` を持つ。検証: `client_audio_config_defaults` を拡張。(3) `IceConfig::default()` が §13 の enabled=true / aggressive_nomination=true / trickle_ice=false / renomination=false / max_host_candidates=16 に一致する。検証: transport_ice_spec.rs の `ice_config_default_values` を §13 値へ更新。(4) `StunServerConfig{uri}` が構築可能（例: `StunServerConfig{uri:"stun.example.com:3478".into()}`）。検証: `stun_server_config_constructs` を uri 形状へ更新。(5) `TurnServerConfig{uri, username:Option<String>, password:Option<SecretString>, transport}` が構築可能。検証: `turn_server_config_constructs` を §13 形状へ更新。

**UT: [Error] — §42 検証の拒否経路**: (1) `event_bus_capacity<16` で validate() が `Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig)` を返し message に "event_bus_capacity" を含む。検証: `client_config_rejects_small_event_bus_capacity`。(2) raw_sip enabled 時 `raw_sip_event_capacity < event_bus_capacity` で InvalidConfig。検証: `client_config_rejects_raw_sip_capacity_less_than_event_bus`。(3) `max_calls==0` で InvalidConfig。検証: `client_config_rejects_zero_max_calls`。(4) `transports` 空で InvalidConfig。検証: `client_config_rejects_empty_transports`。(5) 旧 config.rs の `sip_proxy_host` 空 / port 0 / user_agent>256B の検証規則は旧型削除に伴い撤去される（RFC §10 ClientConfig はこれらフィールドを持たない）。

**UT: [Boundary] — 境界値**: (1) `event_bus_capacity==16`（最小境界）で validate() が Ok。検証: `client_config_accepts_minimum_event_bus_capacity`。(2) `raw_sip_event_capacity == event_bus_capacity`（等値境界）で Ok。検証: `client_config_accepts_raw_sip_capacity_equal_to_event_bus`。(3) §42 sample-rate: `default_delivery_format` の `SampleRate` 全バリアント（Hz8000/Hz16000/Hz24000/Hz48000）で validate() が Ok を返す。SampleRate は閉じた enum（src/model/audio_format_chunkpair.rs:43-52）のため不正値は型レベルで表現不能であり、§42 検査は防御的（到達不能）。(4) `AudioFormat::new` が `frame_ms∉{10,20,40,60}` を `Err(AudioFormatError)` で拒否する（§42 のフレーム保証の型レベル実装）。

**UT: [Invariant] — 公開型単一性と §13 整合（C070/C080/C081 の検証）**: §62 親セクションが存在する（C070 precondition: impl_integration_design.rs に ConfigUnification 設計判断が定義される）ことを確認し、62.1 が §62 の一部として記述される（C070 postcondition: client_config_unify.rs に §62.1 設計レコードが実装される）こと、設定一本化は §10/§13 と矛盾しない（C070 invariant）ことを検証する。C080: N0013 が §10 ClientConfig を定義する（client_config_spec.rs）ことを確認し、62.1 が ClientConfig 一本化を規定する（lib.rs が RFC §10 型を唯一の公開型として再公開）こと、RFC §10 型が唯一の公開型として残る（旧 config.rs ClientConfig が削除される）ことを検証する。C081: N0015 が §12/§13 の transport/ICE/STUN/TURN を定義する（transport_ice_spec.rs）ことを確認し、62.1 が StunServerConfig/TurnServerConfig 一元化と Vec 化を規定する（二重定義を一元化）こと、二重定義が解消され §13 既定値と一致する（IceConfig enabled=true/aggressive_nomination=true/max_host_candidates=16）ことを検証する。具体的検証: (a) `siprs::ClientConfig`（lib.rs）と `crate::config::ClientConfig`（config.rs 再エクスポート）が同一型であることを compile-time 関数 `fn assert_same<T>(_: T, _: T){}` で確認。(b) `crate::config::StunServerConfig` が `transport_ice_spec::StunServerConfig` と同一型であり、旧 config.rs 定義がソースツリーに存在しないことを `find_identifier_outside_comments`（src/transport.rs の既存パターン）で検証。
testIntegration: IT: [Integration point] client.rs(SipClient::new) → runtime/reactor.rs(CoreReactor::spawn) → EventBus publish の経路。SipClient::new(ClientConfig::default()) が Ok を返し、返却された broadcast receiver の最初の制御イベントが SipEventPayload::ClientInitialized であることを検証（src/client.rs::sip_client_constructs_with_valid_config を拡張）。

IT: [Verification] 不正な ClientConfig（event_bus_capacity=8）で SipClient::new が Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig) を返す（fail-fast）。config.validate() が reactor spawn 前に実行され、reactor が起動しないことを検証（client.rs に `client_config_invalid_fails_fast` を追加）。

**IT: [Integration point] — 各インターフェースの接続**: (1) SipClient::new(config: RFC ClientConfig) → BootConfig{config, dtmf_sent_timeout_ms} → CoreReactor::spawn の経路で RFC 型が reactor へ渡る。(2) config.rs の `pub use client_config_spec::ClientConfig` 再エクスポートにより `crate::config::ClientConfig`（runtime/command.rs::RuntimeCommand::Initialize の config フィールド、backend.rs::SipBackend::initialize の引数）が RFC 型に解決されることをコンパイルで検証。(3) `siprs::ClientConfig` と `crate::config::ClientConfig` の型同一性を `fn assert_same<T>(_: T, _: T){}` で検証。

**IT: [Verification] — 統合テストが検証する内容**: (1) 正常系: `SipClient::new(ClientConfig::default())` が Ok((SipClient, Receiver)) を返し、Receiver の最初のイベントが ClientInitialized である（C047 postcondition）。(2) 異常系: `event_bus_capacity<16` で `Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig)`（fail-fast 検証）。(3) `ClientConfig::default()` が `siprs::config::transport_ice_spec::StunServerConfig` と `siprs::StunServerConfig` の同一性を介して §13 型に解決される。

**IT: [Prerequisites] — 統合テストの前提条件**: (1) config.rs が RFC ClientConfig を再エクスポート済み。(2) runtime/reactor.rs::BootConfig が `dtmf_sent_timeout_ms: u64` フィールドを持ち、`boot_config.config.dtmf.sent_timeout_ms` 参照が除去済み。(3) client.rs::SipClient::new の `#[instrument]` フィールドが RFC フィールド（user_agent/log_level 等）へ更新済み。(4) reactor は MockBackend（62.2 未着）のまま。

**IT: [Related tickets] — 関連チケット**: P15-1（§62 実装整合設計 — 型付き設計データと evidence テスト）、P7-2（O-002 DtmfSent タイムアウト — BootConfig への移行）、P3-1（RFC 設定型の原型）、P4-2（AudioFormat/SampleRate 実装）、62.2（バックエンド選択 — 本チケットでは MockBackend 維持）。
testExceptions:
**Exception entry — STUN/TURN/ICE 設定の実 PJSIP 反映**:
  - [Item] 一元化された StunServerConfig/TurnServerConfig/IceConfig が実 PJSUA（pjsua）スタックに設定として反映され、ICE ネゴシエーションが実機で成立すること。実 PJSIP への設定反映は pjsua-native feature（Layer 3+）で検証する。
  - [Reason] 現在のバックエンドは MockBackend（src/runtime/reactor.rs:75 の `Box::new(MockBackend::new())`）であり、pjsua-native feature が未導入（62.2 バックエンド選択機構のスコープ）。PJSIP スタックを起動できない本ビルドでは実設定反映を実行できず、この項目はテスト不能（cannot test）である。ただしこれは「決定的だが原理的にテスト不能」な設計欠陥（architectural defect / design defect）ではなく、pjsua-native feature というテスト可能な経路が別チケット（62.2 / Layer 3+ SIP Integration）に存在するスコープ制約である（not a design defect）。
  - [Alternative verification] Layer 1/2 で代替検証: (a) §13 の型形状（StunServerConfig{uri} / TurnServerConfig{uri,username,password,transport} / IceConfig 既定値）を UT で検証。(b) §42 validate() の全拒否経路を UT で検証。(c) SipClient::new が RFC 型を受理し ClientInitialized を publish することを IT で検証。pjsua-native feature 実装後に Layer 3 統合テストで実設定反映を検証する。

tickets.invariants:
### 正常成立条件 (Normal condition)
RFC §10 ClientConfig が唯一の公開設定型であり、`siprs::ClientConfig`・`crate::config::ClientConfig`・`client_config_spec::ClientConfig` がすべて同一型に解決される。IceConfig 既定値が §13（enabled=true / aggressive_nomination=true / max_host_candidates=16）と一致する。

### エラー時不変条件 (Error invariant)
validate() が InvalidConfig を返す場合、reactor や EventBus への副作用は発生しない — fail-fast は SipClient::new 冒頭で spawn 前に実行される。

### 内部状態不変条件 (Internal state invariant)
StunServerConfig / TurnServerConfig は transport_ice_spec.rs にのみ定義され、旧 config.rs に二重定義が残らない。IceConfig.max_host_candidates は usize（§13 準拠）。

### 境界値不変条件 (Boundary invariant)
event_bus_capacity >= 16、raw_sip enabled 時 raw_sip_event_capacity >= event_bus_capacity、sample_rate ∈ {8000, 16000, 24000, 48000}（AudioFormat 型により型レベル保証）。
tickets.background:
### Goal
RESIDUE 根因 R1（公開 API が RFC 型でない）を解消する。RFC §10 準拠 ClientConfig を唯一の公開型として昇格し、旧 src/config.rs の ClientConfig / StunServerConfig / ClientConfigBuilder を完全削除する。StunServerConfig / TurnServerConfig の二重定義（config.rs:71 と transport_ice_spec.rs:143）を一元化し、stun_servers/turn_servers を Vec 化して §13 の ICE 既定値（enabled=true / aggressive_nomination=true / max_host_candidates=16）に一致させる。

### Purpose
破壊的変更を v0.x 開発期の今一度に完了させ、旧型・二重定義を残さない（RFC §62 の方針）。公開 API が RFC §10/§13 と完全に一致することで、アプリケーションは transports / stun_servers / turn_servers / timeouts / ice を型安全に利用できる。§42 の validate() を SipClient::new で fail-fast 実行し、不正設定を早期に検出する。

### Motivation
README の RESIDUE が示す乖離: 公開 ClientConfig が旧 config.rs 型のまま（§10 の transports / stun_servers / turn_servers / timeouts が存在しない）。`turn_server: Option<StunServerConfig>` は TURN を STUN 型で表す型バグ（impl_integration_design.rs R1 に記録）。§13 ICE 既定値（true/true/16）と現実装（false/false/5）が乖離している。

### Constraints
設計判断 62.1 は §10（N0013）/§13（N0015）と矛盾しないこと（C080/C081 invariant）。破壊的変更は許容（v0.x）だが、62.2〜62.8 の他設計判断（バックエンド選択 / イベントバス一元化等）のスコープを侵さない。実装対象ファイルは src/config/client_config_unify.rs（N0070）。`Initial Design Artifact` ヘッダの削除・編集は禁止（Supreme Law §4）。

acceptanceCriteria: **[Happy path]** `SipClient::new(ClientConfig::default())` が Ok((SipClient, Receiver)) を返し、購読した最初の制御イベントが SipEventPayload::ClientInitialized である。`siprs::ClientConfig` が RFC §10 型（client_config_spec）に解決され、`IceConfig::default()` が §13（enabled=true / aggressive_nomination=true / max_host_candidates=16）と一致する。旧 config.rs の ClientConfig/StunServerConfig が削除され、`crate::config::ClientConfig` が RFC 型に解決される。
**[Error case]** `event_bus_capacity < 16` の ClientConfig で `SipClient::new` が `Err(SipErrorKind::InvalidConfig)` を返し、message に "event_bus_capacity" を含む。reactor は spawn されない（fail-fast）。

**[Edge case]** `event_bus_capacity == 16`（最小境界）と `raw_sip_event_capacity == event_bus_capacity`（等値境界）が validate() を通過する。`default_delivery_format` の全 SampleRate（Hz8000/Hz16000/Hz24000/Hz48000）が validate() を通過する。stun_servers/turn_servers が空 Vec でも `ClientConfig::default().validate()` が Ok。

tickets.boyScoutPlan:
### Translatability Improvement Plan

本チケットが触れるコードの翻訳可能性を向上させる（Boy Scout Rule）:

1. **旧 config.rs の untranslatable なコードを削除で解消**: `ClientConfigBuilder::build()` の `expect("sip_proxy_host is required")`（パニック API）と、複数責務を抱えた旧 validate() を、RFC §10 ClientConfig の型による構造化 + 明確な §42 validate() に置換。パニックに依存する `client_config_builder_build_panics_without_host` テストも撤去。
2. **String プレースホルダーを型に置換**: client_config_spec.rs L51 の `default_delivery_format: String // placeholder for AudioFormat (P4-2)` を `AudioFormat` 型へ置換。文字列 `"16000Hz/i16/stereo"` の暗黙的エンコーディングを、ドメイン型 AudioFormat{sample_rate:Hz16000, bit_depth:I16, channel_layout:StereoInOut, frame_ms:20} で明示化。

testExceptions: [Item] 実 PJSIP シグナリング（SIP REGISTER 送信・200 OK 受信・メディア確立）の自動テストは cannot test — PJSUA 実機呼び出しは `pjsua-native` feature 有効かつ libpjsua 導入済みビルドでのみ実行可能であり、デフォルトの `cargo test`（feature なし）環境では FFI 呼び出しが stub alias（RFC §28, C058）に置き換わるため実シグナリングが発生しない（外部依存による非テスト可能性）。これは not a design defect — 選択機構そのもの（create_backend の cfg 分岐）は pjsua-native 有効ビルドで単体テスト可能であり、PjsuaBackend 内部の pj_status 変換（map_pjsua_status, C111）も unit テスト済み。実シグナリングは §43 Layer 3/4 のスコープ。代替検証: PJSUA 導入環境で `make test`（pjsua-native 有効）を実行し、create_backend の PjsuaBackend 分岐と各 FFI メソッドが Ok を返すことを確認。

[Item] 非 feature 非 test ビルド（`all(not(feature), not(test))` 分岐）の実行経路は not testable — cfg(test) が有効な単体テスト実行環境ではこの分岐がコンパイル時に除外されるため、同一ビルド内からこの実行経路を叩くことができない。これは not an architectural defect — Rust の cfg 機構に起因する必然であり、エラー構築を `unsupported_backend_error()` に抽出して cfg(test) 下で unit テスト可能にし、分岐の存在自体はソーススキャンテストで担保する（「決定的だがテスト不能 → テスト可能へ再設計」の要請を満たす）。代替検証: ① unsupported_backend_error() の戻り値・文言を unit テスト。② `cargo build`（feature なし・非テスト本番ビルド）がコンパイル成功すること。③ そのビルドで SipClient::new が明示エラーを返すことを client_init example で確認。

[Item] TestBackend が FFI（PJSUA）を一切呼ばないことの正の証明は not testable — 成功応答を返す正のテストでは「FFI を呼ばない」ことを直接証明できず、FFI 呼び出しはコンパイル時に cfg(feature) で排除されるため、負の検証（TestBackend 実装に ffi:: / bindings:: 参照が存在しないこと）はソーススキャンでのみ確認可能。これは not a design defect — コンパイル時排除による保証の性質であり、テスト可能性の欠如ではない。代替検証: ソーススキャンテストで TestBackend 実装部（cfg(test) 領域）に `bindings::` / `ffi::` 参照が存在しないこと、および reactor Layer 2 テストが feature なしで完走することを assert。
